children.text: Śāṅkhāyanāraṇyakam
children.translated_text: The <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>

children.text:
ŚĀ 1,1
prajāpatir vai saṃvatsaraḥ | tasyaiṣa ātmā yan mahāvratam | tasmād enat parasmai na śaṃsen net sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām ātmānaṃ parasmin dadhānīti || atho indrasyaiṣa ātmā yan mahāvratam | tasmād enat parasmai na śaṃsen ned indrasyātmānaṃ parasmin dadhānīti || atho yam evaitam ṛṅmayaṃ yajurmayaṃ sāmamayaṃ puruṣaṃ saṃskurvanti tasyaiṣa ātmā yan mahāvratam | tasmād enat parasmai na śaṃsen net sarveṣāṃ chandasām ātmanaṃ parasmin dadhānīti || kāmaṃ tu sattriṇāṃ hotā śaṃset | pitre vācāryāya vātmane haivāsya tacchandastaṃ bhavati | ātmanaiva tad yajñaṃ samardhayati | tasya pañcaviśaḥ stomaḥ | caturviṃśatir vai saṃvatsarasyārdhamāsāḥ, saṃvatsarasyaivāptyai | atho prajāpatir vai saṃvatsaraḥ pañcaviṃśaḥ | atho caturviṃśo vai purastāt kṛto bhavati tasyaiṣa gatir yat pañcaviṃśaḥ | aindraśca ṛṣabhaḥ prājāpatyaścāja upālabhyau | aindraṃ vā etad ahaḥ | indra u vai prajāpatiḥ | tat prājāpatyaṃ rūpam | atho etad eva paśuṣvaindraṃ rūpaṃ yad ṛṣabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 1,1
<s>Prajāpati</s> is indeed the year. The <s>Mahāvrata</s> (great observance) is his self. Therefore one should not recite it to another, lest one place the self of all beings in another. Moreover, the <s>Mahāvrata</s> is the self of <s>Indra</s>. Therefore one should not recite it to another, lest one place <s>Indra</s>'s self in another. Moreover, when they fashion this person composed of <s>Ṛc</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, the <s>Mahāvrata</s> is his self. Therefore one should not recite it to another, lest one place the self of all meters in another. However, the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) of those engaged in a <s>sattra</s> (sacrificial session) may recite it at will—to a father or to a teacher; for one's own self it becomes established in the meters. By one's own self one fulfills that sacrifice. Its <s>stoma</s> (hymn-form) is the twenty-five-fold. For twenty-four are the half-months of the year—for the attainment of the year itself. Moreover, <s>Prajāpati</s> is indeed the year, the twenty-fifth. Moreover, the twenty-four-fold is established first; the twenty-five-fold is its culmination. A bull sacred to <s>Indra</s> and a goat sacred to <s>Prajāpati</s> are to be sacrificed. For this day belongs to <s>Indra</s>. And <s>Indra</s> is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>—that is the <s>Prājāpatya</s> (belonging to Prajāpati) form. Moreover, among the sacrificial animals, the bull is the form belonging to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 1,2
tasya viśoviśo vo atithim iti dvādaśarcam ājyam | dvādaśa vai māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsarasyaivāptyai | tasmin vai dve chandasī bhavato gāyatryaścānuṣṭubhaśca | agniṃ naro dīdhitibhiraraṇyor ityetat pañcaviṃśatyṛcam upasaṃśaṃsati | pañcaviṃśo hi stomaḥ | tad vai śastraṃ samṛddhaṃ yat stomena saṃpadyate | tasmin vai dve chandasī bhavato virājaśca triṣṭubhaśca | tāni catvāri saṃpadyante | catuṣṭayaṃ vā idaṃ sarvam asyaiva sarvasyāptyai | traiṣṭubhaḥ praügaḥ | indrasyaivaitacchando yat triṣṭup | yad enaṃ svena chandasā samardhayati | kuvid aṅga namasā ye vṛdhāsa ity vāyavyaṃ mahadvad vṛdhavat | mahadvat - mahadvad dhyetad ahaḥ | ata evottaraṃ tṛcam aindravāyavaṃ yāvattarastanvo yāvadoja iti yāvannaraścakṣasā dīdhyānā ityetena rūpeṇa | ud vāṃ cakṣurvaruṇa supratīkam iti maitrāvaruṇaṃ devayoreti sūryastatanvān ityetena rūpeṇa | ka u śravat katamo yajñiyānām ityāśvinaṃ yaṃ Suryasya duhitāvṛṇītetyetena rūpeṇa | kathā mahām avṛdhat kasya hotur ityaindraṃ mahadvad vṛdhavat
| mahadvad - mahadvad dhyetad ahaḥ | ko vastrāta vasavaḥ kau varūteti vaiśvadevaṃ sahīyaso varuṇa mitra martād ityetena rūpeṇa | uta syā naḥ sarasvatī juṣāṇeti sarasvataṃ dvārāvṛtasya subhago vyāvar ityetena rūpeṇa | eṣa vā u kadvāṃstraiṣṭubhas tṛcakl̥pto vāmadevyaḥ praügaḥ | prajāpatir vai vāmadevaḥ prajāpatāveva tat sarvān kāman ṛdhnuvanti | tad āhur na traiṣṭubhaṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ syāt | mohayati kl̥ptachandaso yajñamukham | aikāhikam eva syāt | brahma vā ekāhaḥ | brahmaitad ahaḥ | brahmaṇaiva tad brahma samardhayati ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 1,2
Its <s>ājya</s> (libation hymn) is the twelve-versed one beginning with 'viśo-viśo vaḥ atithim.' For twelve are the months of the year—for the attainment of the year. In it are two meters, <s>Gāyatrī</s> and <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. He additionally recites the twenty-five-versed hymn beginning with 'agniṃ naro dīdhitibhir araṇyoḥ,' for the <s>stoma</s> is the twenty-five-fold. That <s>śastra</s> (recitation) is complete which corresponds to the <s>stoma</s>. In it are two meters, <s>Virāj</s> and <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. These four come together; for all this universe is fourfold—for the attainment of this entirety. The <s>praüga</s> (opening recitation) is in <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is indeed the meter of <s>Indra</s>; thus one fulfills it with its own meter. The <s>Vāyavya</s> (hymn to Vāyu) 'kuvid aṅga namasā ye vṛdhāsaḥ' is both great and augmenting. Great—for this day is indeed great. From there onward the next triplet is the <s>Aindravāyava</s> (hymn to Indra and Vāyu) 'yāvat taras tanvo yāvad ojaḥ,' with the form 'yāvan naraś cakṣasā dīdhyānāḥ.' The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> (hymn to Mitra and Varuṇa) is 'ud vāṃ cakṣur varuṇa supratīkam,' with the form 'devayor eti sūryas tatanvān.' The <s>Āśvina</s> (hymn to the Aśvins) is 'ka u śravat katamo yajñiyānām,' with the form 'yaṃ Sūryasya duhitā avṛṇīta.' The <s>Aindra</s> (hymn to Indra) 'kathā mahām avṛdhat kasya hotuḥ' is both great and augmenting. Great—for this day is indeed great. The <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (hymn to the All-gods) is 'ko vas trātā vasavaḥ kau varūtā,' with the form 'sahīyaso varuṇa mitra martāt.' The <s>Sārasvata</s> (hymn to Sarasvatī) is 'uta syā naḥ sarasvatī juṣāṇā,' with the form 'dvārā vṛtasya subhago vyāvaḥ.' This indeed is the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> triplet-arranged <s>praüga</s> of <s>Vāmadeva</s>. <s>Prajāpati</s> is indeed <s>Vāmadeva</s>; in <s>Prajāpati</s> they thereby attain all desires. They say: the morning pressing should not be in <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, for it confuses the beginning of the sacrifice whose meter has been arranged. It should be of the one-day rite. The one-day rite is indeed <s>Brahman</s>. This day is <s>Brahman</s>. By <s>Brahman</s> itself one fulfills that <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 1,3
ā tvā rathaṃ yathotaya iti marutvatīyasya pratipat | idaṃ vaso sutam andha ityanucaraḥ | eṣa eva nitya ekāhātānaḥ | tasyoktaṃ brāhmaṇam | asat su me jaritaḥ sābhivega iti vāsukraṃ pūrvaṃ śastvā mahāṁ indro nṛvad ā carṣaṇiprā ityetasmiṃstraiṣṭubhe nividaṃ dadhāti | tad yad vāsukraṃ pūrvaṃ śaṃsati | indra u vai vasukraḥ | atha yad mahāṁ indro nṛvad ā carṣaṇiprā iti mahadvat | mahadvad dhyetad ahaḥ ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 1,3
The opening of the <s>Marutvatīya</s> (hymn connected with the Maruts) is 'ā tvā rathaṃ yathotaye.' The sequel is 'idaṃ vaso sutam andhaḥ.' This is indeed the constant form of the one-day rite. Its <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (explanation) has been stated. Having first recited the <s>Vāsukra</s> hymn 'asat su me jaritaḥ sābhivegaḥ,' one places the <s>nivid</s> (invocatory formula) in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verse 'mahān indro nṛvad ā carṣaṇiprāḥ.' That he recites the <s>Vāsukra</s> first is because <s>Indra</s> is indeed <s>Vasukra</s>. And the verse 'mahān indro nṛvad ā carṣaṇiprāḥ' is great—for this day is indeed great.

children.text:
ŚĀ 1,4
athaitā ājyāhutīr juhoti | svastyayanam eva tat kurute | yajñasyaiva śāntyai yajamānānāṃ ca bhiṣajyāyai | tā vā aṣṭau bhavanti | etābhir vai devāḥ sarvā aṣṭīr āśnuvata | tatho evaitad yajamānā etābhir eva sarvā aṣṭīr aśnuvate | athaitān parisādāñ japāñ japati | parimādaḥ - āpo vai parimādaḥ | adbhir hīdaṃ sarvaṃ parimattam | atha vai parimādaḥ | annam etad uktham | āpo vā annasyāyataḥ pūrvā āyanti, āpaḥ parimādaḥ | atha vai parimādo yan nakhāni dantās tanūr lomānīti | tasmāt kṛtyāḥ saṃpadvatyo hi bhavanti | pañcaviṃśatir nidhanam | āṅgirasaṃ pratiṣṭhāyaiḥ tadrūpam, bhūtacchandāṃ sāma priyam indrasya dhāmopajagāmeti; krośānukrośe, arātsuḥ; apyeṣāṃ payaḥ, arātsuḥ; arkaṃ cārkapuṣpaṃ ca | ayaṃ vā agnirarkaḥ | asāvādityo 'rkapuṣpam | teṣu yadā paryāyaṃ sāmagāḥ stuvate, atha hotāram āhur anujapeti | te yadi stuvīran athānujapet | yadi
caivaṃ stuvīran yadi ca stuvīran anveva japet ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 1,4
Then he offers these <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter) oblations. Thereby he makes an auspicious passage—for the pacification of the sacrifice and for the healing of the sacrificers. They are indeed eight. By these the gods attained all accomplishments. Likewise the sacrificers by these attain all accomplishments. Then he mutters these <s>parisāda</s> (surrounding) incantations. <s>Parimāda</s> (surrounding purification)—the waters are indeed <s>parimāda</s>, for by waters all this has been purified. Moreover, <s>parimāda</s>—this recitation is food. The waters come first from the source of food; the waters are <s>parimāda</s>. Moreover, <s>parimāda</s> is that which consists of nails, teeth, body, and hair. Therefore the ritual performances become successful. The ending is twenty-five-fold. The <s>Āṅgirasa</s> form serves as the foundation—that is its nature. The <s>Sāman</s> (chant) of the <s>Bhūtacchandas</s> (meters of beings) has approached the dear abode of <s>Indra</s>. At the calling and calling back, they gave; their milk also, they gave. The <s>arka</s> (sacred fire) and the <s>arka</s>-flower—this fire is indeed <s>arka</s>; yonder sun is the <s>arka</s>-flower. When the <s>Sāman</s> singers chant the <s>paryāya</s> (cyclic chants), then they tell the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) to mutter along. If they chant, then he should mutter along. Whether they chant in this way or whether they chant otherwise, he should indeed mutter along.

children.text:
ŚĀ 1,5
tāni vā etani sapta devacchandāṃsi bhavanti | tasmād enān +anujapet | atho aindraṃ vā etad ahaḥ | aindrā japāḥ | tasmād enān anujapet | athātraiva tiṣṭhann agniṃ yathāṅgam upatiṣṭhate namo nama iti | nahi namaskāram ati devāḥ | samiddhasyaivaitān bhāgān upatiṣṭheta yadyuttaravedau bhavati | athātraiva tiṣṭhann ādityam upatiṣṭhate | ākāśaṃ śālāyai kuryur iti haika āhuḥ | deśena tvevopatiṣṭheta tirohito ha vā eṣa etasmin parama ukthe parama āśiṣo vadati - saṃ mahān mahatyādadhād iti | agnir vai mahan iyaṃ pṛthivī mahatī | etau hi samadhattām | saṃ devo devyādadhād iti | vāyur vai devo 'ntarikṣaṃ devī | etau hi samadhattām | saṃ brahma brāhmaṇyādadhād iti | asāv ādityo brahmāsau dyaur brāhmaṇī | etau hi samadhattām | tad imāṁl lokānt saṃdadhāti
| etad ukthaṁ śaṃsiṣyate ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 1,5
These are indeed the seven divine meters. Therefore one should mutter along with them. Moreover, this day belongs to <s>Indra</s>; the incantations belong to <s>Indra</s>. Therefore one should mutter along with them. Then, standing right there, one worships <s>Agni</s> limb by limb with 'namaḥ namaḥ' (homage, homage), for the gods do not transgress homage. One should worship these portions of the kindled fire if it is on the northern <s>vedi</s> (altar). Then, standing right there, one worships <s>Āditya</s> (the sun). Some say: 'One should make an opening in the hall.' But one should worship from a suitable place. For hidden in the supreme <s>uktha</s> (hymn), one utters the supreme blessings: 'The great one placed together with the great one'—<s>Agni</s> is indeed the great one, this earth is the great one, for these two were placed together. 'The god placed together with the goddess'—<s>Vāyu</s> is indeed the god, the atmosphere is the goddess, for these two were placed together. '<s>Brahman</s> placed together with <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>'—yonder sun is <s>Brahman</s>, yonder heaven is <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, for these two were placed together. Thus one joins together these worlds. This <s>uktha</s> shall be recited.

children.text:
ŚĀ 1,6
viśvāmitro ha vā indrasya priyaṃ dhāmopajagāma śastreṇa ca vratacaryayā | taṃ hendra uvāca viśvāmitra varaṃ vṛṇīṣveti | sa hovāca viśvāmitras tvām eva vijānīyām iti | dvitīyam iti | tvām eveti | tṛtīyam iti | tvām eveti | taṃ hendra uvāca mahāṃśca mahatī cāsmi | devaśca devī cāsmi | brahma ca brāhmaṇī cāsmīti | tata u ha viśvāmitro vijijñāsām eva cakre | taṃ hendra uvācaitad vā aham asmi yad etad avocaṃ yad vā ṛṣe 'to bhūyo 'tapās tadeva tat syād yad aham iti | tad vā indro vyāhṛtīr ūce tā upāptā āsann iti | athopanidhāya preṅkhaphalakaṃ trir abhyanya trir abhyavān iti ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 1,6
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> indeed approached the dear abode of <s>Indra</s> through recitation and observance of vows. <s>Indra</s> said to him: 'O <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, choose a boon.' <s>Viśvāmitra</s> said: 'May I know you yourself.' 'A second boon,' said <s>Indra</s>. 'You yourself,' he replied. 'A third.' 'You yourself.' <s>Indra</s> said to him: 'I am both the great and the great one. I am both the god and the goddess. I am both <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>.' Thereupon <s>Viśvāmitra</s> sought to investigate further. <s>Indra</s> said to him: 'I am indeed what I have declared. Or, O sage, if you were to perform further austerities, that would be just what I am.' Thus <s>Indra</s> spoke the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances); they had already been obtained. Then, having placed the swing-plank, thrice 'up' and thrice 'down.'

children.text:
ŚĀ 1,7
tad vā audumbaraṃ bhavati | ūrg vā annādyam udumbara ūrjo 'nnādyasyopāptyai | athainad urasā saṃspṛśya dakṣiṇaṃ bhāgam ātmano 'tiharañ japati - arko 'si vasavastvā gāyatreṇa cchandasārohantu te ta āroḷhāra ityeva tad āha | tān aham anvārohāmi rājyāyeti | rājyaṃ ha vā idam u haiva cakṣate | athottaraṃ bhāgam ātmano 'tiharañ japati - rudrāstvā traiṣṭubhena chandasārohantu te ta āroḷhāra ityeva tad āha | tān aham anvārohāmi svārājyāyeti | svārājyaṃ ha vai rājyād adhitarām iva | atha dakṣiṇaṃ bhāgam ātmano 'tiharañ japati - ādityāstvā jagatena cchandasārohantu te ta āroḷhāra ityeva tad āha | tān aham anvārohāmi sāmrājyāyeti | sāmrājyaṃ ha vai svārājyād adhitarām iva | athottaraṃ bhāgam ātmano 'tiharañ japati - viśve tvā devā ānuṣṭubhena chandasārohantu te ta āroḷhāra ityeva tad āha | tān aham anvārohāmi kāmaprāyeti | kāmapraṃ ha vai sarveṣāṃ parārdhyam | atha samadhisṛpya prāñcau pādā upāvahṛtya bhūmau pratiṣṭhāpayati | udyatataro ha vā eṣo 'smāl lokād bhavati | tad yat pratiṣṭhāpayati | tad asmiṁl loke pratitiṣṭhati pratiṣṭhāyām
apracyutyām | atha trit abhanya trir abhyavān iti | athopari preṅkhaphalake dakṣiṇottariṇam upasthaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇena prādeśena paścāt prāṅ preṅkhaphalakam upaspṛśati | prajāpatiṣ ṭvā rohatu vāyuḥ preṅkhayatv iti | prajāpatir vā etad ārohati vāyuḥ preṅkhayati yaj jīvam | atha trir abhanya trir abhavān iti | atha prāñcau pāṇī parigṛhya japati ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 1,7: That [implement] is made of <s>udumbara</s> (fig wood). <s>Udumbara</s> is indeed <s>ūrj</s> (vital nourishment) and <s>annādya</s> (food); [it is] for the attainment of vital nourishment and food. Then, touching it with his chest, passing it over the right side of his body, he mutters: 'You are <s>Arka</s> (radiance). May the <s>Vasus</s> mount you with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter — they are your mounters' — thus he says. 'I mount after them, for <s>rājya</s> (sovereignty).' For this is indeed called <s>rājya</s> (sovereignty). Then, passing it over the left side of his body, he mutters: 'May the <s>Rudras</s> mount you with the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter — they are your mounters' — thus he says. 'I mount after them, for <s>svārājya</s> (self-sovereignty).' <s>Svārājya</s> is indeed higher than <s>rājya</s>. Then, passing it over the right side of his body, he mutters: 'May the <s>Ādityas</s> mount you with the <s>Jagatī</s> meter — they are your mounters' — thus he says. 'I mount after them, for <s>sāmrājya</s> (supreme sovereignty).' <s>Sāmrājya</s> is indeed higher than <s>svārājya</s>. Then, passing it over the left side of his body, he mutters: 'May the <s>Viśve Devas</s> mount you with the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter — they are your mounters' — thus he says. 'I mount after them, for <s>kāmaprā</s> (fulfillment of desires).' <s>Kāmaprā</s> is indeed the highest of all. Then, having crept forward, bringing both feet forward, he places them firmly on the ground. For he has risen higher than this world. By placing [the feet] down, he thereby establishes himself in this world, in firm standing, in non-falling. Then [he says] 'trit abhanya trir abhyavān.' Then, on top of the swing-plank, having placed his lap from south to north, with the right span [of his hand] he touches the swing-plank from behind, facing forward: '<s>Prajāpati</s> mounts you, <s>Vāyu</s> swings you.' For it is <s>Prajāpati</s> who mounts and <s>Vāyu</s> who swings whatever lives. Then [he says] 'trir abhanya trir abhavān.' Then, clasping both hands forward, he mutters:

children.text:
ŚĀ 1,8
saṃ vāk prāṇena, sam ahaṃ prāṇena, saṃ cakṣur manasā sam ahaṃ manasā, saṃ prajāpatiḥ paśubhiḥ sam ahaṃ paśubhir ityāśiṣam eva tad vadate | suparṇo 'si garutmān iti | prāṇo vai suparṇaḥ | premāṃ vācaṃ vadiṣyāmīti pravadiṣyan hyeṣa etāṃ vācaṃ vadati bahu kariṣyantīṃ bahu kariṣyann iti | bahu hyeṣā vāk kariṣyantī bhavati | bahvayaṃ ya etasyāhnaḥ śastraṃ prāpnoti | bahor bhūyaḥ kariṣyantīṃ bahor bhūyaḥ kariṣyann iti bahor bhūyo hyeṣā vāk kariṣyantī bhavati bahor bhūyo 'yaṃ ya etasyāhnaḥ śastraṃ prāpnoti | svar gamiṣyantīṃ svar gamiṣyann iti svar hyeṣā vāg gamiṣyantī bhavati svar ayaṃ ya etasyāhnaḥ śastraṃ prāpnoti | svar imān yajamānān vakṣyan ity eva brūyāt | yaṃ dviṣyāt taṃ brūyān nā nāmuṃ nāmum iti | sa yāvato ha vā eṣa etasmād devasthāt pratisaṃkhyāya nirdhūnute niṣ ṭad dhūnute | tau ha na bhogyāyaiva bhavataḥ | tam evaitat pradharṣayati | tam evaitat pradharṣyātman dhatte | vāyur vā eṣa prāṇo bhūtvaitad ukthaṃ śaṃsati | tam evaitat pradharṣayati | tam evaitat
pradharṣyātman dhatte | gurau vā eṣa yukto bhavati ya etasyāhnaḥ śatraṃ prāpnoti, tasya gurau yuktasyeśvaraḥ prāṇo yadi nāpaparājetoḥ | tam evaitat pradharsayati | tam evaitat pradharṣyātman dhatte | na ha vā etasyai devatāyai digdhena nāsinā na paraśunā na kenacanāvatardo 'sti | tad ya evaṃ vidvāṃsam apavadati sa eva pāpīyān bhavati | na sa ya evaṃ veda | naivaṃ viduṣo 'vatardo naivaṃ viduṣo 'vatardaḥ ||8||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 1,8: 'May speech unite with breath, may I unite with breath; may sight unite with mind, may I unite with mind; may <s>Prajāpati</s> unite with cattle, may I unite with cattle' — thus he utters a blessing. 'You are <s>Suparṇa</s> (the beautiful-winged one), <s>Garutmān</s> (the eagle).' <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) is indeed <s>Suparṇa</s>. 'I shall speak this loving speech' — for he who is about to recite speaks this speech that will accomplish much, being one who will accomplish much. For this speech indeed accomplishes much. He accomplishes much who attains the <s>śastra</s> (recitation) of this day. 'That which will accomplish more than much, being one who will accomplish more than much' — for this speech indeed accomplishes more than much; he accomplishes more than much who attains the <s>śastra</s> of this day. 'That which will go to heaven, being one who will go to heaven' — for this speech indeed goes to heaven; he goes to heaven who attains the <s>śastra</s> of this day. He should say: 'I shall carry these sacrificers to heaven.' Whomever he hates, him he should say: 'Not so-and-so, not so-and-so.' As many as he shakes off by counting from that divine seat, those he shakes out. Those two are indeed no longer fit for enjoyment. He thereby overpowers him; having overpowered him, he places [the power] in himself. <s>Vāyu</s> indeed, having become <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), recites this <s>uktha</s> (hymn of praise). He thereby overpowers him; having overpowered him, he places [the power] in himself. He who attains the <s>śastra</s> of this day is indeed yoked to a heavy [burden]; of him who is yoked to the heavy, <s>prāṇa</s> is the master, if he does not turn back. He thereby overpowers him; having overpowered him, he places [the power] in himself. Against this deity there is no way of attack, neither with a poisoned arrow, nor with an axe, nor with anything. He who speaks against one who knows thus becomes himself the more sinful; not he who knows thus. There is no way of attack against one who knows thus, no way of attack against one who knows thus.

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,1
hiṃkāreṇa pratipadyata etad uktham | prāṇo vai hiṃkāraḥ prāṇenaivaitad ukthaṃ pratipadyate | atho ūrg vai raso hiṃkāra ūrjam eva tad rasam etasmin ukthe dadhāti / atho amṛtatvaṃ vai hiṃkāro 'mṛtatvam eva tad ātman dhatte | rājanaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavati | etad vai pratyakṣaṃ sāma yad rājanam | tad enat svena sāmnā samardhayati | tad aniruktāsu bhavati | anirukta u vai prajāpatiḥ | tat prājāpatyaṃ rūpam | kavatīṣu syād iti haika āhuḥ | ko vai prajāpatiḥ | tat prājāpatyaṃ rūpam | athaitaṃ tūṣṇīṃśaṃsam upāṃśu śaṃsati | vāg vā etad ahar manas tūṣṇīṃśaṃsaḥ | manasaiva tad vācaṃ samardhayati | tad id āsa bhuvaneṣu jyeṣṭham iti stotriyastṛcaḥ | vāvṛdhānaḥ śavasā bhūryojā iti vṛdhavan mahadvat | mahadvad dhyetad ahaḥ |
sa eṣa ātmā pañcaviṃśaḥ | tan nadenupasṛṣṭaṃ śaṃsati | ātmā vai pañcaviṃśaḥ prajā paśava upasargaḥ | prajayaiva tat paśubhiḥ preṣyair annādyenetyātmānam upasṛjate | nadaṃ va odatīnām iti traiṣṭubhāni pūrvāṇi padāni karoti nadasyottarāṇi | prathamena traiṣṭubhena padena prathamaṃ nadasya padam uṣasamādhāyāvasyati | dvitīyena traiṣṭubhena dvitīyaṃ saṃdhāya praṇauti | tṛtīyena traiṣṭubhena tṛtīyaṃ saṃdhāyāvasyati | caturthena traiṣṭubhena caturthaṃ saṃdhāya praṇauti | evaṃ vihṛtāṃ prathamāṃ triḥ śaṃsati, parācīr uttarā evaṃ vihṛtā eva | yā tṛtīyā sūktasya tasyā uttaram ardharcam utsṛjati nadasya cottaram | so 'yaṃ mukhasya vivaras tena vācaṃ vadati mukhena vai vācaṃ vadati | tau purastād dvipadānāṃ śaṃsati tathā hāsya stotriyānantarhitā bhavatyātmānaṃ śastvā |
atha sūdadohasaṃ parvāṇi saṃhitāni bhavanti | atho āpo vai sūdadohā adbhir vā imāni parvāṇi saṃhitāni bhavanti | atho amṛtatvaṃ vai sūdadohā amṛtatvaṃ eva tad ātman dhatte | atha vai sūdadohāsyaitad rūpam | tad yathā ha vai dāruṇaḥ śleṣma saṃśleṣaṇaṃ syāt paricarmaṇyaṃ vaivam tṛcāśītir evasūdadohāḥ sarveṣāṃ vedānāṃ śaṃśleṣiṇī ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,1: One begins this <s>uktha</s> (hymn of praise) with the <s>hiṃkāra</s> (the syllable 'hiṃ'). <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) is indeed the <s>hiṃkāra</s>; thus one begins this <s>uktha</s> with <s>prāṇa</s> itself. Moreover, <s>ūrj</s> (vital nourishment) and <s>rasa</s> (essence) are the <s>hiṃkāra</s>; thus one places vital nourishment and essence in this <s>uktha</s>. Moreover, <s>amṛtatva</s> (immortality) is the <s>hiṃkāra</s>; thus one places immortality in oneself. The <s>Rājana</s> [sāman] serves as the back [of the recitation]. The <s>Rājana</s> is indeed the directly perceived <s>sāman</s>. Thereby one completes it with its own <s>sāman</s>. It occurs among the <s>aniruktā</s> (unexpressed) [verses]. <s>Prajāpati</s> is indeed unexpressed; that is the form of <s>Prajāpati</s>. Some say it should be among the <s>kavatī</s> [verses]. 'Ka' is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>; that is the form of <s>Prajāpati</s>. Then he recites this <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s> (silent recitation) in a low voice. Speech is indeed this day; mind is the <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s>. Thus one completes speech with mind. 'That which was the greatest in the worlds' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> <s>tṛcas</s> (praise-verses). 'Growing mighty with strength of great power' — containing growth, containing greatness. For this day is indeed great. This <s>ātman</s> (self) is the twenty-fifth. He recites it as connected with the <s>nada</s> (reed-like sound). The <s>ātman</s> is indeed the twenty-fifth; offspring and cattle are the connection. Thus with offspring, cattle, servants, and food, one connects oneself. 'The bull of the white [cows]' — he makes the first words <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and the latter ones of the <s>nada</s>. He joins the first <s>nada</s> word with the first <s>Triṣṭubh</s> word, establishing the dawn, and concludes. He joins the second with the second <s>Triṣṭubh</s> word and chants. He joins the third with the third <s>Triṣṭubh</s> word and concludes. He joins the fourth with the fourth <s>Triṣṭubh</s> word and chants. Thus, the first [verse], having been divided, he recites three times; the latter ones going away are likewise divided. Of the third verse of the <s>sūkta</s>, he omits the latter half-verse and also the latter part of the <s>nada</s>. This is the opening of the mouth; through it one speaks speech, for one speaks speech with the mouth. He recites those two at the beginning of the two-footed [verses]; thus the <s>stotriya</s> remains uninterrupted for him, after reciting [about] the self. Then the <s>sūdadohas</s> verses serve as joints holding together. Moreover, the <s>sūdadohas</s> is indeed waters; through waters these joints are held together. Moreover, <s>amṛtatva</s> (immortality) is indeed the <s>sūdadohas</s>; thus one places immortality in oneself. This is the form of the <s>sūdadohas</s>: just as gum from wood would be a binding agent, like a covering, so the eighty <s>tṛca</s> verses are the <s>sūdadohas</s>, the binder of all the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,2
athetāni śīrṣṇyāni śaṃsati | tāni vai trīṇi tṛcāni bhavanti | trīṇi vā asya śīrṣṇaḥ kapālāni bhavanti | tānyevaitaiḥ saṃdadhāti | tāni trīṇi punarevaikaṃ tredhā tredhā tā nava ṛco bhavanti | nava vai śirasi prāṇāḥ | tānyarkavanti bhavanti | tad etasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,2: Then he recites these 'head' [verses] (<s>śīrṣṇyāni</s>). They are three <s>tṛcas</s> (groups of three verses). The skull has three bone-plates (<s>kapāla</s>). He thereby joins them together with these [verses]. These three, though one, are each divided threefold — thus they become nine verses. There are nine <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) in the head. They contain [the word] <s>arka</s> (radiance). That is the characteristic form of this day [of recitation].

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,3
athaitaṃ graivaṃ śaṃsati | tā vai tisra ṛco bhavanti | trīṇi vā āsāṃ grīvāṇāṃ parvāṇi bhavanti | tānyevaitābhiḥ saṃdadhāti | uṣṇig uttamā | so 'yaṃ skandho vidalo 'vyūḷhaḥ (laḥ) ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,3: Then he recites this 'neck' [section] (<s>graiva</s>). They are three verses. The neck has three joints. He thereby joins them together with these [verses]. The last [meter] is <s>Uṣṇik</s>. This is the shoulder, split open, not yet fully extended.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,4
athaitāṃ akṣāṃ śaṃsati | sā vai triṣṭub bhavati | tasmād akṣaḥ sthaviṣṭhaḥ | ṛṣvā ta indra sthavirasya bāhū iti bāhvor abhirūpā | atha rathantarasya stotriyānurūpau śaṃsati | tayor uktaṃ brāhmaṇam | atha dhāyyāṃ śaṃsati | iyaṃ vai dhāyyā | iyaṃ hi sarveṣu bhūteṣu hitā | sā vai dakṣiṇe bhāge dhīyate | tasmād dakṣiṇaṃ bhāgaṃ puṃsaḥ stryadhiśete | atha rāthantaraṃ pragāthaṃ śaṃsati | tasyoktaṃ brāhmaṇam | sa eka id dhavyaś carṣaṇīnām iti sūktaṃ tat pacchaḥ | tasya dvitīyām uddhṛtya viśvo hyanyo arirājagāmeti | yaitasya dvitīyā tām iha dvitīyāṃ karoti | tad imau pakṣau vyatiṣajatyavivarhāya ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,4: Then he recites this 'axle' [verse] (<s>akṣā</s>). It is a <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [verse]. Therefore the axle is the stoutest [part]. 'Your arms, O <s>Indra</s>, are mighty and powerful' — this is fitting for the arms. Then he recites the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> of the <s>Rathantara</s> [sāman]. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [explanation] for those has been stated. Then he recites the <s>dhāyyā</s> (sustaining verse). This earth is indeed the <s>dhāyyā</s>, for she is placed in all beings. She is placed on the right side; therefore a woman lies on the right side of a man. Then he recites the <s>Rāthantara</s> <s>pragātha</s> (chant-verse). The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> for that has been stated. 'He alone is worthy of praise among the peoples' — that is the <s>sūkta</s> (hymn) which follows. Taking out its second [verse], 'for every other enemy-king has departed' — that which is its second, he makes it the second here. Thus he interweaves these two wings, so they are not separated.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,5
athaitaṃ prahastakaṃ śaṃsati | tā vai tisra ṛco bhavanti | trīṇi vā asya pāṇeḥ parvāṇi bhavanti | tānyevaitābhiḥ saṃdadhāti | aticchandāḥ prathamā so 'yam aṅguṣṭhaḥ | tasmād ayam aṅguṣṭhaḥ sarvā aṅgulīḥ pratyeti | dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣo rāthantaraḥ | atha vā uttaraḥ pakṣo bārhataḥ | etenaivokto brāhmaṇaḥ | tau vā etau pakṣau bārhatarāthantarau caturviṃśau | caturviṃśatir vai saṃvatsarasyārdhamāsāḥ saṃvatsarasyāptyai ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,5: Then he recites this <s>prahastaka</s> (hand section). They are three <s>ṛcs</s> (verses). The hand has three joints. He thereby joins them together with these [verses]. The first is <s>atichandas</s> (beyond meter) — that is this thumb. Therefore this thumb reaches toward all the fingers. The right wing is the <s>Rāthantara</s> [sāman]; and the left wing is the <s>Bārhata</s> [sāman]. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [explanation] for these has been stated. These two wings, the <s>Bārhata</s> and <s>Rāthantara</s>, are twenty-four each. Twenty-four indeed are the half-months of the year — for the attainment of the year.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,6
athaitāni caturuttarāṇi śaṃsati tad anūkam | tā ekaviṃśatir ṛco bhavanti | ekaviṃśatir vā asyānūkasya parvāṇi bhavanti | tānyevaitābhiḥ saṃdadhāti | tāni vai sapta tṛcāni bhavanti | sapta vai chandāṃsi sarveṣām eva chandasām āptyai | tānyarkavanti bhavanti | tad etasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,6: Then he recites these 'four-plus' sections (<s>caturuttarāṇi</s>); that is the spine (<s>anūka</s>). They are twenty-one verses. The spine has twenty-one joints. He thereby joins them together with these [verses]. They are seven <s>tṛcas</s> (groups of three). Seven indeed are the meters — for the attainment of all meters. They contain [the word] <s>arka</s> (radiance). That is the characteristic form of this day.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,7
athaitā aśītīḥ śaṃsati | stotriyān evaitābhir anuśaṃsati gāyatryā gāyatram auṣṇihyā ca bārhatyā ca bṛhadrathantare | iyam eva dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvaṃ gāyatrī savyam auṣṇihī madhyaṃ bārhatī | madhye vā idam ātmano 'nnaṃ dhīyate | triṣṭubhāvantareṇa triṣṭum naividī | vaiśvāmitryāvarkavatyāvabhirūpe | viśvāmitro hyenad apaśyat | mahadvatyo vṛdhavatyaḥ pratipado bhavanti | mahadvad vṛdhavat | mahadvat - mahadvad dhyetad ahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,7: Then he recites these eighty [verses] (<s>aśītīḥ</s>). He thereby recites the <s>stotriyas</s> (praise-verses) with these — with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the <s>Gāyatra</s> [sāman]; with the <s>Auṣṇihī</s> and <s>Bārhatī</s>, the <s>Bṛhadrathantare</s> [sāmans]. This [earth] is indeed the right side — <s>Gāyatrī</s>; the left is <s>Auṣṇihī</s>; the middle is <s>Bārhatī</s>. For food is placed in the middle of the self. With a <s>Triṣṭubh</s> he introduces the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> — the <s>naividī</s> (offering verse). The two <s>Vaiśvāmitrī</s> [verses] containing <s>arka</s> are the <s>abhirūpe</s> (beautiful ones). For <s>Viśvāmitra</s> indeed saw this. The opening verses are those containing greatness and growth. Great and growing — for this day is indeed great.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,8
mahāṁ indro ya ojasetyetayā gāyatrīm aśītiṃ pratipadyate stomair vatsasya vāvṛdha iti mahadvatyā vṛdhavatyā | mahadvad vṛdhavat | mahadvat - mahadvad dhyetad ahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,8: With '<s>Indra</s> is great, who by his power' — with this [verse] he enters the <s>Gāyatrī</s> eighty; 'by praises the calf has grown' — with [a verse] containing growth and greatness. Great and growing — for this day is indeed great.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,9
yā indra bhuja ābhara ityetayā bārhatīm aśītiṃ pratipadyate stotāram in maghavann asya vardhayeti mahadvatyā vṛdhavatyā | mahadvad vṛdhavat | mahadvat - mahadvad dhyetad ahaḥ | ayaṃ te astu haryata ā mandrair indra haribhiḥ sūkte | tad yad ete antataḥ śaṃsati saṃsiddhābhir bṛhatībhir auṣṇihīm aśītiṃ samārohāṇīti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,9: With 'Bring hither, O <s>Indra</s>, your share' — with this [verse] he enters the <s>Bārhatī</s> eighty; 'increase this praiser, O bountiful one' — with [a verse] containing greatness and growth. Great and growing — for this day is indeed great. 'Let this be yours, O bay-horse lover, with inspiring bay horses, in the hymn' — because he recites these at the end with completed <s>Bṛhatī</s> [verses], he ascends to the <s>Auṣṇihī</s> eighty.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,10
indraḥ suteṣu someṣv ityetayauṣṇihīm aśītiṃ pratipadyate vide vṛdhasya dakṣaso mahān hi ṣa iti vṛdhavatyā mahadvatyā | vṛdhavan mahadvat | mahadvad dhyetad ahaḥ | tā vā etā aśītayaḥ saṃśastāḥ saptaviṃśatiśatānyṛcāṃ saṃpadyante | sapta vai viṃśati śatāni saṃvatsarasyāhorātrāṇāṃ tad aśītibhiḥ saṃvatsarasyāhorātrāṇyāpnoti | sāmanidhanair haike gāyatrīr uṣṇihaḥ saṃpādayanti | caturakṣarāṇyu haike punar ādadate | bārhatyā aśītyā aśītiṃ caturakṣarāṇyuddharati kākubhebhyaḥ pragāthebhyaś caturviṃśatiṃ caturakṣarāṇi tāni catuḥśataṃ caturakṣarāṇi catuḥśate gāyatrīṣūpadadhāti | tathā tā gāyatrīr uṣṇihaḥ saṃpadyante | nādriyeta | atraiva saṃpannam | indrāya sāma gāyateti | tad yad etad antataḥ śaṃsati saṃsiddhābhir uṣṇigbhir vaśaṃ samārohāṇīti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,10: With '<s>Indra</s>, at the pressed <s>Soma</s> offerings' — with this [verse] he enters the <s>Auṣṇihī</s> eighty; 'I know the power of the mighty, great is he indeed' — with [a verse] containing growth and greatness. Growing and great — for this day is indeed great. These eighty [verses] having been recited together amount to seven hundred and twenty <s>ṛcs</s>. Seven hundred and twenty indeed are the day-and-nights of the year; thus by the eighties one attains the day-and-nights of the year. Some complete the <s>Gāyatrīs</s> as <s>Uṣṇihs</s> by means of <s>sāman</s>-endings. Some again take out four-syllable [units]: from the <s>Bārhatī</s> eighty he extracts eighty four-syllable [units]; from the <s>kākubha</s> and <s>pragātha</s> [verses], twenty-four four-syllable units — these make four hundred four-syllable units, which he places in four hundred <s>Gāyatrīs</s>. Thus those <s>Gāyatrīs</s> become <s>Uṣṇihs</s>. One should not strive [for this]; here it is already complete. '[He recites] a <s>sāman</s> to <s>Indra</s>.' Because he recites this at the end with completed <s>Uṣṇik</s> [verses], he ascends to the <s>vaśa</s> (belly section).

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,11
atha vaśaṃ śaṃsati | udaraṃ vai vaśaḥ | tena saṃsiddhenānantaryaṃ jigamiṣet | yad ataḥ kiṃca bahirdhā tata eva tac chrapayati yad antar udare | tasmād bahvyo devatā bahūni cchandāṃsi vaśe śasyante | tasmād idaṃ bahu viśvarūpam udare 'nnam avadhīyate | athaitau vihṛtāvardharcau | atha sūdadohasam | sā tata evotsṛjyate | atra caturviṃśatikṛtvaḥ śastā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,11: Then he recites the <s>vaśa</s> (belly). The <s>vaśa</s> is indeed the belly. By this, when completed, one should seek to attain continuity. Whatever is outside, that it 'cooks' which is within the belly. Therefore many deities and many meters are recited in the <s>vaśa</s>. Therefore this abundant food of various forms is placed in the belly. Then these two separated half-verses [are recited]. Then the <s>sūdadohas</s> [verse]. It is released from there. Here the reciter recites twenty-four times.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,12
athaitā dvipadāḥ śaṃsati | pratiṣṭhānīyaṃ vai chando dvipadāḥ pratiṣṭhityā eva ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,12: Then he recites these two-footed [verses] (<s>dvipadāḥ</s>). The two-footed [meter] is indeed a meter of firm standing — for firm standing indeed.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,13
athaitad aindrāgnaṃ sūktaṃ gāyatrīśaṃsaṃ śaṃsati | pratiṣṭhe vā indrāgnī pratiṣṭhityā eva ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,13: Then he recites this hymn to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> (<s>aindrāgna sūkta</s>) with <s>Gāyatrī</s> recitation. <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> are indeed firm standing — for firm standing indeed.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,14
athaitad āvapanaṃ śaṃsati | pratiṣṭhā vā āvapanaṃ pratiṣṭhityā eva | athau etānyeva punararvācīni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,14: Then he recites this depositing section (<s>āvapana</s>). The <s>āvapana</s> is indeed firm standing — for firm standing indeed. And then these same [verses] are repeated in reverse order.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,15
athaitam ānuṣṭubhaṃ samāmnāyaṃ śaṃsati | vāg vā etad ahar vāg anuṣṭub vācyeva tad vācaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati | divaṃ yayeti devān evaitena sūktenaiti | sa pratnathā kavivṛdha iti tṛcam arkavat tena samṛddham | gāyatryuttamā tayā samṛddham | śāsa itthā mahāṁ asīti mahadvat | mahadvad dhyetad ahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,15: Then he recites this <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> tradition (<s>samāmnāya</s>). Speech is indeed this day; speech is <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>; thus with speech he establishes speech firmly. 'He who went to heaven' — by this <s>sūkta</s> (hymn) he goes to the gods. 'He, ancient in the manner of seers, increasing the sage' — the <s>tṛca</s> (triad) contains <s>arka</s> (radiance); by that it is enriched. Having <s>Gāyatrī</s> as the last [verse], by that it is enriched. 'Rule thus, O great one' — containing greatness. For this day is indeed great.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,16
athaitaṃ triṣṭupchataṃ śaṃsati | +indrasyaivaitac chando yat triṣṭup tad enaṃ svena chandasā samardhayati | hairaṇyastūpīyaṃ ca yātaūtīyaṃ ca bārhatarāthantare bṛhadrathantare hi purastāt kṛte bhavataḥ | sajanīyaṃ cādhvaryavo bharatendrāya somam iti ca tāḥ saptaviṃśatir ṛco bhavanti | saptaviṃśatir vai nakṣatrāṇi | tan nakṣatriyāṃ virājaṃ āpnoti | viśvāmitrasya śaṃset | viśvāmitro hyenad apaśyat | vāmadevasya śaṃsed vāmaṃ hyetad devānām | vasiṣṭhasya śaṃsed vasiṣṭhaṃ hyetad devānām | tatra purastād udbrahmīyasya padānuṣaṅgāñ chaṃsati | sarve vai kāmā etasmin antarukthe | tad yathā vraje paśūn avasṛjyārgaleṣīke parivyayet | evam evaitaiḥ padānuṣaṅgaiḥ sarvān kāmān ubhayataḥ parigṛhyātman dhatte | atho udbrahmīyasyārkavatyuttamā | tad etasyāhno rūpam | triḥ śastayā paridadhāti | paridhāyokthavīryaṃ japati | aikāhikaṃ pūrvaṃ | pratiṣṭhā vā evāhaḥ pratiṣṭhityā eva | māhāvratikam uttaram | mahad asīti mahadvat |
mahadvad dhyetad ahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,16: Then he recites this hundred <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [verses]. <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is indeed the meter of <s>Indra</s>; thus he empowers him with his own meter. The <s>Hairaṇyastūpīya</s> and <s>Yātaūtīya</s> [hymns] are the <s>Bārhatarāthantare</s> [sāmans], for the <s>Bṛhadrathantare</s> have been performed first. The <s>Sajanīya</s> [hymn] and 'O priests, [bring] <s>Soma</s> to <s>Indra</s>' — these are twenty-seven verses. Twenty-seven indeed are the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions); thus one attains the <s>nakṣatriyā virāj</s> (the stellar radiance). One should recite [the hymns] of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, for <s>Viśvāmitra</s> indeed saw this. One should recite [those] of <s>Vāmadeva</s>, for this is the finest (<s>vāma</s>) of the gods. One should recite [those] of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, for this is the most excellent (<s>vasiṣṭha</s>) of the gods. There, before the <s>Udbrahmīya</s> [section], he recites word-linkages (<s>padānuṣaṅga</s>). All desires are indeed in this <s>antaruktha</s> (intermediate recitation). Just as one would release cattle into an enclosure and close the bars around them, so with these word-linkages he grasps all desires on both sides and places them in himself. Moreover, the last [verse] of the <s>Udbrahmīya</s> contains <s>arka</s>. That is the characteristic form of this day. He encloses with the thrice-recited [verse]. Having enclosed, he mutters the <s>ukthavīrya</s> (hymn-power). First the <s>aikāhika</s> (one-day) [formula] — for the one-day [rite] is indeed firm standing, for firm standing. The <s>māhāvratika</s> (of the Mahāvrata) [formula] is last. 'You are great' — containing greatness. For this day is indeed great.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,17
tad etat sakṛcchastāyāṃ sūdadohasi, yāvacchastraṃ upasarjanyāṃ saṃkhyāyamānāyām ṛte tūṣṇīṃśaṃsaṃ bṛhatīsahasraṃ saṃpadyate | tasya vā etasya bṛhatīsahasrasya ṣaṭtriṃśad akṣarāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi bhavanti | tāvanti śatasaṃvatsarasyāhāni bhavanti | tac chatasaṃvatsarasyāhānyāpnoti | anuṣṭupsaṃpannam u haike | vāg vā etad ahaḥ | vāg anuṣṭup | vāg +gha sarvāṇi bhūtāni | atho vāg idaṃ sarvam iti | bṛhatīsaṃpannam iti tveva sthitam | bārhato vā eṣa ya eṣa tapati | tad enaṃ svena chandasā samardhayati | trir evāhvayate | trayo vā ime lokāḥ | imān eva tal lokān āpnoti | ekāhikī yājyā pratiṣṭhā vā ekāhaḥ pratiṣṭhityā eva | ananuvaṣaṭ-kṛta eva preṅkhaṃ śrathnanti | sagraham evāyaṃ taṃ prāṅ upāvarohati pratyaṅ preṅkhaphalakam apohati | parāmṛśan grahaṃ japati - yam imaṃ prajayaṃ prājaiṣaṃ tam anvasānīti ned asmāt prajayād ātmānam apādadhānīti | vaiśvakarmaṇo 'tigrāhyaḥ | prājāpatyaṃ vā etad ahaḥ | prajāpatir viśvakarmā tad enaṃ svena rūpeṇa samardhayati | tad dhaitad ahar indro 'girase
provācāṅgirā dīrghatamase | tata u ha dīrghatamā daśa puruṣāyuṣāṇi jijīva | tad apyetad ṛṣir āha dīrghatamā māmateyo jujurvān daśame yuga iti | tad etay āyuṣkāmasya śastram iti ha smāha kauṣītakiḥ | tad ya evaṃ vidvān etad ahaḥ śaṃsati sarvam āyur asmiṃl loka eti | āpnotyamṛtatvam akṣitiṃ svarge loke ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,17: In this [recitation], when the <s>sūdadohas</s> is recited once, as far as the <s>śastra</s> (recitation) extends, with the subordinate [verses] being counted, excluding the <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s> (silent recitation), one thousand <s>Bṛhatīs</s> are completed. Of this thousand <s>Bṛhatīs</s>, there are thirty-six thousand syllables. That many are the days of a hundred-year [life]. Thus one attains the days of a hundred-year life. Some say it is completed in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. Speech is indeed this day; speech is <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>; speech indeed is all beings; and speech is all this. But it is established that it is completed in <s>Bṛhatī</s>. For the <s>Bārhata</s> is indeed that one who shines [the sun]; thus one empowers him with his own meter. He invokes three times indeed. Three are these worlds; thus one attains these worlds. The one-day <s>yājyā</s> (sacrificial formula) is for firm standing, for the one-day [rite] is indeed firm standing, for firm standing. Without the concluding <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> exclamation, they tie up the swing. With the offering-cup in hand, he mounts it going forward and pushes the swing-plank backward. While touching the offering-cup he mutters: 'He whom I have won by offspring, may I follow him' — lest he should separate himself from offspring. The <s>atigrāhya</s> (special cup) belongs to <s>Viśvakarman</s>. This day is indeed <s>Prājāpatya</s> (belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s>). <s>Prajāpati</s> is <s>Viśvakarman</s>; thus one empowers it with its own form. Now, this day <s>Indra</s> proclaimed to <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and <s>Aṅgiras</s> to <s>Dīrghatamas</s>. Then <s>Dīrghatamas</s> lived for ten human lifespans. About this the seer also said: '<s>Dīrghatamas</s>, son of <s>Mamatā</s>, grown old in the tenth generation.' 'This is the <s>śastra</s> for one who desires long life' — thus said <s>Kauṣītaki</s>. He who, knowing thus, recites this day, lives a full life in this world; he attains immortality and imperishability in the heavenly world.

children.text:
ŚĀ 2,18
tat savitur vṛṇīmaha iti vaiśvadevasya +pratipat | vṛṇīmaha iti mahadvatī | mahadvat - mahadvat dhyetad ahaḥ | adyā no deva savitar ityanucaraḥ | viśvā vāmāni dhīmahīti mahadvat | mahadvad dhyetad ahaḥ | tad devasya savitur vāryaṃ mahad iti sāvitraṃ mahadvat| mahadvad dhyetad ahaḥ | te hi dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaśaṃbhuva iti dyāvāpṛthivīyam uruvyacaso mahinī asaścateti mahadvat | mahadvad dhyetad ahaḥ | kim u śreṣṭhaḥ kiṃ yaviṣṭho na ājagann ityārbhavam | na nindima camasaṃ yo mahākula iti mahadvat | mahadvad dhyetad ahaḥ | asya vāmasya palitasya hotur iti salilaṃ vaiśvadevam | salilaṃ hyetad devānām | aikāhike nividaṃ dadhāti | pratiṣṭhā vā ekāhaḥ pratiṣṭhityā eva | aikāhikaṃ vaiśvānarīyam |
pratiṣṭhā vā ekāhaḥ pratiṣṭhityā eva | prayajyavo maruto bhrājadṛṣṭaya iti mārutam | bṛhan mahānta urviyā vi rājatheti bṛhadvat | mahadvat - mahadvat dhyetad ahaḥ | baḷa ityā tad vapeṣu dhāyi darśitam iti jātavedasīyaṃ tasya astāvyagniḥ śimīvadbhir arkair ity arkavatyuttamā | tad etasyāhno rūpam ityagnimārutasūktānīti | etasyāhnaḥ sūktāni | tad agniṣṭomaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate | brahma vā agniṣṭomaḥ | brahmaitad ahaḥ | brahmanyeva tad brahma pratiṣṭhāpyanti | te 'mṛtatvam āpnuvanti ya etad ahar upayanti ya etad ahar upayanti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 2,18: 'That of <s>Savitṛ</s> we choose' (<s>tat savitur vṛṇīmahe</s>) — this is the opening (<s>pratipat</s>) of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (offering to all gods). 'We choose' (<s>vṛṇīmahe</s>) — this contains greatness (<s>mahat</s>). Containing greatness, containing greatness — for this day is great. 'Today, O divine <s>Savitṛ</s>' (<s>adyā no deva savitar</s>) — this is the accompanying verse (<s>anucara</s>). 'May we attain all desirable things' (<s>viśvā vāmāni dhīmahi</s>) — this contains greatness. Containing greatness — for this day is great. 'That great desirable [gift] of the divine <s>Savitṛ</s>' (<s>tad devasya savitur vāryaṃ mahad</s>) — this is the <s>Sāvitra</s> [hymn], containing greatness. Containing greatness — for this day is great. 'For they, Heaven and Earth, are beneficent to all' (<s>te hi dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaśambhuva</s>) — this pertains to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> (Heaven and Earth). 'Broad-extending, mighty, unfailing' — this contains greatness. Containing greatness — for this day is great. 'What is the best, what the youngest that has come to us?' (<s>kim u śreṣṭhaḥ kiṃ yaviṣṭho na ājagan</s>) — this is the <s>Ārbhava</s> [hymn pertaining to the <s>Ṛbhus</s>]. 'We do not disparage the cup which belongs to the great family' (<s>na nindima camasaṃ yo mahākula</s>) — this contains greatness. Containing greatness — for this day is great. 'Of this lovely, hoary <s>hotṛ</s>' (<s>asya vāmasya palitasya hotuḥ</s>) — this is the watery (<s>salila</s>) <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. For this is indeed the watery [offering] of the gods. In the one-day rite (<s>ekāha</s>) he inserts the <s>nivid</s> (liturgical formula). The one-day rite is indeed firm establishment (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>); for firm establishment indeed. The <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> [hymn] for the one-day rite — the one-day rite is indeed firm establishment; for firm establishment indeed. 'The <s>Maruts</s> worthy of sacrifice, of blazing appearance' (<s>prayajyavo maruto bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ</s>) — this is the <s>Māruta</s> [hymn]. 'Great and mighty, you shine far and wide' (<s>bṛhan mahānta urviyā vi rājatha</s>) — this contains <s>bṛhat</s> (greatness). Containing greatness, containing greatness — for this day is great. 'Indeed! That has been placed manifest in the sacrificial portions' (<s>baḷ ityā tad vapeṣu dhāyi darśitam</s>) — this is the <s>Jātavedasīya</s> [hymn pertaining to <s>Jātavedas</s> (Agni)]. Of this, the final verse is '<s>Agni</s> with radiant (<s>arka</s>) hymns of power' (<s>agniḥ śimīvadbhir arkaiḥ</s>) — the concluding verse contains <s>arka</s> (radiance). That is the characteristic form of this day — namely the <s>Agnimāruta</s> hymns. These are the hymns of this day. Thus the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is completed. The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is indeed <s>Brahman</s>. This day is <s>Brahman</s>. They thereby establish <s>Brahman</s> in <s>Brahman</s> itself. They attain immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>) who approach this day, who approach this day.

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 3,1 = KU 1,1
citro ha vai gāṅgyāyanir yakṣyamāṇa āruṇiṃ vavre | sa ha putraṃ śvetaketuṃ prajighāya yājayeti | taṃ hābhyāgataṃ papraccha - gotamasya putra, asti saṃvṛtaṃ loke yasmin mā dhāsyasi, anyatamo vādhvā, tasya mā loke dhāsyasīti | sa hovāca - nāham etad veda hantācāryaṃ pṛcchānīti | sa ha pitaram āsādya papraccha - itīti māprākṣīt kathaṃ pratibravāṇīti | sa hovāca - aham apyetan na veda | sadasyeva vayaṃ svādhyāyam adhītya harāmahe yan naḥ pare dadati | ehyubhau gamiṣyāva iti | sa hi samitpāṇiś citraṃ gāṅgyāyaniṃ praticakrama upāyānīti | taṃ hovāca - brahmārho 'si gotama yo na mānam upāgāḥ | ehi vyeva tvā jñapayiṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 3,1 = KU 1,1: <s>Citra</s>, the descendant of <s>Gaṅgā</s> (<s>Gāṅgyāyani</s>), being about to perform a sacrifice, chose <s>Āruṇi</s> [as his priest]. He sent his son <s>Śvetaketu</s>, saying, 'Perform the sacrifice for him.' When [<s>Śvetaketu</s>] had arrived, [<s>Citra</s>] asked him: 'Son of <s>Gotama</s>, is there a hidden place in the world where you will place me, or is there another path by which you will place me in its world?' He replied: 'I do not know this. Let me ask my teacher.' He went to his father and asked: 'He asked me thus and thus — how shall I answer?' [<s>Āruṇi</s>] said: 'I too do not know this. Let us, having studied the <s>svādhyāya</s> (sacred recitation) in the assembly, collect what others give us. Come, we shall both go.' So, with fuel in hand, he approached <s>Citra Gāṅgyāyani</s>, saying, 'Let me come to you as a student.' [<s>Citra</s>] said to him: 'You are worthy of <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge), O <s>Gotama</s>, since you did not come to pride. Come, I shall make you know.'

children.text:
ŚĀ 3,2 = KU 1,2
sa hovāca ye vai ke cāsmāl lokāt prayanti candramasam eva te sarvaṃ gacchanti | teṣāṃ prāṇaiḥ pūrvapakṣa āpyāyate | tān aparapakṣeṇa prajanayati | etad vai svargasya lokasya dvāraṃ yac candramāḥ | taṃ yaḥ pratyāha tam atiṣrjate | atha yo na pratyāha tam iha vṛṣṭir bhūtvā varṣati | sa iha kīṭo vā pataṅgo vā matsyo vā śakunir vā siṃho vā varāho vā paraśvā vā śārdūlo vā puruṣo vānyo vā teṣu teṣu sthaneṣu pratyājāyate yathākarma yathāvidyam | tam āgataṃ pṛcchati, ko 'sīti | taṃ pratibrūyāt - vicakṣaṇād ṛtavo reta ābhṛtaṃ pañcadaśāt prasūtāt pitryāvataḥ | tan mā puṃsi kartaryerayadhvaṃ puṃsā kartrā mātari māsiṣiñca || sa jāyamāna upajāyamāno dvādaśotrayodaśopamāsaḥ | dvādaśatrayodaśena pitrā saṃ tad vide 'haṃ prati tad vide 'haṃ tan ma ṛtavo 'mṛtyava ārambhadhvam || tena satyena tena tapasā ṛtur asmi ārtavo 'smi | ko 'si tvam asmīti tam atisṛjate ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 3,2 = KU 1,2: He said: 'All those who depart from this world go to the moon. By their <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) the bright half [of the month] swells. Through the dark half he causes them to be born. This is indeed the gate of the heavenly world — the moon. Whoever answers it [correctly], him it lets pass beyond. But whoever does not answer, him it rains down here as rain. He is reborn here as a worm, or a moth, or a fish, or a bird, or a lion, or a boar, or a serpent, or a tiger, or a person, or some other [creature] in these various conditions, according to his deeds, according to his knowledge. To the one who arrives, [the moon] asks: "Who are you?" He should answer: "From the wise one (<s>Vicakṣaṇa</s>), O seasons, the seed has been brought — from the fifteen-fold, from the begetter, from the ancestral realm. Send me into a man, the agent; through the man as agent, pour me into a mother." "So I am born, being additionally born, as a twelfth or thirteenth additional month. Through a father of twelve or thirteen [months], I know that, I know that in return. O seasons, lead me to immortality." "By that truth, by that <s>tapas</s> (austerity), I am a season, I am of the seasons." "Who are you?" "I am you" — thus it lets him pass beyond.

children.text:
ŚĀ 3,3 = KU 1,3
sa etaṃ devayānaṃ panthānam āpadyāgnilokam āgacchati | sa vāyulokam | sa varuṇalokam | sa indralokam | sa prajāpatilokam | sa brahmalokam | tasya vā etasya brahmalokasyārohadaḥ, muhūrtā yaṣṭihāḥ, vijarā nadī, ilyo vṛkṣaḥ, sālajyaṃ saṃsthanam, aparājitam āyatanam, indraprajāpatī dvāragopau, vibhu pramitam, vicakṣaṇāsandī, amitaujāḥ paryaṅkaḥ, priyā ca mānasī, pratirūpā ca cākṣuṣī, puṣpāṇyādāyāvayato vai ca jagāni, ambāś cāmbāyavīś cāpsarasaḥ, ambayā nadyaḥ | tam itthaṃvid āgacchati | taṃ brahmāha - abhidhāva ta mama yaśasā | vijarāṃ vā ayaṃ nadīṃ prāpat | na vā ayaṃ jarayiṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 3,3 = KU 1,3: He enters upon this path of the gods (<s>devayāna</s>). He reaches the world of <s>Agni</s>. Then the world of <s>Vāyu</s>. Then the world of <s>Varuṇa</s>. Then the world of <s>Indra</s>. Then the world of <s>Prajāpati</s>. Then the world of <s>Brahman</s>. Of this world of <s>Brahman</s> there is the lake <s>Āra</s>, the moments (<s>muhūrtas</s>) called <s>Yaṣṭihā</s> (staff-bearers), the river <s>Vijarā</s> (Ageless), the tree <s>Ilya</s>, the abode <s>Sālajya</s>, the citadel <s>Aparājita</s> (Unconquered), the two door-keepers <s>Indra</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s>, the hall <s>Vibhu</s> (Pervading), the throne <s>Vicakṣaṇā</s> (Discerning), the couch <s>Amitaujas</s> (of Immeasurable Splendor), the beloved <s>Mānasī</s> (Mind-born) and her counterpart <s>Cākṣuṣī</s> (Eye-born), who weave the worlds taking flowers, the <s>Apsarases</s> called <s>Ambā</s> and <s>Ambāyavī</s>, and the rivers <s>Ambayā</s>. To this [world] comes one who knows thus. <s>Brahman</s> says to him: 'Run to me! By my glory has this one reached the river <s>Vijarā</s> (Ageless). Truly, he shall not grow old.'

children.text:
ŚĀ 3,4 = KU 1,4
taṃ pañca śatānyapsarasāṃ pratiyanti - śataṃ phalahastāḥ, śatam āñjanahastāḥ, śataṃ mālyahastāḥ, śataṃ vāsohastāḥ, śataṃ cūṛnahastāḥ | taṃ brahmālaṅkāreṇālaṅkurvanti | sa brahmaālaṅkāreṇālaṅkṛto brahma vidvān brahmābhipraiti | sa āgacchatyāraṃ hradam | taṃ manasātyeti | tam itvā saṃprativido majjanti | sa āgacchati muhūrtān yaṣṭihān | te 'smād apadravanti | sa āgacchati vijarāṃ nadīm | tāṃ manasaivātyeti | tat sukṛtaduṣkṛte dhunuvāte | tasya priyā jñātayaḥ sukṛtam upayanti, apriyā duṣkṛtam | tad yathā rathena dhāvayan rathacakre paryavekṣeta | evam āhorātre paryavekṣeta | evaṃ sukṛtaduṣkṛte sarvāṇi ca dvandvāni | sa eṣa visukṛto duṣkṛto brahma vidvān brahmaivābhipraiti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 3,4 = KU 1,4: Five hundred <s>Apsarases</s> go forth to meet him — a hundred with fruits in their hands, a hundred with ointment in their hands, a hundred with garlands in their hands, a hundred with garments in their hands, a hundred with fragrant powder in their hands. They adorn him with the adornment of <s>Brahman</s>. Adorned with the adornment of <s>Brahman</s>, knowing <s>Brahman</s>, he approaches <s>Brahman</s>. He comes to the lake <s>Āra</s>. He crosses it by the mind. Those who arrive at it without full knowledge sink. He comes to the moments (<s>muhūrtas</s>) called <s>Yaṣṭihā</s> (staff-bearers). They flee from him. He comes to the river <s>Vijarā</s> (Ageless). He crosses it by the mind alone. There he shakes off his good and evil deeds. His dear relatives obtain the good deeds, his unloved ones the evil deeds. Just as one driving a chariot would look down upon the two chariot wheels, so he looks down upon day and night, so upon good and evil deeds, and upon all pairs of opposites. He, freed from good and evil deeds, knowing <s>Brahman</s>, approaches <s>Brahman</s> itself.

children.text:
ŚĀ 3,5 = KU 1,5
sa āgacchatīlyaṃ vṛkṣam | taṃ brahmagandhaḥ praviśati | sa āgacchati sālajyaṃ saṃsthānam | taṃ brahmarasaḥ praviśati | sa āgacchatyaparājitam āyatanam | taṃ brahmayaśaḥ praviśati | sa ācacchatīndraprajāpatī dvāragopau | tāv asmād apadravataḥ | sa āgacchati vibhu pramitam | taṃ brahmatejaḥ praviśati | sa āgacchati vicakṣanām āsandīm | bṛhadrathantare sāmanī pūrvau pādau | śyaitanaudhase cāparau | vairūpavairāje anūcye | śākvararaivate tiraścī | sā prajñā prajñayā hi vipaśyati | sa āgacchatyamitaujasaṃ paryaṅkam | sa prāṇaḥ | tasya bhūtaṃ ca bhaviṣyac ca pūrvau pādau | śrīś cerā cāparau | bhadrayajñāyajñīye śīrṣaṇye | bṛhadrathantare anūcye | ṛcaś ca sāmāni ca prācīnātānāni | yajūṃṣi tiraścīnāni | somāṃśavaḥ upastaraṇam | udgītho 'paśrayaḥ | śrīr upabarhaṇam | tasmin brahmāste | tam itthaṃvid pādenaivāgra ārohati | taṃ brahmā pṛcchati | - ko 'sīti | taṃ pratibrūyāt
||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 3,5 = KU 1,5: He comes to the tree <s>Ilya</s>. The fragrance of <s>Brahman</s> enters him. He comes to the abode <s>Sālajya</s>. The flavor (<s>rasa</s>) of <s>Brahman</s> enters him. He comes to the citadel <s>Aparājita</s> (Unconquered). The glory of <s>Brahman</s> enters him. He comes to the two door-keepers <s>Indra</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s>. They flee from him. He comes to the hall <s>Vibhu</s> (Pervading). The splendor (<s>tejas</s>) of <s>Brahman</s> enters him. He comes to the throne <s>Vicakṣaṇā</s> (Discerning). The <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> <s>sāmans</s> are its front two feet; the <s>Śyaita</s> and <s>Naudhasa</s> its back two. The <s>Vairūpa</s> and <s>Vairāja</s> are its lengthwise [supports]; the <s>Śākvara</s> and <s>Raivata</s> its crosswise [supports]. It is <s>Prajñā</s> (Wisdom), for by wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) one sees clearly. He comes to the couch <s>Amitaujas</s> (of Immeasurable Splendor). It is <s>Prāṇa</s> (Life-breath). Its front two feet are the past and the future; its back two are prosperity (<s>śrī</s>) and beauty (<s>irā</s>). The <s>Bhadra</s> and <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> [sāmans] are the two head-pieces; the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> the lengthwise [supports]. The <s>Ṛc</s> verses and <s>Sāman</s> chants are the lengthwise cords; the <s>Yajus</s> formulas the crosswise ones. <s>Soma</s> rays are the coverlet. The <s>Udgītha</s> (chant) is the cushion. Prosperity (<s>Śrī</s>) is the pillow. Upon it <s>Brahman</s> sits. One who knows thus first mounts it with just one foot. <s>Brahman</s> asks him: 'Who are you?' He should reply:

children.text:
ŚĀ 3,6 = KU 1,6
ṛtur asmi | ārtavo 'smi | ākāśād yoneḥ saṃbhūto bhāryāyai retaḥ, saṃvatsarasya tejobhūtasya bhūtasyātmā | bhūtasya bhūtasya tvam ātmāsi | yas tvam asi so 'ham asmi | tam āha - ko 'ham asmīti | satyam iti brūyāt | kiṃ tad yatsatyam iti | yad anyad devebhyaśca prāṇebhyaś ca tat sat | atha yad devāś ca prāṇāś ca tat satyam | tad ekayā vācābhivyāhriyate sattyam iti | etāvad idaṃ sarvam | idaṃ sarvam asmītyevainaṃ tad āha | tad etac chlokenābhyuktam ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 3,6 = KU 1,6: 'I am a season. I am of the seasons. From space as the womb I am born, as seed for a wife, as the radiance of the year, as the <s>ātman</s> (self) of every being. You are the <s>ātman</s> of every being. What you are, that am I.' [<s>Brahman</s>] says to him: 'Who am I?' He should say: 'The Real (<s>Satya</s>).' 'What is that which is the Real?' 'That which is other than the gods and the vital breaths (<s>prāṇas</s>) — that is <s>sat</s> (being). But the gods and the vital breaths — that is <s>tya</s> (truth). This is expressed by the one word <s>sat-tya-m</s> (Reality/Truth). This is all this [universe]. "You are all this" — thus [<s>Brahman</s>] says to him. This is declared by the verse:'

children.text:
ŚĀ 3,7 = KU 1,7
yajūdaraḥ sāmaśirā asāv ṛṅmūrttir avyayaḥ | sa brahmeti vijñeya ṛṣir brahmamayo mahān || iti | tad āha - kena me pauṃsnāni nāmānyāpnoṣīti | prāṇeneti brūyāt | kena napuṃsakānīti | manaseti | kena strīnāmānīti | vāceti | kena gandhān iti | ghrāṇeneti | kena rūpāṇīti | cakṣuṣeti | kena śabdān iti | śrotreṇeti | kenānnarasān iti | jihvayeti | kena karmāṇīti | hastābhyām iti | kena sukhaduḥkhe iti | śarīreṇeti | kenānandaṃ ratiṃ prajātim iti | upastheneti | kenetyā iti | pādābhyām iti | kena dhiyo vijnātavyaṃ kāmān iti | prajñayaiveti brūyāt |
tam āha - āpo vai khalu me loko 'yaṃ te 'sāv iti | sā yā brahmaṇo jitir yā vyaṣṭiḥ, tāṃ jitiṃ jayati, tāṃ vyaṣṭiṃ vyaśnute ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 3,7 = KU 1,7: Whose belly is the <s>Yajus</s>, whose head is the <s>Sāman</s>, who is that one whose form is the <s>Ṛc</s>, the imperishable one — he is to be known as <s>Brahman</s>, the great seer composed of <s>Brahman</s>. Then he says: 'By what do you obtain my masculine names?' 'By <s>prāṇa</s> (breath),' one should reply. 'By what the neuter names?' 'By mind.' 'By what the feminine names?' 'By speech.' 'By what odors?' 'By the sense of smell.' 'By what forms?' 'By sight.' 'By what sounds?' 'By hearing.' 'By what tastes of food?' 'By the tongue.' 'By what actions?' 'By the hands.' 'By what pleasure and pain?' 'By the body.' 'By what bliss, delight, and procreation?' 'By the generative organ.' 'By what movement?' 'By the feet.' 'By what thoughts, that which is to be known, and desires?' 'By <s>prajñā</s> (intelligence) alone,' one should reply. He says to him: 'Waters indeed are my world; that [world] is yours.' Whatever victory belongs to <s>Brahman</s>, whatever attainment — that victory he wins, that attainment he attains, who knows thus, who knows thus.

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,1 = KU 2,1
prāṇo brahmeti ha smāha kauṣītakiḥ | tasya vā etasya prāṇasya brahmaṇo mano dūtam, cakṣur goptṛ, śrotraṃ śrāvayitṛ, vāk pariveṣṭrī | sa yo ha vā etasya prāṇasya brahmaṇo mano dūtaṃ veda dūtavān bhavati | yaś cakṣur goptṛ goptṛmān bhavati | yaḥ śrotraṃ śrāvayitṛ saṃśrāvayitṛmān bhavati | yo vācaṃ pariveṣṭrīṃ pariveṣṭrīmān bhavati | tasmai vā etasmai brahmaṇa etā devatā ayācamānāya baliṃ haranti | evaṃ haivāsmai sarvāṇi bhūtānyayācamānāyaiva baliṃ haranti ya evaṃ veda | tasyopaniṣan na yāced iti | tad yathā grāmaṃ bhikṣitvālabdhvupaviśen nāham ato dattam aśnīyām iti | ta evainam upamantrayante ye purastāt pratyācakṣīran | eṣa dharmo 'yācato bhavati | annadās tvevainam upamantrayante - dadāma ta iti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 4,1 = KU 2,1: '<s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) is <s>Brahman</s>' — thus declared <s>Kauṣītaki</s>. Of this <s>Prāṇa</s> that is <s>Brahman</s>, mind is the messenger, sight is the guardian, hearing is the announcer, speech is the attendant. He who knows that mind is the messenger of this <s>Prāṇa</s> that is <s>Brahman</s> becomes possessed of a messenger. He who knows sight as its guardian becomes possessed of a guardian. He who knows hearing as its announcer becomes possessed of an announcer. He who knows speech as its attendant becomes possessed of an attendant. To this <s>Brahman</s>, all these deities bring tribute without being asked. Likewise, to one who knows thus, all beings bring tribute without being asked. The secret teaching (<s>upaniṣad</s>) thereof is: 'One should not beg.' It is as if a man, having begged through a village and not having obtained, were to sit down saying, 'I would not eat what is given from here.' Then those very ones who previously refused him invite him [saying], 'Let us give to you.' This is the <s>dharma</s> (rule) of one who does not beg. The food-givers themselves invite him, saying: 'We shall give to you.'

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,2 = KU 2,2
prāṇo brahmeti ha smāha paiṅgyaḥ | tasya vā etasya prāṇasya brahmaṇo vāk parastāc cakṣur ārundhate | cakṣuḥ parastātc chrotraṃ ārundhate | śrotraṃ parastān mana ārundhathe | manaḥ parastāt prāṇa ārundhate | tasmai vā etasmai prāṇāya brahmaṇa etā devatā ayācamānāya baliṃ haranti | evaṃ haivāsmai sarvāṇi bhūtānyayācamānāyaiva baliṃ haranti | ya evaṃ veda tasyopaniṣan na yāced iti | tad yathā grāmaṃ bhikṣitvālabdhvupaviśen nāham ato dattam aśnīyām iti | ta evainam upamantrayante ye purastāt pratyācakṣīran | eṣa dharmo 'yācato bhavati | annadās tvevainam upamantrayante - dadāma ta iti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 4,2 = KU 2,2: '<s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) is <s>Brahman</s>' — thus declared <s>Paiṅgya</s>. Of this <s>Prāṇa</s> that is <s>Brahman</s>, speech is enclosed beyond [it]; sight is enclosed beyond speech; hearing is enclosed beyond sight; mind is enclosed beyond hearing; <s>prāṇa</s> is enclosed beyond mind. To this <s>Prāṇa</s> that is <s>Brahman</s>, all these deities bring tribute without being asked. Likewise, to one who knows thus, all beings bring tribute without being asked. The secret teaching (<s>upaniṣad</s>) thereof is: 'One should not beg.' It is as if a man, having begged through a village and not having obtained, were to sit down saying, 'I would not eat what is given from here.' Then those very ones who previously refused him invite him. This is the <s>dharma</s> (rule) of one who does not beg. The food-givers themselves invite him, saying: 'We shall give to you.'

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,3 = KU 2,3
athāta ekadhanāvarodhanam | ya ekadhanam abhidhyāyāt paurṇamāsyāṃ vāmāvāsyāyāṃ vā śuddhapakṣe vā puṇye nakṣatra eteṣām ekasmin parvaṇyagnim upasamādhāya parisamuhya paristīrya paryukṣya dakṣiṇaṃ ānvācya sruveṇāyahutīr juhoti | vāṅ nāma devatāvarodhinī sā me 'muṣmād idam avarundhyāt tasyai svāhā | prāṇo nāma devatāvarodhinī sā me 'muṣmād idam avarundhyāt tasyai svāhā | śrotraṃ nāma devatāvarodhinī sā me 'muṣmād idam avarundhyāt tasyai svāhā | mano nāma devatāvarodhinī sā me 'muṣmād idam avarundhyāt tasyai svāhā | prajñā nāma devatāvarodhinī sā me 'muṣmād idam avarundhyāt tasyai svāhā | atha dhūmagandhaṃ prajighrāyājyalepanenāṅgānyanuvimṛjya vācaṃyamo 'bhipravrajyārthaṃ +brūyād dūtaṃ vā prahiṇuyāt | labhate haiva ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 4,3 = KU 2,3: Now, the rite of obtaining a single treasure (<s>ekadhanāvarodhana</s>). If one should desire a single treasure, on a full-moon night, or on a new-moon night, or during the bright fortnight, or under an auspicious asterism, at one of these junctures, having built up the fire, swept around it, spread the sacrificial grass, sprinkled water, and bent the right knee, he offers oblations of ghee with the ladle: 'Speech by name is the deity that obtains — may she obtain this for me from so-and-so; to her, <s>svāhā</s>!' 'Breath by name is the deity that obtains — may it obtain this for me from so-and-so; to it, <s>svāhā</s>!' 'Hearing by name is the deity that obtains — may it obtain this for me from so-and-so; to it, <s>svāhā</s>!' 'Mind by name is the deity that obtains — may it obtain this for me from so-and-so; to it, <s>svāhā</s>!' 'Intelligence by name is the deity that obtains — may she obtain this for me from so-and-so; to her, <s>svāhā</s>!' Then, having smelled the scent of the smoke and rubbed his limbs with the remnants of ghee, maintaining silence, he should go forth and declare his purpose or send a messenger. He indeed obtains [his desire].

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,4 = KU 2,4
athāto daivaḥ smaraḥ | yasya priyo bubhūṣed yasyai yeṣāṃ vā yāsāṃ vaiteṣām evaikasmin parvaṇyetayaivāvṛtaitā ājyāhutīr juhoti | vācaṃ te mayi juhomyasau svāhā | prāṇaṃ te mayi juhomyasau svāhā | mayi cakṣus te juhomyasau svāhā | śrotraṃ te mayi juhomyasau svāhā | manas te mayi juhomyasau svāhā | prajñāṃ te mayi juhomyasau svāheti | atha dhūmagandhaṃ prajighrāyājyalepanenāṅgānyanuvimṛjya vācaṃyamo 'bhipravrajy saṃsparśaṃ jigamiṣet | abhivātād vā tiṣṭhet saṃbhāṣamāṇaḥ | priyo haiva bhavati | smarate haivāsya ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 4,4 = KU 2,4: Now, the divine love-charm (<s>daivaḥ smaraḥ</s>). If one wishes to become dear to any man or woman, or to any men or women, at one of these same junctures, by this same procedure, he offers these oblations of ghee: 'Your speech I offer into myself, O so-and-so, <s>svāhā</s>!' 'Your breath I offer into myself, O so-and-so, <s>svāhā</s>!' 'Your sight I offer into myself, O so-and-so, <s>svāhā</s>!' 'Your hearing I offer into myself, O so-and-so, <s>svāhā</s>!' 'Your mind I offer into myself, O so-and-so, <s>svāhā</s>!' 'Your intelligence I offer into myself, O so-and-so, <s>svāhā</s>!' Then, having smelled the scent of the smoke and rubbed his limbs with the remnants of ghee, maintaining silence, he should go forth and seek to make contact, or should stand upwind while conversing. He indeed becomes dear [to that person]. That person indeed remembers him.

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,5 = KU 2,5
athātaḥ sāṃyamanaṃ prātardanam | āntaram agnihotram ityācakṣate | yāvad vai puruṣo bhāṣate na tāvat prāṇituṃ śaknoti | prāṇaṃ tadā vāci juhoti | yāvad vai puruṣaḥ prāṇiti na tāvad bhāṣituṃ śaknoti | vācaṃ tadā prāṇe juhoti | ete anante amṛte āhutī jāgracca svapaṃśca saṃtataṃ juhoti | atha yā anyā āhutayo 'ntavatyas tāḥ karmamayyo hi bhavanti | tad dha smaitat pūrve vidvāṃso 'gnihotraṃ na juhavāñcakruḥ ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 4,5 = KU 2,5: Now, the restraint [taught by] <s>Prātardana</s>, which they call the 'inner <s>agnihotra</s>' (fire-sacrifice). As long as a person speaks, he cannot breathe; he thereby offers breath into speech. As long as a person breathes, he cannot speak; he thereby offers speech into breath. These two are unending, immortal oblations that one offers continuously, whether waking or sleeping. All other oblations have an end, for they consist of [ritual] action. Knowing this, the ancient sages did not perform the [external] <s>agnihotra</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,6 = KU 2,6
ukthaṃ brahmeti ha smāha śuṣkabhṛṅgāraḥ | tad ṛg ityupāsīta | sarvāṇi hāsmai bhūtani śraiṣṭhyāyābhyacyante | tad yajur ityupāsīta | sarvāṇi hāsmai bhūtāni śraiṣṭhyāya yujyante | tat sāma ityupāsīta | sarvāṇi hāsmai bhūtāni śraiṣṭhyāya saṃnamante | tac chrīr ityupāsīt | tad yaśa ityupāsīta | tat teja ityupāsīta | tad yathaitac chrīmattamaṃ yaśasvitamaṃ tejasvitamam iti śastreṣu bhavati | evaṃ haiva sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu śrīmattamo yaśasvitamas tejasitamo bhavati ya evaṃ veda | tad etad aiṣṭikaṃ karma yam ātmānam adhvaryuḥ saṃskaroti | tasmin yajurmayaṃ pravayati | yajurmaya ṛṅmayaṃ hotā | ṛṅmaye sāmamayam udgātā | sa eṣa trayyai vidyāyā ātmā | eṣa u evaitad indrasyātmā bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 4,6 = KU 2,6: 'The <s>uktha</s> (hymn of praise) is <s>Brahman</s>' — thus declared <s>Śuṣkabhṛṅgāra</s>. One should meditate on it as <s>Ṛc</s> (verse); then all beings bow down to him for his preeminence. One should meditate on it as <s>Yajus</s> (sacrificial formula); then all beings are yoked to him for his preeminence. One should meditate on it as <s>Sāman</s> (chant); then all beings bow down to him for his preeminence. One should meditate on it as <s>Śrī</s> (glory). One should meditate on it as <s>Yaśas</s> (fame). One should meditate on it as <s>Tejas</s> (splendor). Just as this [uktha] is the most glorious, the most famous, the most splendid among the <s>śastras</s> (recitations), so too does one who knows thus become the most glorious, the most famous, the most splendid among all beings. This is the <s>aiṣṭika</s> (sacrificial) rite: the self which the <s>Adhvaryu</s> priest prepares — into that he weaves what is made of <s>Yajus</s>; into what is made of <s>Yajus</s>, the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest [weaves] what is made of <s>Ṛc</s>; into what is made of <s>Ṛc</s>, the <s>Udgātṛ</s> priest [weaves] what is made of <s>Sāman</s>. This is the self of the threefold knowledge (<s>trayī vidyā</s>). And this indeed becomes the self of <s>Indra</s> — he who knows thus.

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,7 = KU 2,7
athātaḥ sarvajitaḥ kauṣītakes trīṇyupāsanāni bhavanti | sarvajid dha sma kauṣītakir udyantam ādityam upatiṣṭhate yajñopavītaṃ kṛtvodakam ānīya triḥ prasicyodakapātram | vargo 'si pāpmānaṃ me vṛṅdhīti | etayaivāvṛtā madhye santam | udvargo 'si pāpmānaṃ ma udvṛṅdhīti | etayaivāvṛtāstaṃ yantam | saṃvargo 'si pāpmānaṃ me saṃvṛṅdhīti | tad yad ahorātrābhyāṃ pāpaṃ karoti saṃ tad vṛṅkte | tatho evaivaṃ vidvān etayaivāvṛtādityam upatiṣṭhate | yad ahorātrābhyāṃ pāpaṃ karoti saṃ tad vṛṅkte ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 4,7 = KU 2,7: Now, the three meditations of <s>Sarvajit Kauṣītaki</s>. <s>Sarvajit Kauṣītaki</s> used to worship the rising sun, having put on the sacred thread, brought water, and sprinkled [the water vessel] three times [saying]: 'You are <s>Varga</s> (the remover) — remove my sin!' By this same procedure, [he worships the sun] at midday: 'You are <s>Udvarga</s> (the upward remover) — remove my sin upward!' By this same procedure, [he worships the] setting [sun]: 'You are <s>Saṃvarga</s> (the complete remover) — completely remove my sin!' Whatever sin he commits by day and night, that he removes. Likewise, one who knows thus and worships the sun by this same procedure — whatever sin he commits by day and night, that he removes.

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,8 = KU 2,8
atha māsimāsyāvāsyāyāṃ vṛttāyāṃ paścāc candramasaṃ dṛśyamānam upatiṣṭhetaitayaivāvṛtā | haritatṛṇe vā pratyasya - yan me susīmaṃ hṛdayaṃ divi candramasi śritam | manye 'haṃ māṃ tad vidvāṃsaṃ māhaṃ putryam aghaṃ rudam || iti | na hyasmāt pūrvā prajā praitīti nu jātaputrasya | athājātaputrasya - āpyāyasva sametu +te, saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājāḥ, yam ādityā aṃśum āpyāyayantītyetās tisra ṛco japitvā - māsmākaṃ prāṇena prajayā paśubhir āpyāyayiṣṭhāḥ | yo' smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmas tasya prāṇena prajayā paśubhir āpyāyayasvetyaindrīm āvṛtam āvarta ādityasyāvṛtam anvāvarta iti dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum anvāvartate ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 4,8 = KU 2,8: Now, month by month, when the new-moon night has passed, one should worship the moon as it appears in the west, by this same procedure. Or, having cast [a glance] at green grass, [one recites]: 'That which is my well-bounded heart, established in the moon in heaven — I consider myself as one who knows that; may I not weep over misfortune to my children.' Indeed, his offspring does not die before him — this is [the rite] for one who has a son already born. For one whose son is not yet born: having muttered these three <s>ṛcas</s> (verses) — '<s>Āpyāyasva</s>: Swell up, let [nourishment] come together for you, let your milk streams and your vigors unite, that drop which the <s>Ādityas</s> cause to swell' — [he says]: 'Do not swell at the cost of our breath, offspring, and cattle. Swell at the cost of the breath, offspring, and cattle of him who hates us and whom we hate.' Thus he turns with the turn of <s>Indra</s>, he turns with the turn of <s>Āditya</s> — he turns his right arm around.

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,9 = KU 2,9
atha paurṇamāsyāṃ purastāc candramasaṃ dṛśyamānam upatiṣṭhaitayaivāvṛtā | somo rājāsi vicakṣaṇaḥ pañcamukho 'si prajāpatiḥ | brāhmaṇas ta ekaṃ mukhaṃ tena mukhena rājño 'tsi | tena mukhena māṃ annādaṃ kuru | rājā ta ekaṃ mukhaṃ tena mukhena viśo 'tsi | tena mukhena māṃ annādaṃ kuru | śyenas ta ekaṃ mukhaṃ tena mukhena pakṣiṇo 'tsi | tena mukhena māṃ annādaṃ kuru | agniṣ ṭa ekaṃ mukhaṃ tena mukhenemaṃ lokam atsi | tena mukhena māṃ annādaṃ kuru | māsmākaṃ prāṇena prajayā paśubhir apakṣeṣṭhāḥ | yo' smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmas tasya prāṇena prajayā paśubhir apakṣīyasveti daivīm āvṛtam āvarta ādityasyāvṛtam anvāvarta iti dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum anvāvartate ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 4,9 = KU 2,9
Then on the full-moon night, one should worship the moon as it becomes visible in the east, with this same formula: 'You are <s>Soma</s>, the king, the discerning one. You are five-faced. You are <s>Prajāpati</s>. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (priest) is one face of yours; by that face you consume kings. By that face make me an eater of food. The king is one face of yours; by that face you consume the common people. By that face make me an eater of food. The hawk is one face of yours; by that face you consume birds. By that face make me an eater of food. Fire is one face of yours; by that face you consume this world. By that face make me an eater of food. Do not diminish us in breath, offspring, and cattle. He who hates us and whom we hate—diminish him in breath, offspring, and cattle.' 'I turn the divine turn, I turn the turn of <s>Āditya</s>' — thus he turns his right arm around.

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,10 = KU 2,10
atha saṃvekṣyan jāyāyai hṛdayam abhi mṛśet - yat te susīme hṛdayaṃ śritam antaḥ prajāpatau | tenāmṛtatvasyeśāne mā tvaṃ putryam aghaṃ ni gā iti || na hyasyāḥ pūrvā prajā praitīti ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 4,10 = KU 2,10
Then, when about to cohabit, he should touch his wife's heart [and say]: 'O beautiful one (<s>susīme</s>), your heart that rests within <s>Prajāpati</s>—by that, O mistress of immortality, may you not come to grief on account of your children.' For her earlier offspring does not perish.

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,11 = KU 2,11
atha proṣyāyan putrasya mūrdhanam abhijighret - aṅgād aṅgāt saṃbhavasi hṛdayād adhi jāyase | ātmā vai putranāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śatam iti nāmāsya dadhāti | aśmā bhava paraśur bhava, hiraṇyam astṛtaṃ bhava | tejo vai putrānāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śatam iti nāmāsya gṛhṇāti | athainaṃ parigṛhṇāti | yena prajāpatiḥ prajāḥ paryagṛhṇāt tad ariṣṭyaitena tvā parigṛhṇāmi, asāv iti | athāsya dakṣiṇe karṇe japati - asme prayandhi maghavann ṛjīṣin iti | indraṃ śreṣṭhāni draviṇāni dhehīti savye | mā bhetthā mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ śataṃ śarada āyuṣaḥ | jīvasva putra te nāmnā mūrdhānam abhijighrāmīti trir asya mūrdānam abhijighret | gavāṃ tvāṃ hiṃkāreṇābhihiṃkaromīti trir asya mūrdhānam abhihiṃkaroti ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 4,11 = KU 2,11
Then, when about to go on a journey, he should smell his son's head [and say]: 'From limb after limb you are born, from the heart you arise. You are truly the self called son. Live a hundred autumns'—thus he gives him a name. 'Be a stone, be an axe, be uncut gold. You are indeed the splendor called son. Live a hundred autumns'—thus he calls his name. Then he embraces him: 'With that embrace by which <s>Prajāpati</s> embraced his offspring for their safety, with that I embrace you, so-and-so.' Then he whispers in his right ear: 'Bestow upon us, O bounteous one, O winner of spoils.' In the left [ear]: 'O <s>Indra</s>, bestow the choicest riches.' 'Do not fear, do not tremble. May you have a hundred autumns of life. Live, O son! By your name I smell your head'—three times he smells his head. 'With the lowing of cows I low over you'—three times he lows over his head.

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,12 = KU 2,12
athato daivaḥ parimaraḥ | etad vai brahma dīpyate yad agnir jvalati | athaitan mriyate yan na jvalati | tasyādityam eva tejo gacchati vāyuṃ prāṇaḥ | etad vai brahma dīpyate yad ādityo dṛśyate | athaitan mriyate yan na dṛśyate | tasya candramasam eva tejo gacchati vāyuṃ prāṇaḥ | etad vai brahma dīpyate yac candramā dṛśyate | athaitan mriyate yan na dṛśyate | tasya vidyutam eva tejo gacchati vāyuṃ prāṇaḥ | etad vai brahma dīpyate yad vidyud vidyotate | athaitan mriyate yan na vidyotate | tasyādiśa eva tejo gacchati vāyuṃ prāṇaḥ | tā vā etā sarvā devatā vāyum eva praviśya vāyau mṛtvā na mṛcchante | tasmād eva punarudīrate | ityadhidaivam | athādhyātmam ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 4,12 = KU 2,12
Now, concerning the divine dying-around (<s>daivaḥ parimaraḥ</s>). This <s>Brahman</s> indeed shines when fire blazes. And it dies when it does not blaze. Its radiance goes to the sun, its breath to <s>Vāyu</s> (wind). This <s>Brahman</s> indeed shines when the sun is seen. And it dies when it is not seen. Its radiance goes to the moon, its breath to <s>Vāyu</s>. This <s>Brahman</s> indeed shines when the moon is seen. And it dies when it is not seen. Its radiance goes to lightning, its breath to <s>Vāyu</s>. This <s>Brahman</s> indeed shines when lightning flashes. And it dies when it does not flash. Its radiance goes to the quarters, its breath to <s>Vāyu</s>. All these deities, having entered <s>Vāyu</s> alone, having died in <s>Vāyu</s>, do not perish. From there indeed they rise again. This is with reference to the divine. Now with reference to the self.

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,13 = KU 2,13
