etad vai brahma dīpyate yad vācā vadati | athaitan mriyate yan na vadati | tasya cakṣur eva tejo gacchati | prāṇaṃ prāṇaḥ | etad vai brahma dīpyate yac cakṣuṣā paśyati | athaitan mriyate yan na paśyati | tasya śrotram eva tejo gacchati | prāṇaṃ prāṇaḥ | etad vai brahma dīpyate yac chrotreṇa śṛṇoti | athaitan mriyate yan na śṛṇoti | tasya mana eva tejo gacchati | prāṇaṃ prāṇaḥ | etad vai brahma dīpyate yan manasā dhyāyati | athaitan mriyate yan na dhyāyati | tasya prāṇam eva tejo gacchati | prāṇaṃ prāṇaḥ | tā vā etā sarvā devatā prāṇam eva praviśya prāṇe mṛtvā na mṛcchante | tasmād eva punar udīrate | tad yad iha vā evaṃ vidvāṃsam ubhau parvatāv abhipravarteyātāṃ dakṣiṇaścottaraś ca tustūrṣamāṇau na hainaṃ stṛṇvīyātām | atha ya enaṃ dviṣanti yāṃś ca svayaṃ dveṣṭi ta evainaṃ parimriyante ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 4,13 = KU 2,13
This <s>Brahman</s> indeed shines when one speaks with speech. And it dies when one does not speak. Its radiance goes to the eye, its breath to <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath). This <s>Brahman</s> indeed shines when one sees with the eye. And it dies when one does not see. Its radiance goes to the ear, its breath to <s>prāṇa</s>. This <s>Brahman</s> indeed shines when one hears with the ear. And it dies when one does not hear. Its radiance goes to the mind, its breath to <s>prāṇa</s>. This <s>Brahman</s> indeed shines when one thinks with the mind. And it dies when one does not think. Its radiance goes to <s>prāṇa</s>, its breath to <s>prāṇa</s>. All these deities, having entered <s>prāṇa</s> alone, having died in <s>prāṇa</s>, do not perish. From there indeed they rise again. Even if both mountains, southern and northern, were to roll toward one who knows thus, seeking to crush him, they could not crush him. But those who hate him and those whom he himself hates—they indeed die around him.

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,14 = KU 2,14
athāto niḥśreyasādānam | etā ha vai devatā ahaṃśreyase vividamānā asmāc charīrād uccakramuḥ | tad dha papāta, śuṣkaṃ dārubhūtaṃ śiśye | athainad vāk praviveśa | tad vācā vadac chiśya eva | athainac cakṣuḥ praviveśa | tad vācā vadac cakṣuṣā paśyac chiśya eva | athainac chrotraṃ praviveśa | tad vācā vadac cakṣuṣā paśyac chrotreṇa śṛṇvac chiśya eva | athainan manaḥ praviveśa | tad vācā vadac cakṣuṣā paśyac chrotreṇa śṛṇvan manasā dhyāyac chiśya eva | athainat prāṇaḥ praviveśa | tat tata eva samuttasthau | tā vā etā sarvā devatā prāṇe niḥśreyasaṃ viditvā prāṇam eva prajñātmānam abhisaṃbhūya +sahaivaitaiḥ sarvair asmāc charīrād uccakramuḥ | te vāyupratiṣṭhā ākāśātmānaḥ svar īyuḥ | tatho evaivaṃ vidvān prāṇe niḥśreyasaṃ viditvā prāṇam eva prajñātmānam abhisaṃbhūya +sahaivaitaiḥ sarvair asmāc charīrād utkrāmati | sa vāyupratiṣṭha ākāśātmā svar eti | sa tad gacchati yatraite devāḥ | tat prāpya yad amṛtā devāḥ | tad amṛto bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 4,14 = KU 2,14
Now, the teaching of <s>niḥśreyasa</s> (the highest good). These deities indeed, contending among themselves for supremacy, departed from this body. It fell down and lay like a dried-up piece of wood. Then speech entered it. Speaking with speech, it still lay there. Then the eye entered it. Speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, it still lay there. Then the ear entered it. Speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear, it still lay there. Then the mind entered it. Speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear, thinking with the mind, it still lay there. Then <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) entered it. Thereupon it immediately rose up. All these deities, having recognized the highest good in <s>prāṇa</s>, having united with <s>prāṇa</s> alone as the intelligent self, departed together with all of these from this body. They, established in <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), having <s>ākāśa</s> (space) as their self, went to heaven. Likewise, one who knows thus, having recognized the highest good in <s>prāṇa</s>, having united with <s>prāṇa</s> alone as the intelligent self, departs together with all of these from this body. Established in <s>Vāyu</s>, having <s>ākāśa</s> as his self, he goes to heaven. He goes to where these gods are. Having reached that which the immortal gods have reached, he becomes immortal—he who knows thus.

children.text:
ŚĀ 4,15 = KU 2,15
athātaḥ pitāputrīyaṃ saṃpradānam iti cācakṣate | pitā putraṃ preṣyann āhvayati | navais tṛṇair agāraṃ saṃstīryāgnim upasamādhāyodakumbhaṃ sapātram upanidhāyāhatena vāsasā saṃpracchannaḥ pitā śete | etya putra upariṣṭād abhinipadyata indriyair indriyāṇi saṃspṛśya | api vāsmā āsīnāyābhimukhāyaiva saṃpradadyāt | athāsmai saṃprayacchati | vācaṃ me tvayi dadhānīti pitā | vācaṃ te mayi dadha iti putraḥ | prāṇaṃ me tvayi dadhānīti pitā | prāṇaṃ te mayi dadha iti putraḥ | cakṣur me tvayi dadhānīti pitā | cakṣus te mayi dadha iti putraḥ | śrotraṃ me tvayi dadhānīti pitā | śrotraṃ te mayi dadha iti putraḥ | annarasān me tvayi dadhānīti pitā | annarasāṃs te mayi dadha iti putraḥ | karmāṇi me tvayi dadhānīti
pitā | karmāṇi te mayi dadha iti putraḥ | sukhaduḥkhe me tvayi dadhānīti pitā | sukhaduḥkhe te mayi dadha iti putraḥ | ānandaṃ ratiṃ prajātiṃ me tvayi dadhānīti pitā | ānandaṃ ratiṃ prajātiṃ te mayi dadha iti putraḥ | ityāṃ me tvayi dadhānīti pitā | ityāṃ te mayi dadha iti putraḥ | dhiyo vijñātavyaṃ kāmān me tvayi dadhānīti pitā | dhiyo vijñātavyaṃ kāmāṃs te mayi dadha iti putraḥ | mano me tvayi dadhānīti pitā | manas te mayi dadha iti putraḥ | prajñāṃ me tvayi dadhānīti pitā | prajñāṃ te mayi dadha iti putraḥ | yad u vā upābhigadaḥ syāt samāsenaiva brūyāt | prāṇān me tvayi dadhānīti pitā | prāṇāṃs te mayi dadha iti
putraḥ | atha dakṣiṇāvṛd upaniṣkrāmati | taṃ pitrānumantrayate | yaśo brahmavarcasaṃ kīrtis tvā juṣatām iti | athetaraḥ savyam anvaṃsam abhyavekṣate | pāṇināntardhāya vasanāntena vā pracchādya svargāṁl lokān kāmān āpnuhīti | sa yadyugadaḥ syāt putrasyaiśvarye pitā vaset | pari vā vrajet | yadyu vai preyāt tathaivainaṃ samāpayeyuḥ | yathā samāpayitavyo bhavati yathā samāpayitavyo bhavati ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 4,15 = KU 2,15
Now, the father-to-son transmission (<s>pitāputrīya saṃpradāna</s>)—thus they call it. A father, when about to depart, summons his son. Having strewn the house with fresh grass, having built up the fire, having placed a water-pot with a vessel beside it, the father lies down covered with a fresh garment. The son comes and lies down on top, touching organ to organ. Or the father may transmit to him while he sits face to face. Then he transmits to him: 'I place my speech in you,' says the father. 'I take your speech in me,' says the son. 'I place my breath in you,' says the father. 'I take your breath in me,' says the son. 'I place my eye in you,' says the father. 'I take your eye in me,' says the son. 'I place my ear in you,' says the father. 'I take your ear in me,' says the son. 'I place my food-essences in you,' says the father. 'I take your food-essences in me,' says the son. 'I place my actions in you,' says the father. 'I take your actions in me,' says the son. 'I place my pleasure and pain in you,' says the father. 'I take your pleasure and pain in me,' says the son. 'I place my bliss, delight, and procreation in you,' says the father. 'I take your bliss, delight, and procreation in me,' says the son. 'I place my movement in you,' says the father. 'I take your movement in me,' says the son. 'I place my thoughts, knowledge, and desires in you,' says the father. 'I take your thoughts, knowledge, and desires in me,' says the son. 'I place my mind in you,' says the father. 'I take your mind in me,' says the son. 'I place my wisdom in you,' says the father. 'I take your wisdom in me,' says the son. If however he is too ill to speak, he should say it in summary: 'I place my vital breaths in you,' says the father. 'I take your vital breaths in me,' says the son. Then he departs turning to the right. The father blesses him: 'May glory, sacred splendor, and fame attend you.' Then the other looks over his left shoulder, covering his face with his hand or concealing it with the edge of his garment: 'May you attain the heavenly worlds and desires.' If he recovers, the father should live under the authority of his son, or he should become a wandering ascetic. But if he should die, they should perform the funeral rites for him as he ought to be cremated, as he ought to be cremated.

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 5,1 = KU 3,1
pratardano ha vai daivodāsir indrasya priyaṃ dhāmopajagāma yuddhena ca pauruṣeṇa ca | taṃ indra uvāca pratardanaṃ varaṃ vṛṇīṣveti | sa hovāca pratardanaḥ - tvam eva me vṛṇīṣva yaṃ tvaṃ manuṣyāya hitatamaṃ manyasa iti | taṃ indra uvāca - na vai varo 'varasmai vṛṇīte | tvam eva vṛṇīṣveti | avaro vai kila meti hovāca pratardanaḥ | atho khalvindraḥ satyād eva neyāya | satyaṃ hīndraḥ | taṃ hendra uvāca - mām eva vijānīhi | etad evāhaṃ manuṣyāya hitatamaṃ manye yo māṃ vijānīyāt | triśīrṣāṇaṃ tvāṣṭram ahanam | arurmukhān yatīn sālāvṛkebhyaḥ prāyacchham | bahvīḥ saṃdhā atrikramya divi prahlādīyān atṛṇaham antarikṣe, paulomān pṛthivyāṃ kālakhañjā | tasya me tatra na lomacanāmīyata | sa yo māṃ veda na ha vai tasya kena ca karmaṇā loko mīyate | na steyena na bhrūṇahatyayā na mātṛvadhena na pitṛvadhena | nādya pāpaṃ cakruṣo mukhān nīlaṃ vyetīti ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 5,1 = KU 3,1
<s>Pratardana</s>, son of <s>Divodāsa</s>, indeed came to the beloved abode of <s>Indra</s> through battle and through heroism. <s>Indra</s> said to <s>Pratardana</s>: "Choose a boon." <s>Pratardana</s> said: "You yourself choose for me that which you consider most beneficial for a human being." <s>Indra</s> said to him: "A superior does not choose for an inferior. You yourself choose." <s>Pratardana</s> said: "Then I am indeed an inferior." But then <s>Indra</s> did not deviate from the truth, for <s>Indra</s> is truth. <s>Indra</s> said to him: "Know me alone. This is what I consider most beneficial for a human being—that one should know me. I slew the three-headed son of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>. I delivered the <s>Arunmukha</s> ascetics to the wolves. Transgressing many compacts, I destroyed the <s>Prahlādīyas</s> in heaven, the <s>Paulomas</s> in the atmosphere, and the <s>Kālakhañjas</s> on earth. In all that, not a single hair of mine was harmed. He who knows me—his world is not diminished by any action whatsoever: not by theft, not by the killing of an embryo, not by the murder of his mother, not by the murder of his father. Even if he has committed evil, the dark color does not leave his face."

children.text:
ŚĀ 5,2 = KU 3,2
sa hovāca prāṇo 'smi prajñātmā | taṃ mām āyur amṛtam ityupāsva | āyuḥ prāṇaḥ | prāṇo vā āyuḥ | yāvad +dhyasmin śarīre prāṇo bhavati yāvad āyuḥ | prāṇena hyevāsmiṁl loke 'mṛtatvam āpnoti | prajñayā satyaṃ saṃkalpaṃ | sa yo mām āyur amṛtam ityupāste | sarvam āyur asmil loka eti | āpnotyamṛtatvam akṣitiṃ svarge loke | tad dhaika āhur ekabhūyaṃ vai prāṇā gacchantīti | na hi kaścana śaknuyāt sakṛd vācā nāma prajñāpayituṃ cakṣuṣā rūpaṃ śrotreṇa śabdaṃ manasā dhyātum | ekabhūyaṃ vai prāṇā bhūtvaivaikaikam etāni sarvāṇi prajñāpayantīti | vācaṃ vadantīṃ sarve prāṇā anuvadanti | cakṣuḥ paśyat sarve prāṇā anupaśyanti | śrotraṃ śṛṇvat sarve prāṇā anuśṛṇvanti | mano dhyāyat sarve prāṇā anudhyāyanti | prāṇaṃ prāṇantaṃ sarve prāṇā anuprāṇanti | evam u haitad iti hendra uvāca | asti tveva prāṇānāṃ niḥśreyasam iti ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 5,2 = KU 3,2
He said: "I am <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), the conscious self (<s>prajñātman</s>). Worship me as life, as immortality. Life is <s>prāṇa</s>; <s>prāṇa</s> is life. As long as <s>prāṇa</s> remains in this body, so long is life. For by <s>prāṇa</s> alone one obtains immortality in this world; by <s>prajñā</s> (consciousness), true resolve. He who worships me as life and immortality attains a full life in this world and obtains immortality and imperishability in the heavenly world." Regarding this, some say: "The vital functions indeed become one." For no one could simultaneously make known a name through speech, a form through sight, a sound through hearing, or a thought through mind. Rather, the vital functions, having become one, make each of these known one by one. When speech speaks, all the vital functions speak along with it. When the eye sees, all the vital functions see along with it. When the ear hears, all the vital functions hear along with it. When the mind thinks, all the vital functions think along with it. When <s>prāṇa</s> breathes, all the vital functions breathe along with it. "It is indeed so," said <s>Indra</s>. "But there is a supreme good among the vital functions."

children.text:
ŚĀ 5,3 = KU 3,3
jīvati vāgapetaḥ | mūkān hi paśyāmaḥ | jīvati cakṣurapetaḥ | anvān hi paśyāmaḥ | jīvati śrotrāpetaḥ | badhirān hi paśyāmaḥ | jīvati mano'petaḥ | bālān hi paśyāmaḥ | jīvati bāhucchinnaḥ | jīvatyūrucchinnaḥ | ityevaṃ hi paśyāma iti | atha khalu prāṇa eva prajñātmedaṃ śarīraṃ parigṛhyotthāpayati | tasmād etad evoktham upāsīteti | saiṣā prāṇe sarvāptiḥ | yo vai prāṇaḥ sā prajñā | yā vā prajñā sa prāṇaḥ | tasyaiṣaiva dṛṣṭiḥ | etad vijñānam | yatraitat puruṣaḥ suptaḥ svapnaṃ na kaṃcana paśyati | athāsmin prāṇa evaikadhā bhavati | tad enaṃ vāk sarvair nāmabhiḥ sahāpyeti | cakṣuḥ sarvai rūpaiḥ sahāpyeti | śrotraṃ sarvaiḥ śabdaiḥ sahāpyeti | manaḥ sarvair dhyānaiḥ sahāpyeti | sa yadā pratibudhyate | yathāgner jvalataḥ sarvā diśo
visphuliṅgā vipratiṣṭheran evam evaitasmād ātmanaḥ prāṇā yathāyatanaṃ vipratiṣṭhante | prāṇebhyo devāḥ | devebhyo lokāḥ | sa eṣa prāṇa eva prajñātmedaṃ śarīraṃ parigṛhyotthāpayati | tasmād etad evoktham upāsīteti | saiṣā prāṇe sarvāptiḥ | yo vai prāṇaḥ sā prajñā | yā vā prajñā sa prāṇaḥ | tasyaiṣaiva siddhiḥ | etad vijñānam | yatraitat puruṣa ārto mariṣyann ābalyam etya saṃmoham eti | tam āhuḥ - udakramīc cittam | na śṛṇoti | na paśyati | na vācā vadati | na dhyāyati | athāsmin prāṇa ekaikadhā bhavati | tad enaṃ vāk sarvair nāmabhiḥ sahāpyeti | cakṣuḥ sarvai rūpaiḥ sahāpyeti | śrotraṃ sarvaiḥ śabdaiḥ sahāpyeti | manaḥ sarvair dhyātaiḥ sahāpyeti | sa yadāsmāc charīrād utkrāmati sahaivaitaiḥ sarvair utkrāmati ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 5,3 = KU 3,3
One lives without speech, for we see the mute. One lives without sight, for we see the blind. One lives without hearing, for we see the deaf. One lives without mind, for we see the simple-minded. One lives with arms cut off. One lives with thighs cut off. For thus we observe. But it is <s>prāṇa</s> alone, the conscious self (<s>prajñātman</s>), that takes hold of this body and raises it up. Therefore one should worship this alone as the <s>uktha</s> (hymn of praise). This is the attainment of everything in <s>prāṇa</s>. What is <s>prāṇa</s>, that is <s>prajñā</s> (consciousness). What is <s>prajñā</s>, that is <s>prāṇa</s>. This is the proof of that; this is the understanding: When a person is asleep and sees no dream whatsoever, then he becomes one with <s>prāṇa</s> alone. Then speech, together with all names, enters into it; sight, together with all forms, enters into it; hearing, together with all sounds, enters into it; mind, together with all thoughts, enters into it. When he awakens, just as from a blazing fire sparks would fly forth in all directions, even so from this <s>ātman</s> (self) the vital functions go forth to their respective stations; from the vital functions, the gods; from the gods, the worlds. This very <s>prāṇa</s>, the conscious self, takes hold of this body and raises it up. Therefore one should worship this alone as the <s>uktha</s>. This is the attainment of everything in <s>prāṇa</s>. What is <s>prāṇa</s>, that is <s>prajñā</s>. What is <s>prajñā</s>, that is <s>prāṇa</s>. This is the accomplishment of that; this is the understanding: When a person, being ill and about to die, reaches such weakness that he falls into unconsciousness, they say: "His consciousness has departed. He does not hear. He does not see. He does not speak with speech. He does not think." Then he becomes one with <s>prāṇa</s> alone. Then speech, together with all names, enters into it; sight, together with all forms, enters into it; hearing, together with all sounds, enters into it; mind, together with all things thought of, enters into it. When he departs from this body, he departs together with all of these.

children.text:
ŚĀ 5,4 = KU 3,4
vāg evāsmin sarvāṇi nāmānyabhivisṛjyante | vācā sarvāṇi nāmānyāpnoti | prāṇa evāsmin sarve gandhā abhivisṛjyante | prāṇena sarvā gandhān āpnoti | cakṣur evāsmin sarvāṇi rūpāṇyabhivisṛjyante | cakṣuṣā sarvāṇi rūpāṇyāpnoti | śrotram evāsmin sarve śabdā abhivisṛjyante | śrotreṇa sarvāñ chabdān āpnoti | mana evāsmin sarvāṇi dhyātānyabhivisṛjyante | manasā sarvāṇi dhyātānyāpnoti | saha hyetāvasmiñ charīre vasataḥ sahotkrāmataḥ | atha yathāsmai prajñāyai sarvāṇi bhūtānyekaṃ bhavanti | tad vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 5,4 = KU 3,4
Into speech alone are all names deposited; through speech one obtains all names. Into <s>prāṇa</s> alone are all odors deposited; through <s>prāṇa</s> one obtains all odors. Into the eye alone are all forms deposited; through the eye one obtains all forms. Into the ear alone are all sounds deposited; through the ear one obtains all sounds. Into the mind alone are all thoughts deposited; through the mind one obtains all thoughts. For these two dwell together in this body and depart together. Now, how all beings become one for this <s>prajñā</s> (consciousness)—that we shall explain.

children.text:
ŚĀ 5,5 = KU 3,5
vāg evāsyā ekam aṅgam udūḷham | tasyai nāma parastāt prativihitā bhūtamātrā | prāṇa evāsyā ekam aṅgam udūḷham | tasya gandhaḥ parastāt prativihitā bhūtamātrā | cakṣur evāsyā ekam aṅgam udūḷham | tasya rūpaṃ parastāt prativihitā bhūtamātrā | śrotram evāsyā ekam aṅgam udūḷham | tasya śabdaḥ parastāt prativihitā bhūtamātrā | jihvaivāsyā ekam aṅgam udūḷham | tasyā annarasaḥ parastāt prativihitā bhūtamātrā | hastāvevāsyā ekam aṅgam udūḷham | tayoḥ karma parastāt prativihitā bhūtamātrā | śarīramevāsyā ekam aṅgam udūḷham | tasya sukhaduḥkhe parastāt prativihitā bhūtamātrā | upastha evāsyā ekam aṅgam udūḷham | tasyānando ratiḥ prajātiḥ parastāt prativihitā bhūtamātrā | pādāvevāsyā ekam aṅgam udūḷham | tayor ityāḥ parastāt prativihitā bhūtamātrā | mana evāsyā ekam aṅgam udūḷham | tasya dhīḥ kāmāḥ parastāt prativihitā bhūtamātrā ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 5,5 = KU 3,5
Speech is indeed one limb drawn out from it; name is the corresponding external element (<s>bhūtamātrā</s>) placed over against it. <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) is indeed one limb drawn out from it; odor is the corresponding external element placed over against it. The eye is indeed one limb drawn out from it; form is the corresponding external element placed over against it. The ear is indeed one limb drawn out from it; sound is the corresponding external element placed over against it. The tongue is indeed one limb drawn out from it; the taste of food is the corresponding external element placed over against it. The two hands are indeed one limb drawn out from it; action is the corresponding external element placed over against it. The body is indeed one limb drawn out from it; pleasure and pain are the corresponding external elements placed over against it. The generative organ is indeed one limb drawn out from it; bliss, delight, and procreation are the corresponding external elements placed over against it. The two feet are indeed one limb drawn out from it; movements are the corresponding external elements placed over against it. The mind is indeed one limb drawn out from it; intelligence and desires are the corresponding external elements placed over against it.

children.text:
ŚĀ 5,6 = KU 3,6
prajñayā vācaṃ samāruhya vācā sarvāṇi nāmānyāpnoti | prajñayā prāṇaṃ samāruhya prāṇena sarvān gandhān āpnoti | prajñayā cakṣuḥ samāruhya cakṣuṣā sarvāṇi rūpāṇyāpnoti | prajñayā śrotraṃ samāruhya śrotreṇa sarvāñ chabdān āpnoti | prajñayā jihvāṃ samāruhya jihvayā sarvān rasān āpnoti | prajñayā hastau samāruhya hastābhyāṃ sarvāṇi karmāṇyāpnoti | prajñayā śarīraṃ samāruhya śarīreṇa sukhaduḥkhe āpnoti | prajñayopasthaṃ samāruhyupasthenānandaṃ ratiṃ prajātim āpnoti | prajñayā pādau samāruhya pādābhyāṃ sarvā ityā āpnoti | prajñayā manaḥ samāruhya manasā sarvāṇi dhyātānyāpnoti |
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 5,6 = KU 3,6
By mounting speech through <s>prajñā</s> (consciousness), one obtains all names through speech. By mounting <s>prāṇa</s> through <s>prajñā</s>, one obtains all odors through <s>prāṇa</s>. By mounting the eye through <s>prajñā</s>, one obtains all forms through the eye. By mounting the ear through <s>prajñā</s>, one obtains all sounds through the ear. By mounting the tongue through <s>prajñā</s>, one obtains all tastes through the tongue. By mounting the two hands through <s>prajñā</s>, one obtains all actions through the hands. By mounting the body through <s>prajñā</s>, one obtains pleasure and pain through the body. By mounting the generative organ through <s>prajñā</s>, one obtains bliss, delight, and procreation through the generative organ. By mounting the two feet through <s>prajñā</s>, one obtains all movements through the feet. By mounting the mind through <s>prajñā</s>, one obtains all thoughts through the mind.

children.text:
ŚĀ 5,7 = KU 3,7
na hi prajñāpetā vāṅ nāma kiṃcana prajñāpayet | anyatra me mano 'bhūd ityāha | nāham etan nāma prājñāsiṣam iti | na hi prajñāpetaḥ prāṇo gandhaṃ kaṃcana prajñāpayet | anyatra me mano 'bhūd ityāha | nāham etaṃ gandhaṃ prājñāsiṣam iti | na hi prajñāpetaṃ cakṣū rūpaṃ kiṃcana prajñāpayet | anyatra me mano 'bhūd ityāha | nāham etad rūpaṃ prājñāsiṣam iti | na hi prajñāpetaṃ śrotraṃ śabdaṃ kaṃcana prajñāpayet | anyatra me mano 'bhūd ityāha | nāham etaṃ śabdaṃ prājñāsiṣam iti | na hi prajñāpetā jihvānnarasaṃ kaṃcana prajñāpayet | anyatra me mano 'bhūd ityāha | nāham etam annarasaṃ prājñāsiṣam iti | na hi prajñāpetau hastau karma kiṃcana prajñāpayetām | anyatra nau mano 'bhūd ityāhatuḥ | nāvām etat karma prājñāsiṣveti | na hi prajñāpetaṃ śarīraṃ na sukhaṃ na duḥkhaṃ kiṃcana prajñāpayet | anyatra me mano 'bhūd ityāha | nāham etaṃ na sukhaṃ na duḥkhaṃ prājñāsiṣam iti | na hi prajñāpeta upastha ānandaṃ na ratiṃ na prajātiṃ kāṃcana prajñāpayet | anyatra me mano 'bhūd ityāha | nāham etam ānandaṃ na ratiṃ prajātiṃ prājñāsiṣam iti
| na hi prajñāpetau pādāv ityāṃ kāṃcana prajñāpayet | anyatra nau mano 'bhūd ityāha | nāvām etām ityāṃ prājñāsiṣveti | na hi prajñāpetā dhīḥ kāṃcana sidhyet,na prajñātavyaṃ prajñāyet ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 5,7 = KU 3,7: For without <s>prajñā</s> (intelligence), speech would not make any name known. 'My mind was elsewhere,' one says — 'I did not cognize that name.' For without <s>prajñā</s>, <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) would not make any odor known. 'My mind was elsewhere,' one says — 'I did not cognize that odor.' For without <s>prajñā</s>, the eye would not make any form known. 'My mind was elsewhere,' one says — 'I did not cognize that form.' For without <s>prajñā</s>, the ear would not make any sound known. 'My mind was elsewhere,' one says — 'I did not cognize that sound.' For without <s>prajñā</s>, the tongue would not make any taste of food known. 'My mind was elsewhere,' one says — 'I did not cognize that taste of food.' For without <s>prajñā</s>, the two hands would not make any action known. 'Our mind was elsewhere,' they say — 'We did not cognize that action.' For without <s>prajñā</s>, the body would not make any pleasure or pain known. 'My mind was elsewhere,' one says — 'I did not cognize that pleasure or pain.' For without <s>prajñā</s>, the generative organ would not make any bliss, delight, or procreation known. 'My mind was elsewhere,' one says — 'I did not cognize that bliss, delight, or procreation.' For without <s>prajñā</s>, the two feet would not make any movement known. 'Our mind was elsewhere,' they say — 'We did not cognize that movement.' For without <s>prajñā</s>, no thought would succeed, nothing cognizable would be cognized.

children.text:
ŚĀ 5,8 = KU 3,8
na vācaṃ vijijñāsīti | vaktāraṃ vidyāt | na gandhaṃ vijijñāsīti | ghrātāraṃ vidyāt | na rūpaṃ vijijñāsīti | draṣṭāraṃ vidyāt | na śabdaṃ vijijñāsīti | śrotāraṃ vidyāt | nānnarasaṃ vijijñāsīti | annarasasya vijñātāraṃ vidyāt | na karma vijijñāsīti | kartāraṃ vidyāt | na sukhaduḥkhe vijijñāsīti | sukhaduḥkhayor vistāraṃ vidyāt | nānandaṃ na ratiṃ na prajātiṃ vijijñāsīti | ānandasya rateḥ prajāter vijñātāraṃ vidyāt | netyāṃ vijijñāsīti | etāraṃ vidyāt | na mano vijijñāsīti | mantāraṃ vidyāt | tā vā etā daśaiva bhūtamātrā adhiprajñam | daśa prajñāmātrā adhibhutam | yad dhi bhūtamātrā na syur na prajñāmātrāḥ syuḥ | yad vā prajñāmātrā na syur na bhūtamātrāḥ syuḥ |
na hyanyatarato rūpaṃ kiṃcana sidhyet | no eta nānā | tad yathā rathasyāreṣu nemir arpitaḥ | nābhāvarā arpitāḥ | evam evaitā bhūtāmātrāḥ prajñāmātrāsvarpitāḥ | prajñāmātrāḥ prāṇe 'rpitāḥ | sa eṣa prāṇa eva prajñātmānanto 'jaro 'mṛto na sādhunā karmaṇā bhūyān bhavati np evāsādhunā kanīyān | eṣa hyeva sādhu karma kārayati taṃ yam ebhyo lokebhya unninīṣate | eṣa u evāsādhu karma kārayati taṃ yam adho ninīṣate | eṣa lokapālaḥ | eṣa lokādhipatiḥ | eṣa lokeśaḥ | sa ma ātmeti vidyāt sa ma ātmeti vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 5,8 = KU 3,8: One should not seek to know speech; one should know the speaker. One should not seek to know odor; one should know the smeller. One should not seek to know form; one should know the seer. One should not seek to know sound; one should know the hearer. One should not seek to know the taste of food; one should know the knower of the taste of food. One should not seek to know action; one should know the doer. One should not seek to know pleasure and pain; one should know the knower of pleasure and pain. One should not seek to know bliss, delight, and procreation; one should know the knower of bliss, delight, and procreation. One should not seek to know movement; one should know the mover. One should not seek to know mind; one should know the thinker. These are indeed just ten elemental aspects (<s>bhūtamātrā</s>) with reference to <s>prajñā</s> (intelligence), and ten cognitive aspects (<s>prajñāmātrā</s>) with reference to the elements. For if there were no elemental aspects, there would be no cognitive aspects; and if there were no cognitive aspects, there would be no elemental aspects. For from either alone, no form whatsoever would be realized. And these are not separate. Just as the rim is fixed on the spokes of a wheel, and the spokes are fixed in the hub, so these elemental aspects are fixed in the cognitive aspects, and the cognitive aspects are fixed in <s>prāṇa</s> (breath). This <s>prāṇa</s> indeed is the intelligent self (<s>prajñātman</s>) — blissful, unaging, immortal. He does not become greater by good action, nor lesser by bad action. For it is he who causes him to do good action, whom he wishes to lead upward from these worlds; and it is he who causes him to do bad action, whom he wishes to lead downward. He is the protector of the world, he is the sovereign of the world, he is the lord of the world. 'He is my self' — thus one should know; 'He is my self' — thus one should know.

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,1 = KU 4,1
atha gārgyo bālākir anūcānaḥ saṃspaṣṭa āsa | so 'vasad uśīnareṣu so 'vasan matsyeṣu kurupañcāleṣu kāśivideheṣviti | sa hājātaśatruṃ kāśyam āvrajyovāca - brahma te bravāṇīti | taṃ hovācājataśatruḥ - sahasraṃ dadmi ta ityetasyāṃ vāci | janako janaka iti vā u janā dhāvantīti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,1 = KU 4,1: Now, <s>Gārgya Bālāki</s> was a learned man, widely known. He dwelt among the <s>Uśīnaras</s>, among the <s>Matsyas</s>, among the <s>Kuru-Pañcālas</s>, among the <s>Kāśi-Videhas</s>. He came to <s>Ajātaśatru</s> of <s>Kāśī</s> and said: 'Let me declare <s>Brahman</s> to you.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'I give you a thousand [cows] for this teaching.' At such words, people will come running, saying '<s>Janaka</s>! <s>Janaka</s>!'

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,2 = KU 4,2
āditye bṛhat, candramasyannam, vidyuti satyam, stanayitnau śabdaḥ, vāyāvindro vaikuṇṭhaḥ, ākāśe pūrṇam, agnau viṣāsahiḥ, apsu tejaḥ | ityadhidaivatam | atādhyātmam - ādarśe pratirūpaḥ, chāyāyāṃ dvitīyaḥ, pratiśrutkāyām asuriti, śabde mṛtyuḥ, svapne yamaḥ, śarīre prajāpatiḥ, dakṣiṇe' kṣiṇi vācaḥ, savye 'kṣiṇi satyasya ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,2 = KU 4,2: In the sun, the Great (<s>Bṛhat</s>); in the moon, Food; in lightning, Truth; in thunder, Sound; in wind, <s>Indra Vaikuṇṭha</s> (the Invincible); in space, the Full; in fire, the Vanquisher; in water, Radiance (<s>Tejas</s>). Thus with reference to the divinities (<s>adhidaivatam</s>). Now with reference to the self (<s>adhyātmam</s>): in the mirror, the Counter-image; in the shadow, the Second; in the echo, Life (<s>asu</s>); in sound, Death; in dream, <s>Yama</s>; in the body, <s>Prajāpati</s>; in the right eye, Speech; in the left eye, Truth.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,3 = KU 4,3
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣa āditye puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | bṛhan pāṇḍaravāsā atiṣṭhāḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ Mūrdheti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste 'tiṣṭhāḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ mūrdhā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,3 = KU 4,3: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> (person) who is in the sun — him indeed I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in dialogue about this one. I worship him as the Great (<s>Bṛhat</s>), the one clad in white garments, the supreme, the head of all beings.' He who worships him thus becomes supreme, the head of all beings.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,4 = KU 4,4
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣa candramasi puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | annasyātmeti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste 'nnasyātmā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,4 = KU 4,4: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> who is in the moon — him indeed I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in dialogue about this one. I worship him as the self of Food (<s>Anna</s>).' He who worships him thus becomes the self of food.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,5 = KU 4,5
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣa vidyuti puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | satyasyātmeti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste satyasyātmā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,5 = KU 4,5: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> who is in lightning — him indeed I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in dialogue about this one. I worship him as the self of Truth (<s>Satya</s>).' He who worships him thus becomes the self of truth.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,6 = KU 4,6
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣa stanayitnau puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | śabdasyātmeti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste śabdasyātmā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,6 = KU 4,6: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> who is in thunder — him indeed I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in dialogue about this one. I worship him as the self of Sound (<s>Śabda</s>).' He who worships him thus becomes the self of sound.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,7 = KU 4,7
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣa vāyau puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | indro vaikuṇṭho 'parājitā seneti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste jiṣṇur ha vā aparājiṣṇur anyatastyajāyī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,7 = KU 4,7: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> who is in wind — him indeed I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in dialogue about this one. I worship him as <s>Indra Vaikuṇṭha</s>, the unconquered army.' He who worships him thus becomes victorious, unconquerable, a conqueror of adversaries.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,8 = KU 4,8
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣa ākāśe puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | pūṛnam apravarti brahmeti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste pūryate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,8 = KU 4,8: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> who is in space — him indeed I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in dialogue about this one. I worship him as the Full (<s>Pūrṇa</s>), the non-receding <s>Brahman</s>.' He who worships him thus is filled with offspring, cattle, fame, the splendor of sacred knowledge (<s>brahmavarcasa</s>), and the heavenly world; he lives a full life.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,9 = KU 4,9
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣo 'gnau puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | viṣāsahir iti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste viṣāsahir haivānyeṣu bhavati ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,9 = KU 4,9: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> who is in fire — him indeed I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in dialogue about this one. I worship him as the Vanquisher (<s>Viṣāsahi</s>).' He who worships him thus becomes a vanquisher among others.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,10 = KU 4,10
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣo 'psu puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | tejasa ātmeti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste tejasa ātmā bhavati | ityadhidaivatam | athādhyātmam ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,10 = KU 4,10: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> who is in water — him indeed I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in dialogue about this one. I worship him as the self of Radiance (<s>Tejas</s>).' He who worships him thus becomes the self of radiance. Thus with reference to the divinities (<s>adhidaivatam</s>). Now with reference to the self (<s>adhyātmam</s>).

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,11 = KU 4,11
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣa ādarśe puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | pratirūpa iti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste pratirūpo haivāsya prajāyām ājāyate nāpratirūpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,11 = KU 4,11: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> who is in the mirror — him indeed I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in dialogue about this one. I worship him as the Counter-image (<s>Pratirūpa</s>).' He who worships him thus — in his progeny is born one who is like him, not one who is unlike him.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,12 = KU 4,12
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣa cchāyāyāṃ puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | dvitīyo 'napaga iti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste vindate dvitīyāt | dvitīyavān bhavati ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,12 = KU 4,12: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> who is in the shadow — him indeed I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in dialogue about this one. I worship him as the Second, the inseparable companion.' He who worships him thus obtains from a companion; he becomes one who has a companion.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,13 = KU 4,13
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣa pratiśrutkāyāṃ puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | asur iti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste na purā kālāt saṃmoham eti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,13 = KU 4,13: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> who is in the echo — him indeed I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in dialogue about this one. I worship him as Life (<s>Asu</s>).' He who worships him thus does not fall into a swoon before his time.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,14 = KU 4,14
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣa śabde puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | mṛtyur iti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste na purā kālāt praiti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,14 = KU 4,14: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> (person) who is in sound — him I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in a dialogue about this. I worship him as Death.' He who worships him thus does not depart before his time.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,15 = KU 4,15
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - yenaitat puruṣaḥ suptaḥ svapnayā carati tamu evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | yamo rājeti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste sarvaṃ hāsmā idaṃ śraiṣṭhyāya yamyate ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,15 = KU 4,15: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'That by which a person who is asleep moves about in dream — him I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in a dialogue about this. I worship him as King <s>Yama</s>.' He who worships him thus — all this is subdued for his preeminence.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,16 = KU 4,16
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣa śarīre puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | prajāpatir iti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste prajāyate prajayā paśbhir yaśasā brahmavaracasema svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,16 = KU 4,16: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> (person) who is in the body — him I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in a dialogue about this. I worship him as <s>Prajāpati</s>.' He who worships him thus is born with offspring, cattle, fame, the luster of sacred knowledge, and the heavenly world; he lives out his full life.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,17 = KU 4,17
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣa dakṣiṇe 'kṣiṇi puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | vāca ātmāgner ātmā jyotiṣa ātmeti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste eteṣāṃ sarveṣām ātmā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,17 = KU 4,17: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> (person) who is in the right eye — him I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in a dialogue about this. I worship him as the self of speech, the self of fire, the self of light.' He who worships him thus becomes the self of all these.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,18 = KU 4,18
sa hovāca bālākiḥ - ya evaiṣa savye 'kṣiṇi puruṣas tam evāham upāsa iti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mā maitasmin saṃvādayiṣṭhāḥ | satyasyātm vidyuta ātmā tejasa ātmeti vā aham etam upāsa iti | sa yo haitam evam upāste eteṣāṃ sarveṣām ātmā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,18 = KU 4,18: <s>Bālāki</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> (person) who is in the left eye — him I worship.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Do not engage me in a dialogue about this. I worship him as the self of truth, the self of lightning, the self of splendor.' He who worships him thus becomes the self of all these.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,19 = KU 4,19
tata u ha bālākis tūṣṇīm āsa | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - etāvān nu bālākā3 iti | etāvad iti hovāca bālākiḥ | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - mṛṣā vai khalu mā saṃvādayiṣṭhā brahma te bravāṇīti | sa hovāca - yo vai bālāka eteṣāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ kartā yasya vaitat karma sa vai veditavya iti | tata u ha bālākiḥ samitpāṇiḥ praticakrama upāyānīti | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - pratilomarūpam eva tan manye yat kṣatriyo brāhmaṇam upanayeta | ehi vyeva tvā jñapayiṣyāmīti | taṃ ha pāṇāvabhipadya pravavrāja | tau ha suptaṃ puruṣam ājagmatuḥ | taṃ hājātaśatrur āmantrayāñcakre - bṛhan pāṇḍaravāsaḥ soma rājann iti | sa u ha śiśya eva | tat u hainaṃ yaṣṭyā vicikṣepa | sa tata eva samuttasthau | taṃ hovācājātaśatruḥ - kvaiṣa etad bālāke puruṣo 'śayiṣṭa, yatraitad abhūt, yata etad āgād iti | hitā nama puruṣasya nāḍyo hṛdayāt purītatam abhipratanvanti tad yathā sahasradhā keśo vipāṭitastvāvad aṇvyaḥ |
piṅgalasyāṇimnyas tiṣṭhanti śuklasya kṛṣṇasya pītasya lohitasya ca | tāsu tadā bhavati yadā suptaḥ svapnaṃ na kaṃcana paśyati ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,19 = KU 4,19: Thereupon <s>Bālāki</s> fell silent. <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Is that all, <s>Bālāki</s>?' 'That is all,' said <s>Bālāki</s>. <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'You have engaged me in a dialogue in vain. Let me tell you about <s>Brahman</s>.' He said: 'He, O <s>Bālāki</s>, who is the maker of these <s>puruṣas</s> (persons), whose work all this is — he alone is to be known.' Thereupon <s>Bālāki</s>, fuel in hand, came forward [saying]: 'Let me come to you as a student.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'I consider it contrary to the natural order that a <s>kṣatriya</s> should initiate a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. Come, I shall make you understand.' Taking him by the hand, he went forth. They came upon a person who was asleep. <s>Ajātaśatru</s> addressed him: 'O great one, clad in white, O King <s>Soma</s>!' But he simply lay there. Then he pushed him with a stick, and he rose up. <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to him: 'Where, O <s>Bālāki</s>, did this person lie? Where was he? Whence did he come back?' The <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) of a person called <s>hitā</s> extend from the heart to the <s>purītat</s> (pericardium), as fine as a hair split a thousandfold. They stand filled with a fine [fluid] — tawny, white, dark, yellow, and red. In these [channels] he remains when, being asleep, he sees no dream.

children.text:
ŚĀ 6,20 = KU 4,20
athāsmin prāṇa ekaikadhā bhavati | tad enaṃ vāk sarvair nāmabhiḥ sahāpyeti | cakṣuḥ sarvai rūpaiḥ sahāpyeti | śrotraṃ sarvaiḥ śabdaiḥ sahāpyeti | manaḥ sarvair dhyātaiḥ sahāpyeti | sa yadA pratibudhyate, yathāgner jvalataḥ sarvā diśo visphuliṅgā vipratiṣṭheran evam evaitasmād ātmanaḥ prāṇā yathāyatanaṃ vipratiṣṭhante prāṇebhyo devāḥ devebhyo lokāḥ | sa eṣa prāṇa eva prajñātmedaṃ śarīram AtmAnam anupraviṣṭa ā lomabhya ā nakhebhyaḥ | tad yathā kṣuraḥ kṣuradhāne vopahito viśvaṃbharo vā viśvaṃbarakulāya evam evaiṣa prajñātmedaṃ śarīram ātmānam anupraviṣṭa ā lomabhya ā nakhebhyaḥ | tam etam ātmānam eta ātmāno 'nvavasyante yathā śreṣṭhinaṃ svāḥ | tad yatha śreṣṭhī svair bhuṅkte yathā vā svāḥ śreṣṭhinaṃ bhuñjanti | evam evaiṣa prajñātmaitair ātmabhir bhuṅkte | evam evaita ātmāna etam ātmānaṃ bhuñjanti | sa yāvad dha vā indra etam ātmānaṃ na vijajñe tāvad enam asurā abhibabhūvuḥ | sa yadā vijajñe 'tha hatvāsurān vijitya sarveṣāṃ ca devānāṃ śraiṣṭhyaṃ svārājyam ādhipatyaṃ paryait |
tathau evaivaṃ vidvān sarvān pāpmano 'pahaty sarveṣāṃ ca bhūtānām śraiṣṭhyaṃ svārājya ādhipatyaṃ paryeti | ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 6,20 = KU 4,20: Then in this <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) alone he becomes unified. Speech, together with all names, enters into it; sight, together with all forms, enters into it; hearing, together with all sounds, enters into it; mind, together with all thoughts, enters into it. When he awakens, just as from a blazing fire sparks fly forth in all directions, so from this <s>ātman</s> (self) the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) go forth to their respective stations; from the <s>prāṇas</s>, the gods; from the gods, the worlds. This <s>prāṇa</s> that is conscious intelligence (<s>prajñātman</s>) has entered this body, this self, down to the hairs, down to the nails. Just as a razor is placed in a razor-case, or as the all-sustainer is [placed] in the all-sustaining household, so this conscious self (<s>prajñātman</s>) has entered this body, this self, down to the hairs, down to the nails. On this self, these [other] selves depend, as dependents on a chief. Just as a chief enjoys [the labor] of his dependents, or dependents enjoy [the protection] of a chief, so this conscious self enjoys through these selves, and these selves enjoy through this self. As long as <s>Indra</s> did not know this self, so long the <s>Asuras</s> overpowered him. When he knew it, then having slain the <s>Asuras</s>, he attained the preeminence, self-sovereignty, and overlordship of all the gods. Likewise, one who knows thus wards off all evils and attains the preeminence, self-sovereignty, and overlordship of all beings — he who knows thus, he who knows thus.

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,1
om ṛtaṃ vadiṣyāmi | satyaṃ vadiṣyāmi | tan mām avatu tad vaktāram avatvavatu mām avatu vaktāram | mayi bhargo mayi mahaḥ | vāṅ me manasi pratiṣṭhitā | mano me vāci pratiṣṭhitam | āvir āvir mayyābhūḥ | vedasya ma āṇīḥ | ṛta mā mā hiṃsīḥ | anenādhītenāhorātrān tsaṃvasāmi | agne iḷā nama iḷā namaḥ | ṛṣibhyo mantrakṛdbhyo mantrapatibhyo namo 'stu devebhyaḥ | śivā naḥ śaṭamā bhava sumṛḍīkā sarasvati mā te vyoma saṃdṛśi | adabdhaṃ mana iṣiraṃ cakṣuḥ sūryo jyotiṣāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ | dīkṣe mā mā hiṃsīḥ ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,1: <s>Oṃ</s>. I shall speak what is right. I shall speak what is true. May that protect me; may it protect the speaker; may it protect me, may it protect the speaker. May radiance be in me; may greatness be in me. My speech is established in my mind; my mind is established in my speech. Reveal yourself, reveal yourself to me! Be the pin of the <s>Veda</s> for me. O <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), do not forsake me! With this study, I dwell day and night. O <s>Agni</s>, <s>Iḷā</s> — homage, homage to <s>Iḷā</s>! Homage to the <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers), the makers of mantras, the lords of mantras! Homage to the gods! Be auspicious to us, O <s>Śatamā</s>; be gracious, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>; may your expanse not be [merely] seen. The undefeated mind, the keen sight — <s>Sūrya</s> is the best of lights. O <s>Dīkṣā</s> (consecration), do not forsake me!

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,2
athātaḥ saṃhitāyā upaniṣat | pṛthivī pūrvarūpaṃ dyaur uttararūpaṃ vāyuḥ saṃhiteti śauravīro māṇḍūkeyaḥ | ākāśaḥ saṃhitetyasya māṇḍavyo vedayāñ cakre - sa hāviparihṛto mene na me 'sya putreṇa samagād iti | parihṛto mena ity āgastyaḥ | samānaṃ hyatra pituśca putrasya ca vāyuś cākāśaś ca | ityadhidaivatam | athādhyātmam | vāk pūrvarūpaṃ mana uttararūpaṃ prāṇaḥ saṃhiteti śauravīro māṇḍūkeyaḥ | atha ha smāsya putra āha dīrghaḥ - manasā vā agre kīrtayati tad vācā vadati | tasmān mana eva pūrvarūpaṃ vāg uttararūpaṃ mano vāk prāṇas tveva saṃhiteti | sa eṣo 'śvarathaḥ praṣṭivāhano manovākprāṇasaṃhitaḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ gamayati | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur etīti nu māṇḍūkeyānām ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,2: Now, the secret teaching (<s>upaniṣad</s>) of the <s>saṃhitā</s> (combination). Earth is the prior form; heaven is the latter form; wind is the combination — [thus taught] <s>Śauravīra Māṇḍūkeya</s>. 'Space is the combination' — thus <s>Māṇḍavya</s> taught his son. He considered himself unrefuted, [thinking]: 'My son has not equaled me in this.' 'He was refuted' — [says] <s>Āgastya</s>. For here the father's and the son's [teaching] are the same — both wind and space [serve as combination]. This is with reference to the deities. Now with reference to the self: speech is the prior form; mind is the latter form; <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) is the combination — [thus taught] <s>Śauravīra Māṇḍūkeya</s>. Then his son <s>Dīrgha</s> said: 'With the mind one first conceives, then speaks with speech. Therefore mind is the prior form, speech the latter form; but <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) alone is indeed the combination.' This is the chariot with the horse and driver, the combination of mind, speech, and breath that conveys one to the heavenly world. He who knows this <s>saṃhitā</s> thus is joined with offspring, cattle, fame, the luster of sacred knowledge, the heavenly world, and lives a full life — thus according to the <s>Māṇḍūkeyas</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,3
śākalyasya pṛthivyagniḥ pṛthivī vāg anuvyāhārāḥ | sa yadi nirbhujaḥ khalu vai vayaṃ madhyamo vāk prāṇena mātā jāyā prajñā vāg bṛhadgatirvālisarvamuttamam ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,3: According to <s>Śākalya</s>: earth and fire — earth is speech, the secondary utterances. If indeed we are without arms [powerless], the middle one is speech with breath, the mother, the wife; <s>prajñā</s> (intelligence) is speech, the great-going, powerful — all that is the highest.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,4
atha śākalyasya | pṛthivī pūrvarūpaṃ dyaur uttararūpaṃ vāyuḥ saṃhitā vṛṣṭiḥ saṃdhiḥ saṃdhātā | tad utāpi yatraitad balavad anugṛhṇan mahāmegho vṛṣṭiṃ varṣati | dyāvāpṛthivyau samadhātām ityadhidaivatam | athādhyātmam | puruṣo 'yaṃ sarvam āṇḍam | dve vidale bhavataḥ | tatredam eva pūrvarūpam idam uttararūpam | tatrāyam antareṇākāśaḥ | yathāsau dyāvāpṛthivyor antareṇākāśa etasminn ākāśe prāṇa āyatto bhavati yathāmuṣminn ākāśe vāyur āyatto bhavati | yathāmūni trīṇi jyotīṃṣyevam imāni puruṣe trīṇi jyotīṃṣi | yathāsau divyāditya evam idaṃ śirasi cakṣuḥ | yathāsāvantarikṣe vidyud evam idam ātmani hṛdayam | yathāyam agniḥ pṛthivyam evam idam upasthe retaḥ | evamiva ha sma sarvata ātmānam anuvidhāyāha - idam eva pūrvarūpam idam uttararūpaṃ mano vāk prāṇas tveva saṃhiteti | sa eṣo ' śvarathaḥ praṣṭivahano manovākprāṇasaṃhitaḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ gamayati | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ +veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena
sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,4: Now, according to <s>Śākalya</s>: earth is the prior form; heaven is the latter form; wind is the combination; rain is the juncture; [wind] is the joiner. Moreover, when a powerful great cloud pours forth rain, holding [it] fast — heaven and earth are joined together. This is with reference to the deities. Now with reference to the self: this person is the entire egg. It has two halves. Here this [lower half] is the prior form, that [upper half] is the latter form. In between is this space. Just as in the space between heaven and earth, <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) is sustained in this space, just as wind is sustained in that [cosmic] space. Just as those three luminaries [exist in the cosmos], so these three luminaries [exist] in a person. Just as yonder divine sun, so is sight here in the head. Just as lightning in the atmosphere, so is the heart here in the self. Just as fire on earth, so is semen here in the lap. Thus, having traced the self in every way, he said: 'This is the prior form, that is the latter form; mind and speech [are the halves], but <s>prāṇa</s> alone is the combination.' This is the chariot with the horse and driver, the combination of mind, speech, and breath that conveys one to the heavenly world. He who knows this <s>saṃhitā</s> thus is joined with offspring, cattle, fame, the luster of sacred knowledge, the heavenly world, and lives a full life.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,5
pṛthivī pūrvarūpaṃ dyaur uttararūpaṃ vāyuḥ saṃhitā diśaḥ saṃdhir ādityaḥ saṃdhāteti vaiśvāmitraḥ | ityadhidaivatam | athādhyātmam | vāk pūrvarūpaṃ mana uttararūpaṃ prāṇaḥ saṃhitā śrotraṃ saṃdhiś cakṣuḥ saṃdhātā | sa ya evam etāṃ etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,5: Earth is the prior form, heaven the latter form, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) the conjunction (<s>saṃhitā</s>), the directions the joint (<s>saṃdhi</s>), <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) the joiner (<s>saṃdhātṛ</s>) — thus [teaches] <s>Vaiśvāmitra</s>. This is concerning the deities (<s>adhidaivatam</s>). Now concerning the self (<s>adhyātmam</s>): Speech is the prior form, mind the latter form, <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) the conjunction, hearing the joint, sight the joiner. He who knows this conjunction in this way is joined with offspring, cattle, glory, the splendor of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmavarcas</s>), and the heavenly world, and lives his full lifespan.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,6
agniḥ pūrvarūpaṃ candramā uttararūpaṃ vidyut saṃhiteti sūryadattaḥ | ityadhidaivatam | athādhyātmam - vāk pūrvarūpaṃ mana uttararūpaṃ satyaṃ saṃhitā | sa ya evam etāṃ etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,6: <s>Agni</s> (fire) is the prior form, the moon (<s>Candramā</s>) the latter form, lightning the conjunction — thus [teaches] <s>Sūryadatta</s>. This is concerning the deities. Now concerning the self: Speech is the prior form, mind the latter form, truth (<s>satya</s>) the conjunction. He who knows this conjunction in this way is joined with offspring, cattle, glory, the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>, and the heavenly world, and lives his full lifespan.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,7
pṛthivī pūrvarūpaṃ dyaur uttararūpaṃ kālaḥ saṃhiteti rādheyaḥ | ityadhidaivatam | athādhyātmam - vāk pūrvarūpaṃ mana uttararūpaṃ ātmā saṃhitā | sa ya evam etāṃ etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,7: Earth is the prior form, heaven the latter form, time (<s>kāla</s>) the conjunction — thus [teaches] <s>Rādheya</s>. This is concerning the deities. Now concerning the self: Speech is the prior form, mind the latter form, the <s>ātman</s> (self) the conjunction. He who knows this conjunction in this way is joined with offspring, cattle, glory, the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>, and the heavenly world, and lives his full lifespan.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,8
vāk pūrvarūpaṃ mana uttararūpaṃ vidyā saṃhiteti pauṣkarasādiḥ | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,8: Speech is the prior form, mind the latter form, knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) the conjunction — thus [teaches] <s>Pauṣkarasādi</s>. He who knows this conjunction in this way is joined with offspring, cattle, glory, the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>, and the heavenly world, and lives his full lifespan.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,9
athāto 'nuvyāhārāḥ | prāṇo vaṃśa iti vidyāt | sa ya enaṃ prāṇaṃ vaṃśaṃ bruvan param upavadet śaknuvan kaścic cen manyeta - prāṇaṃ vaṃśaṃ +samadhām | prāṇaṃ vaṃśaṃ saṃdhitsituṃ na śaknoṣītyāttha | prāṇas tvā vaṃśo hāsyatītyevainaṃ brūyāt | atha ced aśaknuvan manyeta prāṇaṃ vaṃśaṃ samadhitsīḥ taṃ nāśakaḥ saṃdhātuṃ prāṇas tvā vaṃśo hāsyatītyevainaṃ brūyāt | yathā nu kathā ca bruvan vābruvan vā brūyād abhyāśam eva yat tat tathā syāt | na tvevānyat kuśalād brāhmaṇaṃ brūyād atidyumna eva brāhmaṇaṃ brūyān nātidyumne ca na brāhmaṇaṃ brūyān namo 'stu brāhmaṇebhya iti śauravīro māṇḍūkeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,9: Now, the counter-utterances (<s>anuvyāhāras</s>). One should know that <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) is the <s>vaṃśa</s> (lineage recitation). If someone, while reciting the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>vaṃśa</s>, should challenge another and think himself capable — 'I have mastered the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>vaṃśa</s>' — [the other] should say to him: 'You say you are unable to join the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>vaṃśa</s>; the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>vaṃśa</s> will abandon you.' And if he thinks [the challenger] incapable: 'You attempted to master the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>vaṃśa</s> but were unable to join it; the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>vaṃśa</s> will abandon you' — thus he should say to him. However the discussion goes, whether one speaks or does not speak, whatever is said should be near [the truth]. But one should not speak a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (sacred teaching) to anyone other than a skilled person. One should speak a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> only to one of surpassing brilliance (<s>atidyumna</s>), and to one who is not of surpassing brilliance one should not speak a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. 'Homage to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>!' — thus [says] <s>Śauravīra Māṇḍūkeya</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,10
sa yadi prāṇaṃ vaṃśaṃ bruvantaṃ param upavadet śaknuvantaṃ cen manyeta - prāṇaṃ vaṃśaṃ samadhitsiṣam prāṇaṃ vaṃśaṃ saṃdhitsituṃ na śaknoṣītyāttha | prāṇas tvā vaṃśo hāsyatītyevainaṃ brūyāt | atha ced aśaknuvantaṃ manyeta - prāṇaṃ vaṃśaṃ samadhitsīs tan nāśakaḥ saṃdhātum | prāṇas tvā vaṃśo hāsyatītyevainaṃ brūyāt | yathā nu kathā ca bruvantaṃ vābruvantaṃ vā brūyād abhyāśam eva yat tat tathā syāt | na tvevānyat kuśalād brāhmaṇaṃ brūyād atidyumna eva brāhmaṇaṃ brūyān nātidyumne ca na brāhmaṇaṃ brūyān namo 'stu brāhmaṇebhya iti śauravīro māṇḍūkeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,10: If someone, while reciting the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>vaṃśa</s>, should challenge another and think himself capable — 'I attempted to master the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>vaṃśa</s>, yet you say I am unable to join the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>vaṃśa</s>; the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>vaṃśa</s> will abandon you' — thus he should say to him. And if he thinks [the challenger] incapable — 'You attempted to master the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>vaṃśa</s> but were unable to join it; the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>vaṃśa</s> will abandon you' — thus he should say to him. However the discussion goes, whether one speaks or does not speak, whatever is said should be near [the truth].

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,11
athāto nirbhujapravādāḥ | pṛthivyāyatanaṃ nirbhujaṃ divāyatanaṃ pratṛṇṇam antartikṣāyatanam ubhayam antareṇa | sa ya enaṃ nirbhujaṃ bruvan param upavadet | pṛthivīṃ devatām āraḥ pṛthivī tvā devatāriṣyatītyenaṃ brūyāt | atha yadi pratṛṇṇam bruvan param upavaded divaṃ devatām āro dyaus tvā devatāriṣyatītyenaṃ brūyāt | atha yadyubhayam antareṇa bruvan param upavaded antarikṣaṃ devatām āra antarikṣaṃ tvā devatāriṣyatītiyenaṃ brūyāt | yad dhi saṃdhiṃ vivartayati tan nirbhujasya rūpam | atha yac chuddhe akṣare abhivyāharati tat pratṛṇṇasyāgra u eva | ubhayam antareṇobhayaṃ vyāptaṃ bhavati | annādyakāmo nirbhujaṃ brūyāt svargakāṃaḥ pratṛṇṇam ubhayakāma ubhayamantareṇa | sa ya enaṃ nirbhujaṃ bruvan param upavaded acyoṣṭhā avarābhyāṃ sthānābhyām ityenaṃ brūyāt | atha yadi pratṛṇṇam bruvan param upavaded acyoṣṭhā uttarābhyāṃ sthānābhyām ityevainaṃ brūyāt | yastvevobhayam antareṇāha tasya tasya nāstyupavādaḥ | yathā nu kathā ca bruvan vābruvan vā brūyād abhyāśam kuśalād brāhmaṇaṃ brūyād atidyumna evaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ brūyān nātidyumne ca na brāhmaṇaṃ brūyāt | namo 'stu brāhmaṇebhya iti śauravīro māṇḍūkeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,11: Now, the <s>nirbhuja</s> (bent-arm) discussions. That which has the earth as its abode is <s>nirbhuja</s> (downward-bent); that which has heaven as its abode is <s>pratṛṇṇa</s> (upward-extended); that which has the atmosphere as its abode is both, being between the two. If someone, while reciting the <s>nirbhuja</s>, should challenge another — [the other should say:] 'You have reached the earth as deity; the earth as deity will destroy you.' And if [he is] reciting the <s>pratṛṇṇa</s> and challenges another — 'You have reached heaven as deity; heaven as deity will destroy you.'

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,12
atha khalvāhur nirbhujavaktrāḥ | pūrvam evākṣaraṃ pūrvarūpam uttaram uttararūpam | yakāravakārāvantareṇa sā saṃhiteti | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,12: Now then, the <s>nirbhuja</s>-speakers say: The prior syllable is the prior form, the latter syllable the latter form. The letters <s>ya</s> and <s>va</s> between them — that is the conjunction (<s>saṃhitā</s>). He who knows this conjunction in this way is joined with offspring, cattle, glory, the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>, and the heavenly world, and lives his full lifespan.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,13
atha vai vayaṃ brūmo nirbhujavaktrāḥ sma iti ha smāha hvastro māṇḍūkeyaḥ | pūrvam evākṣaraṃ pūrvarūpam uttaram uttararūpam | tad yāsau mātrā pūrvarūpottarūpe antareṇa yena saṃdhiṃ vivartayati yena mātrāmātraṃ vibhajati yena svarāt svaraṃ vijñāpayati sā saṃhiteti | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,13: 'But we say that we are the <s>nirbhuja</s>-speakers' — thus used to say <s>Hvastra Māṇḍūkeya</s>. The prior syllable is the prior form, the latter syllable the latter form. That <s>mātrā</s> (phonetic measure) between the prior and latter forms, by which one turns the junction, by which one divides syllable from syllable, by which one distinguishes vowel from vowel — that is the conjunction. He who knows this conjunction in this way is joined with offspring, cattle, glory, the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>, and the heavenly world, and lives his full lifespan.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,14
atha ha smāsya putra āha madhyamaḥ prātiyodhīputro magadhavāsī pūrvam evākṣaraṃ pūrvarūpam uttaram uttararūpam | tad yāsau mātrā saṃdhivijñāpanī sāma tad bhavati sāmaihāvaṃ saṃhitāṃ manya iti | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam - mā naḥ stenebhyo ye abhi druhas pade nirāmiṇo ripavo 'nneṣu jāgṛdhuḥ | ā devānām ohate vi vrayo hṛdi bṛhaspate na paraḥ sāmno viduḥ || iti | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,14: Then his middle son, <s>Prātiyodhīputra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, said: The prior syllable is the prior form, the latter syllable the latter form. That <s>mātrā</s> (phonetic measure) which makes the junction known — that becomes <s>Sāman</s> (chant). 'Thus I consider this conjunction to be <s>Sāman</s>.' This is declared by the <s>Ṛc</s> verse: 'May they not [harm] us — the thieves who lie in wait with hostile intent, the sleepless plunderers watching over our food. May the...'

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,15
vāk prāṇena saṃdhīyata iti kauṇṭharavyaḥ | prāṇaḥ pavamānena pavamāno viśvair devair viśve devāḥ svargeṇa lokena svargo loko brahmaṇā saiṣāvaraparā saṃhitā | sa ya evam etām avaraparāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda evaṃ haiva sa prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena saṃdhīyate yathaiṣāvaraparā saṃhitā | sa yadi pareṇa vopasṛṣṭaḥ svena vārthenābhivyāhared abhivyāharann eva vidyāt - divaṃ saṃhitāgamad viduṣo devān abhivyāhārārtham evaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | etenāvarapareṇa tathā haiva tad bhavati ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,15: Speech is conjoined with <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) — thus [teaches] <s>Kauṇṭharavya</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> with <s>Pavamāna</s> (the purifying [Soma]); <s>Pavamāna</s> with all the gods (<s>Viśve Devāḥ</s>); all the gods with the heavenly world; the heavenly world with <s>Brahman</s>. This is the successive conjunction (<s>avaraparā saṃhitā</s>). He who knows this successive conjunction is thus joined with offspring, cattle, glory, the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>, and the heavenly world, just as this successive [chain extends].

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,16
mātā pūrvarūpaṃ pitottararūpaṃ prajā saṃhiteti bhārgavaḥ | tad etad ekam eva sarvaṃ abhyanūktam | mātā ca hyevedaṃ pitā ca prajā ca sarvam | saiṣāditisaṃhitā | aditir hevedaṃ sarvaṃ yad idaṃ kiṃcid viśvabhūtam | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam - aditir dyaur aditir antarikṣaṃ aditir mātā sā pitā sa putraḥ | viśve devā aditiḥ pañca janā aditir jātam aditir janitvam || sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,16: The mother is the prior form, the father the latter form, offspring the conjunction — thus [teaches] <s>Bhārgava</s>. With this, all this has been declared. For the mother, the father, and offspring are indeed everything. This is the <s>Aditi</s>-conjunction. For <s>Aditi</s> is indeed all this, whatever exists, all that has come into being. This is declared by the <s>Ṛc</s> verse: '<s>Aditi</s> is heaven, <s>Aditi</s> is the atmosphere, <s>Aditi</s> is the mother, she is the father, she is the son...'

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,17
jāyā pūrvarūpaṃ patir uttararūpaṃ putraḥ saṃhitā retaḥ saṃdhiḥ prajananaṃ saṃdhānam iti sthaviraḥ śākalyaḥ | saiṣā prajāpatisaṃhitā | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,17: The wife is the prior form, the husband the latter form, the son the conjunction, semen (<s>retas</s>) the joint, procreation (<s>prajanana</s>) the joining — thus [teaches] <s>Sthavira Śākalya</s>. This is the <s>Prajāpati</s>-conjunction. He who knows this conjunction in this way is joined with offspring, cattle, glory, the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>, and the heavenly world, and lives his full lifespan.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,18
prajñā pūrvarūpaṃ śraddhottararūpaṃ karma saṃhitā satyaṃ saṃdhānam iti kāśyapaḥ | saiṣā satyasaṃhitā | tad āhur yat satyasaṃdhā devā iti | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 7,18: Wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is the prior form, faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) the latter form, ritual action (<s>karma</s>) the conjunction, truth (<s>satya</s>) the joining — thus [teaches] <s>Kāśyapa</s>. This is the Truth-conjunction (<s>satya-saṃhitā</s>). Therefore they say: 'The gods are truth-conjoined (<s>satya-saṃdhā</s>).' He who knows this conjunction in this way is joined with offspring, cattle, glory, the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>, and the heavenly world, and lives his full lifespan.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,19
vāk saṃhiteti pañcālacaṇḍaḥ | vācā vai vedāḥ saṃdhīyante vācā chandāṃsi vācā mitrāṇi saṃdadhati | tad yatraitad adhīte vā bhāṣate vā vāci tadā prāṇo bhavati | vāk tadā prāṇaṃ reḷhi | atha yat svapiti vā tūṣṇīṃ vā bhavati prāṇe tadā vāg bhavati prāṇastadā vācaṃ reḷhi. tāv anyonyaṃ rīḷhaḥ | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam - ekaḥ suparṇaḥ sa samudram āviveśa, sa idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ vicaṣṭe | taṃ pākena manasāpaśyam antitas, taṃ mātā reḷhi sa u reḷhi mātaram || iti | vāg vai mātā prāṇo vatsaḥ | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 7,19
'Speech is the <s>saṃhitā</s> (conjunction)' — so said <s>Pañcālacaṇḍa</s>. By speech indeed the <s>Vedas</s> are joined together, by speech the meters, by speech friendships are formed. When one studies or speaks, <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) then rests in speech; speech then nourishes <s>prāṇa</s>. But when one sleeps or is silent, speech then rests in <s>prāṇa</s>; <s>prāṇa</s> then nourishes speech. These two nourish each other. This has been expressed by the <s>Ṛc</s> verse: 'One beautiful-winged bird entered the ocean; he surveys this entire world. With simple mind I saw him nearby — the mother nourishes him and he nourishes the mother.' Speech is indeed the mother, <s>prāṇa</s> is the calf. He who knows this <s>saṃhitā</s> thus is joined with offspring, cattle, glory, sacred splendor, and the heavenly world, and lives his full life.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,20
bṛhadrathaṃtareṇa rūpeṇa saṃhitā saṃdhīyata iti tārkṣyaḥ | vāg vai rathaṃtarasya rūpaṃ prāṇo bṛhataḥ | ubhābhyām u khalu saṃhitā saṃdhīyate vācā ca prāṇena ca | etasyāṃ ha smopaniṣadi saṃvatsaraṃ gā rakṣayata iti tārkṣyaḥ | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 7,20
'The <s>saṃhitā</s> is joined through the form of <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>' — so said <s>Tārkṣya</s>. Speech is indeed the form of <s>Rathantara</s>, <s>prāṇa</s> the form of <s>Bṛhat</s>. Through both indeed the <s>saṃhitā</s> is joined — through speech and <s>prāṇa</s>. 'In this <s>Upaniṣad</s> one should tend cows for a year' — so said <s>Tārkṣya</s>. He who knows this <s>saṃhitā</s> thus is joined with offspring, cattle, glory, sacred splendor, and the heavenly world, and lives his full life.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,21
gatiḥ pūrvvarūpaṃ nivṛttir uttararūpaṃ sthitiḥ saṃhiteti jāratkārava ārtabhāgaḥ | tasyām etasyāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dhvaṃsayo nimeṣāḥ kāṣṭhāḥ kalāḥ kṣaṇā muhūrtā ahorātrā ardhamāsā māsā ṛtavaḥ saṃvatsarāś ca saṃdhīyante | saiṣā saṃhitainān kālān saṃdadhāti | kālo gatinivṛttisthitīḥ saṃdadhāti | gatinivṛttisthitibhir idaṃ sarvaṃ saṃdhīyate | ityadhidaivatam | athādhyātmam - bhūtaṃ pūrvarūpaṃ bhaviṣyad uttararūpaṃ bhavat saṃhiteti kālasaṃdhiḥ | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam - mahat tan nāma guhyaṃ puruspṛg yena bhutaṃ janayo yena bhavyam | pratnaṃ jātaṃ jyotir yad asya priyaṃ priyāḥ samaviśanta pañca || iti | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 7,21
'Motion is the prior form, cessation is the latter form, rest is the <s>saṃhitā</s>' — so said <s>Jāratkārava Ārtabhāga</s>. In this <s>saṃhitā</s>, moments, blinks, <s>kāṣṭhā</s>-units, <s>kalā</s>-units, instants, <s>muhūrtas</s> (hours), days-and-nights, half-months, months, seasons, and years are all joined together. This <s>saṃhitā</s> joins together these time-units. Time joins together motion, cessation, and rest. Through motion, cessation, and rest all this is joined together. This is with reference to the divine. Now with reference to the self: the past is the prior form, the future is the latter form, the present is the <s>saṃhitā</s> — this is the junction of time. This has been expressed by the <s>Ṛc</s> verse: 'Great is that secret name, widely touching, by which you generated the past and the future. The ancient born light which is dear to him — the five dear ones entered it.' He who knows this <s>saṃhitā</s> thus is joined with offspring, cattle, glory, sacred splendor, and the heavenly world, and lives his full life.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,22
athāto vāliśikhāyaner vacaḥ | pañcemāni mahābhūtāni bhavantīti ha smāha vāliśikhayaniḥ | pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyautīṃṣi tāni mithaḥ saṃhitani bhavanti | aatha yānyanyāni kṣudrāṇi mahābhūtaiḥ saṃdhīyante saiṣā sarvavibhūtasaṃhitā | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 7,22
Now, the teaching of <s>Vāliśikhāyani</s>. 'There are these five great elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>)' — so said <s>Vāliśikhāyani</s>: earth, wind, space, water, and lights. These are mutually conjoined. And whatever other small things are joined with the great elements — this is the <s>saṃhitā</s> of all manifestations. He who knows this <s>saṃhitā</s> thus is joined with offspring, cattle, glory, sacred splendor, and the heavenly world, and lives his full life.

children.text:
ŚĀ 7,23
sarvā vāg brahmeti ha smāha lauhikyaḥ | ye tu kecana śabdā vācam eva tāṃ vidyāt | tad apyetad ṛṣir āha - ahaṃ rudrebhir vasubhiś carāmīti | saiṣā vāk sarvaśabdā bhavati | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti | yatā caitad brahma kāmarūpi kāmacāri bhavatyevaṃ haiva sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu kāmarūpī kāmacārī bhavati | ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 7,23
'All speech is <s>Brahman</s>' — so said <s>Lauhikya</s>. Whatever sounds there are, one should know them as speech alone. The <s>Ṛṣi</s> (seer) also said this: 'I move with the <s>Rudras</s> and the <s>Vasus</s>.' This speech becomes all sounds. He who knows this <s>saṃhitā</s> thus is joined with offspring, cattle, glory, sacred splendor, and the heavenly world, and lives his full life. Just as this <s>Brahman</s> becomes of any form at will and moves wherever it wishes, so too does he who knows thus become of any form and move freely among all beings — he who knows thus, he who knows thus.

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 8,1
prāṇo vaṃśa iti ha smāha sthaviraḥ śākalyaḥ | tadu yathā śālāvaṃśe sarve 'nye vaṃśāḥ samāhitāḥ syur evam evaitasmin prāṇe sarva ātmā samāhitaḥ | tasyaitadyātmanaḥ prāṇa ūṣmarūpam asthīni sparśarūpaṃ majjānaḥ svararūpaṃ māṃsaṃ lohitam ityetac caturtham antasthārūpam iti | treyaṃ tveva na etat proktam iti ha smāha hvastro māṇḍūkeyaḥ | tasyaitasya trayasya trīṇītaḥ ṣaṣṭiśatāni bhavanti saṃdhīnāṃ trīṇītas tāni saptaviṃśatiśatāni bhavanti | sapta vai viṃśatiśatāni saṃvatsarasyāhorātrāṇām | tat saṃvatsarasyāhorātrāṇyāpnoti | sa eṣa saṃvatsarasaṃmānaś cakṣurmayaś śrotramayaś chandomayo manomayo vāṅmaya ātmā | sa ya evam etaṃ saṃvatsarasaṃmānaṃ cakṣurmayaṃ śrotramayaṃ chandomayaṃ manomayaṃ vāmayam ātmānaṃ veda saṃvatsarasya sāyaujyaṃ salokatāṃ sarūpatāṃ sabhakṣatām aśnute | putrī paśumān bhavati sarvam āyur etyasyāruṇikeyo devayāñcakre ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 8,1
'<s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) is the ridge-pole (<s>vaṃśa</s>)' — so said the elder <s>Śākalya</s>. Just as in the ridge-pole of a hall all other beams are established, so in this <s>prāṇa</s> the entire self is established. Of this self: <s>prāṇa</s> is the form of sibilants (<s>ūṣman</s>), bones are the form of stops (<s>sparśa</s>), marrow is the form of vowels (<s>svara</s>), flesh and blood — this fourth is the form of semivowels (<s>antasthā</s>). 'But only three should be spoken of, not this' — so said <s>Hvastra Māṇḍūkeya</s>. Of these three, there are three hundred and sixty; of the conjunctions, three times that, making twenty-seven hundred. Twenty-seven hundred are indeed the days and nights of the year. Thus one attains the days and nights of the year. This is the self measured by the year, made of the eye, made of the ear, made of meter, made of mind, made of speech. He who knows this self measured by the year, made of the eye, made of the ear, made of meter, made of mind, made of speech, attains co-power, co-world, co-form, and co-enjoyment with the year. He becomes possessed of sons, possessed of cattle, lives his full life — thus <s>Āruṇikeya</s> performed the divine journey.

children.text:
ŚĀ 8,2
atha kauṣṭharavyaḥ | trīṇi ṣaṣṭiśatānyakṣarāṇām | trīṇi ṣaṣṭiśatānyūṣmaṇām | trīṇi ṣaṣṭiśatāni saṃdhīnām | yānyakṣarāṇyavocāmāhāni tāni | yān ūṣmaṇo rātrayastāḥ | yān saṃdhīn avocāmāhorātrāṇāṃ te saṃdhayaḥ | ityadhidaivatam | athādhyātmam - yānyakṣarāṇyadhidaivatam avocāmāsthīni tānyadhyātmam | yān ūṣmaṇo 'dhidaivatam avocāma +majjānas te 'dhyātmam | eṣa u ha vai saṃpratiprāṇo yan majjā etad retaḥ na vā ṛte prāṇād retasaḥ siddhir asti | yad vā ṛte prāṇād retaḥ sicyeta tat pūyen na saṃbhavet | yān saṃdhīn adhidaivatam avocāma parvāṇi tānyadhyātmam | tasyaitasyāsthnāṃ +majjā parvaṇām iti pañcetaścatvāriṃśacchatāni bhavanti | saṃdhīnāṃ pañcetastadaśītisahasraṃ bhavati | aśītisahasraṃ vārkalino bṛhatīr aharahani saṃpādayanti | sa eṣo 'haḥsaṃmānaś cakṣurmayaś śrotramayaś chandomayo manomayo vāṅmaya ātmā | sa ya evam etad ahaḥsaṃmānaṃ cakṣurmayaṃ śrotramayaṃ chandomayaṃ manomayaṃ vāmayam ātmānaṃ veda ahnāṃ sāyaujyaṃ salokatāṃ sarūpatāṃ sabhakṣatām aśnute | putrī paśumān bhavati sarvam āyur eti ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 8,2
Now <s>Kauṣṭharavya</s>'s teaching: three hundred and sixty are the syllables, three hundred and sixty are the sibilants, three hundred and sixty are the conjunctions. The syllables we have spoken of — those are the days. The sibilants — those are the nights. The conjunctions we have spoken of — those are the junctions of the days and nights. This is with reference to the divine. Now with reference to the self: the syllables we spoke of with reference to the divine — those are the bones in the self. The sibilants we spoke of with reference to the divine — those are the marrow in the self. This marrow is indeed the concordant <s>prāṇa</s>; it is the semen. For without <s>prāṇa</s> there is no success of semen; if semen were shed without <s>prāṇa</s>, it would decay and not produce [offspring]. The conjunctions we spoke of with reference to the divine — those are the joints in the self. Of these bones, marrow, and joints, there are five hundred and forty. Of the conjunctions, there are eighty thousand. The <s>Arkins</s> (chanters) produce eighty thousand <s>Bṛhatī</s> [verses] day after day. This is the self measured by the day, made of the eye, made of the ear, made of meter, made of mind, made of speech. He who knows this self measured by the day, made of the eye, made of the ear, made of meter, made of mind, made of speech, attains co-power, co-world, co-form, and co-enjoyment with the days. He becomes possessed of sons, possessed of cattle, and lives his full life.

children.text:
ŚĀ 8,3
catvāraḥ puruṣā iti vāstyaḥ - śarīrapuruṣaś chandaḥpuruṣo vedepuruṣo mahāpuruṣa iti | śarīrapuruṣa iti yam avocam ya evāyaṃ daivika ātmā tasyaitasya yo 'yam aśarīraḥ prajñātmā sa rasaḥ | chandaḥpuruṣa iti yam avocāmākṣarasamāmnāya eva | tasyaitasyākāro rasaḥ | vedapuruṣa iti yam avocāma yena devān vedargvedaṃ yajurvedaṃ sāmavedam iti tasyaitasya brahmarasaḥ | tasmād brahmiṣṭhaṃ brahmāṇam ṛtvijaṃ kurvīta yo yajñasyolvaṇaṃ vidyāt | mahāpuruṣa iti yam avocāma saṃvatsara eva tasyaitasyāsāv ādityo rasaḥ | sa yaś cāyam aśarīraḥ prajñātmā yaś cāsāv āditya ekam etad iti vidyāt | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 8,3
'There are four persons (<s>puruṣas</s>)' — so said <s>Vāstya</s>: the body-person (<s>śarīra-puruṣa</s>), the meter-person (<s>chandaḥ-puruṣa</s>), the Veda-person (<s>veda-puruṣa</s>), and the great person (<s>mahā-puruṣa</s>). The body-person is the one we have spoken of — the divine self; of this one, the bodiless intelligent self (<s>aśarīraḥ prajñātmā</s>) is the essence. The meter-person is the one we have spoken of — the collection of syllables itself; of this one, the syllable 'a' is the essence. The Veda-person is the one we have spoken of — that by which one knows the gods, the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, and the <s>Sāmaveda</s>; of this one, <s>Brahman</s> is the essence. Therefore one should make a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (priest) who is most learned in <s>Brahman</s> the <s>Ṛtvij</s> (officiating priest) — one who would know the excess of the sacrifice. The great person is the one we have spoken of — the year itself; of this one, yonder sun is the essence. One should know that the bodiless intelligent self and yonder sun are one and the same. This has been expressed by the <s>Ṛc</s> verse:

children.text:
ŚĀ 8,4
citraṃ devānām udagād anīkaṃ cakṣur mitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ | āprā dyāvāpṛthivī antarikṣaṃ sūrya ātmā jagatas tasthuṣaś ca || iti | etām evānuvidyāṃ saṃhitāṃ saṃdhīyamānāṃ manya iti ha smāha vātsyaḥ -- etam u haiva bahvṛcā mahadukthe mīmāṃsanta etam agnāv adhvaryava etaṃ mahāvrate chandogā etam asyām etam antarikṣa etaṃ divi etam agnāv etaṃ vāyāv etaṃ candramasy etaṃ nakṣatreṣv etam apsv etam oṣadhīṣv etaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣv etam akṣareṣv etam eva brahmetyupāsate | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 8,4
'The brilliant face of the gods has risen, the eye of <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Agni</s>. He has filled heaven, earth, and the atmosphere — <s>Sūrya</s> is the self of all that moves and stands.' 'I consider this very learning, this <s>saṃhitā</s>, to be being joined' — so said <s>Vātsya</s>. 'This indeed the <s>Bahvṛcas</s> (Ṛgvedic priests) investigate in the <s>Mahad Uktha</s> (great hymn), this the <s>Adhvaryus</s> (Yajurvedic priests) investigate in the fire, this the <s>Chandogas</s> (Sāmavedic priests) in the <s>Mahāvrata</s>, this in this [earth], this in the atmosphere, this in heaven, this in fire, this in wind, this in the moon, this in the stars, this in the waters, this in plants, this in all beings, this in the syllables — this they worship as <s>Brahman</s> itself.' This has been expressed by the <s>Ṛc</s> verse:

children.text:
ŚĀ 8,5
ud vayaṃ tamasas pari jyotiṣ paśyanta uttaram | devaṃ devatrā sūryam aganma jyotir uttamam || iti | sa eṣo 'kṣarasaṃmānaś cakṣurmayaḥ śrotramayaś chandamayo manomayo vāṅmaya ātmā | sa ya evam etam akṣarasaṃānaṃ cakṣurmayaṃ śrotramayaṃ chandamayaṃ manomayaṃ vāṅmayam ātmānaṃ parasmai śaṃsati dugdhadohā asya vedā bhavanti | abhāgo vāci bhavati abhāgo 'nūkte | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 8,5
'Rising above darkness, we see the higher light. Going to the god among gods, <s>Sūrya</s>, we have reached the supreme light.' This is the self measured by syllables, made of the eye, made of the ear, made of meter, made of mind, made of speech. He who recites this self measured by syllables, made of the eye, made of the ear, made of meter, made of mind, made of speech, to another — his <s>Vedas</s> become milked dry. He becomes portionless in speech, portionless in recitation. This has been expressed by the <s>Ṛc</s> verse:
