children.text:
ŚĀ 8,6
yas tityāja sacividaṃ sakhāyaṃ na tasya vācy api bhāgo asti | yad īṃ śṛnoty alakaṃ śṛṇoti na hi praveda sukṛtasya panthām || iti | nāsyānūkte vāco bhāgo astīty eva tad āha tan na parasmā etad ahaḥ śaṃset | nāgniṃ cinuyān na mahāvratena stuyān ned ātmano 'pihīyā iti | sa yaś cāyam aśarīraḥ prajñātmā yaś cāsāv āditya ekam etad ity avocāma tau yatra vipradṛśyete ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 8,6: 'He who has forsaken his companion, the well-wisher — he has no share in speech. What he hears, he hears in vain, for he does not know the path of good action.' Thus [the verse says]. He who has not been taught has no share in speech — this is indeed what it says. Therefore one should not recite this day [of recitation] to another. One should not build the fire-altar, nor should one sing with the <s>Mahāvrata</s> [rite] — lest one be diminished from the self. Now, we have said that this bodiless intelligent self (<s>aśarīra prajñātman</s>) and yonder sun are one and the same. Where these two appear to diverge —

children.text:
ŚĀ 8,7
candramā ivādityo dṛśyate na raśmayaḥ prādur bhavanti | lohinī dyaur bhavati yathā mañjiṣṭhāḥ | vyastaḥ pāyur bhavati | saṃpareto 'syātmā na ciram iva jīviṣyatīti vidyāt | sa yat karaṇīyaṃ manyeta tat kuryāt | athāpyādarśe vodake vā jihmaśirasaṃ vāśirasaṃ vātmānaṃ paśyen na vā paśyet | tad apy evam eva vidyāt | athāpi cchidrā chāyā bhavati na vā bhavati tad apy evam eva vidyāt | athāpi cchidra ivādityo rathanābhir ivākhyāyet tad apy evam eva vidyāt | athāpi nīla ivāgnir dṛśyeta yathā mayūragrīvā mahāmeghe vā marīcīr iva paśyet | anabhre vā vidyutaṃ paśyet | abhra enāṃ mna paśyet tad apy evam eva vidyāt | athāpy apidhāyākṣiṇī upekṣeta tatraitad varāṭakānīva na paśyet tad apy evam eva vidyāt | athāpy apidhāya karṇā upāsīta | ya eṣo 'gner iva jvalataḥ śabdo rathasyevopabdis taṃ na yadā śṛṇuyāt tad apy evam eva vidyāt | athāpi viparyaste kanyake dṛśyete dvijihmevā na vā dṛśyetetad apy evam eva vidyāt | sa yo 'to 'śruto 'mato 'vijñāto 'dṛṣṭo 'nādiṣṭo 'ghuṣṭaḥ śrotā mantā vijñātā draṣṭādeṣṭā ghoṣṭā sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām āntaraḥ puruṣaḥ sa ma ātmeti
vidyāt | sa utkrāmann evaitam aśarīraṃ prajñātmānam abhisaṃpadyate vijahātītaraṃ dauhikam | saiṣā sarvasyai vāca upaniṣat | sarvā haivemāḥ sarvasyai vācaupaniṣadaḥ | imāṃ tv evam ācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 8,7: The sun appears like the moon, its rays do not come forth; the sky becomes reddish, as if dyed with madder; the breeze becomes scattered; the self is about to depart — one should know: 'He will not live much longer.' He should do whatever he considers needs to be done. Also, if in a mirror or in water one sees oneself with a crooked head, or headless, or does not see oneself [at all] — that too one should know in the same way. Also, if the shadow becomes full of holes, or does not appear at all — that too one should know in the same way. Also, if the sun appears full of holes, or looks like a wheel-hub — that too one should know in the same way. Also, if fire appears blue like a peacock's neck, or one sees what looks like rays in a great cloud, or one sees lightning in a cloudless sky, or a cloud but does not see it — that too one should know in the same way. Also, if upon closing the eyes and looking inward, one does not see something like cowrie-shells — that too one should know in the same way. Also, if upon closing the ears and listening inward, one does not hear the sound like that of a blazing fire or like the rumbling of a chariot — that too one should know in the same way. Also, if the pupils of the eyes appear reversed, or appear doubly askew, or are not seen — that too one should know in the same way. He who, though unheard, unthought, unknown, unseen, undirected, unannounced, is the hearer, the thinker, the knower, the seer, the director, the announcer — the inner <s>puruṣa</s> of all beings — 'He is my self,' one should know. He, at the time of departing, enters into this bodiless intelligent self (<s>aśarīra prajñātman</s>) and leaves behind the other, the bodily one (<s>dauhika</s>). This is the secret teaching (<s>upaniṣad</s>) of all speech. All these indeed are the secret teachings of all speech. But they declare this one in particular.

children.text:
ŚĀ 8,8
pṛthivyā rūpaṃ sparśā antarikṣasyoṣmāṇo divaḥ svarāḥ | agne rūpaṃ sparśā vāyor ūṣmāṇa ādityasya svarāḥ | ṛgvedasya rūpaṃ sparśā yajurvedasyoṣmāṇaḥ sāmavedasya svarāḥ | rathantarasya rūpaṃ sparśā vāmadevyasyoṣmāṇo bṛhataḥ svarāḥ | prāṇasya rūpaṃ sparśā apānasyoṣmāṇo manasaḥ svarāḥ | prāṇasya rūpaṃ sparśā apānasyoṣmāṇa udānasya svarāḥ svarā iti punardattaḥ | eṣa u haiva sarvāṃ vācaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 8,8: Of the earth, the vowels (<s>rūpa</s>); the stops (<s>sparśa</s>) of the atmosphere; the sibilants (<s>ūṣmān</s>) of heaven; the tones (<s>svara</s>). Of <s>Agni</s> (fire), the vowels; the stops of <s>Vāyu</s> (wind); the sibilants of <s>Āditya</s> (the sun); the tones. Of the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the vowels; the stops of the <s>Yajurveda</s>; the sibilants of the <s>Sāmaveda</s>; the tones. Of the <s>Rathantara</s> [sāman], the vowels; the stops of the <s>Vāmadevya</s> [sāman]; the sibilants of the <s>Bṛhat</s> [sāman]; the tones. Of <s>prāṇa</s> (inbreath), the vowels; the stops of <s>apāna</s> (outbreath); the sibilants of the mind; the tones. Of <s>prāṇa</s>, the vowels; the stops of <s>apāna</s>; the sibilants of <s>udāna</s> (upward breath); the tones — the tones [are thus] given back again. He who knows thus indeed knows all speech.

children.text:
ŚĀ 8,9
atha khalv iyaṃ daivī vīṇā bhavati tadanukṛtir asau mānuṣī bhavati | tad yatheyaṃ śastravatī tardmavatī bhavaty evam evāsau śastravatī tardmavatī bhavati | tad yathāsyāḥ śira evam amuṣyāḥ śiraḥ | tad yathāsyai vaṃśa evam amuṣyā daṇḍaḥ | tad yathāsyā udaram evam amuṣyā ambhaṇaṃ | tad yathāsyai mukhanāsike akṣiṇī ity evam amuṣyāś chidrāṇi | tad yathāsyā aṅgulinigrahā upastaraṇānīty evam amuṣyāḥ parvāṇi | tad yathāsyā aṅgulaya evam amuṣyās tantryaḥ | tad yathāsyai jihvaivam amuṣyā vādanam | tad yathāsyāḥ svarā evam amuṣyāḥ svarāḥ | tad yathā haiveyaṃ romaśena carmaṇāpihitā bhavaty evam evāsau romaśena carmaṇāpihitā bhavati | romaśena ha sma carmaṇā purā vīṇā apidadhati | saiṣā daivī vīṇā bhavati | sa ya evam etāṃ daivīṃ vīṇāṃ veda śrutavadanatamo bhavati bhūmiprāsya kīrtir bhavati +śuśrūṣante hāsya parṣatsu bhāṣyamāṇasyedam astu yad ayam īhate yatrāryā vāg vadati vidur enaṃ tatra ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 8,9: Now, this is the divine <s>vīṇā</s> (lute); the human [lute] is made in imitation of it. Just as this [body] has the <s>śastra</s> (recitation) and the breath-holes, so that [instrument] has the plectrum and the holes. Just as this [body] has a head, so that [instrument] has a head. Just as this [body] has a spine (<s>vaṃśa</s>), so that [instrument] has a neck-piece (<s>daṇḍa</s>). Just as this [body] has a belly, so that [instrument] has a resonating chamber (<s>ambhaṇa</s>). Just as this [body] has a face, nostrils, and eyes, so that [instrument] has its openings. Just as this [body] has fingers, finger-grips, and coverings, so that [instrument] has its joints. Just as this [body] has fingers, so that [instrument] has its strings. Just as this [body] has a tongue, so that [instrument] has a plectrum. Just as this [body] has tones, so that [instrument] has tones. Just as this [body] is covered by hairy skin, so that [instrument] is covered by hairy skin. Indeed, in ancient times they used to cover the <s>vīṇā</s> with hairy skin. This is the divine <s>vīṇā</s>. He who thus knows this divine <s>vīṇā</s> becomes the most learned in <s>Veda</s> recitation; his fame spreads across the earth; wherever noble speech is spoken, they recognize him. People listen eagerly when he speaks in assemblies: 'May that which he strives for be fulfilled.'

children.text:
ŚĀ 8,10
athātas tāṇḍavindasya vacaḥ | tad yatheyaṃ akuśalena vādayitrāvīṇārabdhā na kṛtsnaṃ vīṇārthaṃ sādhayaty evam evākuśalena vaktrā vāg ārabdhā na kṛtsnaṃ vāg arthaṃ sādhayati | tad yathā haiveyaṃ kuśalena vādayitrā vīṇārabdhā kṛtsnaṃ vīṇārthaṃ sādhayaty evam eva kuśalena vaktrā vāg ārabdhā kṛtsnaṃ vāg arthaṃ sādhayati | tasyai vā etasyai vīṇāyai yā tviṣiḥ sā saṃhiteti kātyāyanīputro jātūkarṇyaḥ | atha ha smaitat kṛtsnahārito brāhmaṇam evodāharati ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 8,10: Now, the words of <s>Tāṇḍavinda</s>. Just as this [lute], when taken up by an unskilled player, does not accomplish the full purpose of the <s>vīṇā</s>, so speech, when taken up by an unskilled speaker, does not accomplish the full purpose of speech. And just as this [lute], when taken up by a skilled player, accomplishes the full purpose of the <s>vīṇā</s>, so speech, when taken up by a skilled speaker, accomplishes the full purpose of speech. Of this <s>vīṇā</s>, whatever luster it has, that is the <s>saṃhitā</s> (combination) — so said <s>Jātūkarṇya</s>, son of <s>Kātyāyanī</s>. And <s>Kṛtsnahārita</s> used to cite this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text] indeed.

children.text:
ŚĀ 8,11
prajāpatiḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā vyasraṃsata sa chandobhir ātmānaṃ samadadhat | tad yac chandobhir ātmānaṃ samadadhat tasmāt saṃhitā | tasyai vā etasyai saṃhitāyai ṇakaro balaṃ ṣakāraḥ prāṇa ātmā saṃhitā | athaiṣā kṣudramiśrā vikṛtis tāni nakhāni romāṇi vyañjanānīti | sa yo 'tra vicikitset saṇakāraṃ eva brūyād ṛte ṇakāram iti saṇakāram eva brūyāt | evam eva yo 'tra vicikitset saṣakāraṃ eva brūyād ṛte ṣakāram iti saṣakāram eva brūyāt | tau vā etau ṇakāraṣakārau vidvān anusaṃhitam ṛco 'dhīyītāyuṣyam iti vidyād evam eva vidyāt | atha vāg itihāsapurāṇaṃ yac cānyat kiṃcid brāhmīkṛtyevādhīyīta tad apy evam eva vidyāt | te yad vayam anusaṃhitam ṛco 'dhīmahe yac ca māṇḍūkeyīyam adhyāyaṃ prabrūmas tena no ṇakāraṣakārā upāptāv iti ha smāha hrasvo māṇḍūkeyaḥ | atha yad vayam anusaṃhitam ṛco 'dhīmahe yac ca svādhyāyam adhīmahe tena no ṇakāraṣakārā upāptāv iti ha smāha sthaviraḥ śākalyaḥ | etad dha sma vai tad vidvāṃsa āhuḥ kāvaṣeyāḥ kimarthā vayaṃ yakṣyāmahe kimarthā vayam adheṣyāmahe vāci hi prāṇaṃ juhumaḥ prāṇe vācaṃ yo hy eva prabhavaḥ sa evāpyaya iti | tā etāḥ saṃhitā
nānantevāsine brūyān nāsaṃvatsaravāsine nābrahmacāriṇe nāvedavide nāpavaktra ity ācāryā ity ācāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 8,11: <s>Prajāpati</s>, having created beings, fell apart. He put himself together with the meters (<s>chandas</s>). Because he put himself together (<s>samadadhat</s>) with the meters, therefore it is called <s>saṃhitā</s> (putting together, combination). Of this <s>saṃhitā</s>, the <s>ṇa</s>-sound is the strength; the <s>ṣa</s>-sound is the <s>prāṇa</s> (breath); the self is the <s>saṃhitā</s>. Now, this minor modification is the mixed alteration; the nails, hairs, and consonants belong to it. If one should be uncertain here, one should pronounce the <s>ṇa</s>-sound where otherwise one would omit the <s>ṇa</s>-sound — one should pronounce the <s>ṇa</s>-sound. Likewise, if one should be uncertain here, one should pronounce the <s>ṣa</s>-sound where otherwise one would omit the <s>ṣa</s>-sound — one should pronounce the <s>ṣa</s>-sound. The learned one, knowing these <s>ṇa</s>-sound and <s>ṣa</s>-sound, should recite the <s>ṛcs</s> (verses) with proper combination (<s>anusaṃhita</s>); one should know this as conducive to long life. Whatever one studies — speech, <s>itihāsa</s> (history), <s>purāṇa</s> (legend), and whatever else pertains to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-study — that too one should know in the same way. 'That which we recite the <s>ṛcs</s> with proper combination, and the <s>Māṇḍūkeyīya</s> chapter that we teach — by that the <s>ṇa</s>-sound and <s>ṣa</s>-sound are acquired by us,' so said the young <s>Māṇḍūkeya</s>. 'That which we recite the <s>ṛcs</s> with proper combination, and the self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) that we study — by that the <s>ṇa</s>-sound and <s>ṣa</s>-sound are acquired by us,' so said the elder <s>Śākalya</s>. This indeed the wise <s>Kāvaṣeyas</s> used to say: 'For what purpose should we sacrifice? For what purpose should we study? For in speech we offer <s>prāṇa</s>; in <s>prāṇa</s>, speech. That which is indeed the source is also the dissolution.' These teachings on <s>saṃhitā</s> should not be told to one who is not a resident student, nor to one who has not dwelt [with a teacher] for a year, nor to one who does not observe <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship), nor to one who does not know the <s>Veda</s>, nor to one who speaks improperly — thus [say] the teachers, thus [say] the teachers.

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake aṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 9,1
om | tat savitur vṛṇīmahe | vayaṃ devasya bhojanam | śreṣṭhaṃ sarvadhātamam | turaṃ bhagasya dhīmahi | tat savitur vareṇyaṃ | bhargo devasya dhīmahi | dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt || adabdhaṃ mana iṣiraṃ cakṣuḥ | sūryo jyotiṣāṃ śreṣṭho dīkṣe mā mā hiṃsīḥ ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 9,1: <s>Oṃ</s>. We choose that of <s>Savitṛ</s>. We [seek] the nourishment of the god, the best, all-sustaining. We meditate on the generosity of <s>Bhaga</s>. We meditate on that excellent splendor of divine <s>Savitṛ</s>; may he inspire our thoughts. The unassailable mind, the keen sight — <s>Sūrya</s> is the best of lights. O <s>Dīkṣā</s> (consecration), do not harm me!

children.text:
ŚĀ 9,2
yo ha vai jyeṣṭhaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ ca veda jyeṣṭhaś ca ha vai śreṣṭhaś ca svānāṃ bhavati | prāṇo vai jyeṣṭhaś ca śreṣṭhaś ca | yo ha vai vasiṣṭhāṃ veda vasiṣṭho ha svānāṃ bhavati vāg vai vasiṣṭhā | yo ha vai pratiṣṭhāṃ veda prati ha tiṣṭhaty asmiṃś ca loke 'muṣmiṃś ca cakṣur ha pratiṣṭhā | yo ha vai saṃpadaṃ veda saṃ hāsmai kāmāḥ saṃpadyante śrotraṃ ha vā u saṃpat | yo ha vā āyatanaṃ vedāyatano ha svānāṃ bhavati mano vā āyatanam | atha hemā devatāḥ prajāpatiṃ pitaram etyābruvan ko vai naḥ śreṣṭha iti | sa hovāca prajāpatir yasmin va utkrānte śarīraṃ pāpiṣṭham iva manyate sa vai śreṣṭha iti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 9,2: He who indeed knows the eldest and the best becomes the eldest and the best among his own people. <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) is indeed the eldest and the best. He who knows the most excellent (<s>vasiṣṭha</s>) becomes the most excellent among his own people; speech is indeed the most excellent. He who knows firm standing (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) stands firm in this world and in the other world; the eye is indeed firm standing. He who knows success (<s>saṃpad</s>) — for him desires are fulfilled; hearing is indeed success. He who knows the abode (<s>āyatana</s>) becomes the abode of his own people; the mind is indeed the abode. Now, these deities went to <s>Prajāpati</s>, their father, and said: 'Which of us is the best?' He, <s>Prajāpati</s>, said: 'That one, upon whose departure the body is considered most deficient — that one is the best.'

children.text:
ŚĀ 9,3
sā ha vāg uccakrāma | yathā mūkā avadantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa dhyāyanto manasaivam iti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 9,3: Speech departed. Just as the dumb, not speaking but breathing with breath, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear, thinking with the mind — so [they continued].

children.text:
ŚĀ 9,4
cakṣur hoccakrāma | yathāndhā apaśyantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa dhyāyanto manasaivam iti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 9,4: The eye departed. Just as the blind, not seeing but breathing with breath, speaking with speech, hearing with the ear, thinking with the mind — so [they continued].

children.text:
ŚĀ 9,5
śrotraṃ hoccakrāma | yathā badhirā aśṛṇvantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaḥ cakṣuṣā dhyāyanto manasaivam iti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 9,5: The ear departed. Just as the deaf, not hearing but breathing with breath, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, thinking with the mind — so [they continued].

children.text:
ŚĀ 9,6
mano hoccakrāma | yathā bālā amanasaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaḥ cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇaivam iti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 9,6: The mind departed. Just as the simple-minded, without mind but breathing with breath, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear — so [they continued].

children.text:
ŚĀ 9,7
prāṇo hoccakrāma | tatas tad yatheha saindhavaḥ suhayaḥ paḍbīśaśaṅkūn saṃkhided evam asau prāṇān samakhidat | te ha sametyocur bhagavan motkramīr iti | sa hovāca prāṇaḥ kiṃ me 'nnaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | yat kiṃcāśvabhya ivāśakunibhya iti | kiṃ me vāso bhaviṣyatīty āpa iti hocuḥ | tasmād vā ayam aśiṣyan purastāc copariṣṭāc cādbhiḥ paridadhāti | lambhuko hāsya vāso bhavaty anagno hi bhavati | had dha smaitat satyakāmo jābālo gośrute vaiyāghrapadyāyoktvovāca | apy evaṃ śuṣkasya sthāṇoḥ prabrūyāj jayerann asya śākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśanīti | vanaspate śatavalśo viroheti dyāṃ mā lekhīr antarikṣaṃ mā mā hiṃsīr iti ha yājñavalkyaḥ ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 9,7
<s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) departed. Thereupon, just as a powerful Sindhu horse would pull out the foot-pegs and tethering stakes, so it pulled out the vital functions. They came together and said: "Lord, do not depart from us!" <s>Prāṇa</s> said: "What shall my food be?" "Whatever there is, even [what is fit] for dogs and birds," they said. "What shall my garment be?" "Water," they said. Therefore, one who is about to eat first covers himself with water from in front and from above. He becomes a receiver of garments and is not naked. Regarding this, <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>, having told this to <s>Gośruti Vaiyāghrapadya</s>, said: "Even if one were to say this to a dry stump, branches would sprout from it and leaves would grow." "O lord of the forest, may you grow with a hundred shoots; may I reach to heaven; may you not scratch me, may you not injure the atmosphere" — thus [said] <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 9,8
atha yadi mahaj jigamiṣet trirātraṃ dīkṣitvāmāvāsyāyāṃ sarvauṣadasya manthaṃ dadhimadhubhyām upamanthyāgnim upassamādhāya parisamuhya paristīrya paryukṣya dakṣiṇaṃ jānv ācyottarato 'gneḥ kaṃse manthaṃ kṛtvā hutvā homān manthe saṃpātaṃ ānayet | jyeṣṭhāya śreṣṭhāya svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃpātam ānayet | pratiṣṭhāyai svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃpātam ānayet | saṃpade svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃpātam ānayet | tat savitur vareṇyam iti pacchaḥ prāśya tat savitur vṛṇīmaha iti paccha ācāmati mahāvyāhṛtibhiś caturthaṃ nirṇijya kāṃsyaṃ carmaṇi vā sthaṇḍile vā saṃviśati | sa yadi striyaṃ paśyet samṛddhaṃ karmeti vidyāt samṛddhaṃ karmeti vidyāt ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 9,8
Now, if one wishes to attain greatness, having observed the consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) for three nights, on the new-moon night, having stirred up a mixture of all herbs with curds and honey, having built up the fire, swept around it, spread the sacrificial grass, sprinkled water, having bent the right knee to the north of the fire, he places the mixture in a bronze vessel. Having offered the oblations, he should bring the remnant into the mixture. "To the eldest, to the best, <s>svāhā</s>!" — having offered in the fire, he should bring the remnant into the mixture. "To the foundation, <s>svāhā</s>!" — having offered in the fire, he should bring the remnant into the mixture. "To prosperity, <s>svāhā</s>!" — having offered in the fire, he should bring the remnant into the mixture. "That excellent [glory] of <s>Savitṛ</s>" — having eaten the remainder, "[That] of <s>Savitṛ</s> we choose" — having sipped water afterwards, having rinsed four times with the <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great sacred utterances), he places the bronze [vessel] on a skin or on bare ground and lies down. If he sees a woman [in a dream], he should know that the rite has succeeded — he should know that the rite has succeeded.

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake navamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 10,1
athāto 'dhyātmikam | āntaram agnihotram ity ācakṣate | etā ha vai devatāḥ puruṣa eva pratiṣṭhitā agnir vāci vāyuḥ prāṇa ādityaś cakṣuṣi candramā manasi diśaḥ śrotra āpo retasi | etāsu ha vai sarvāsu hutaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca | so 'śnāti sa pibati sa tṛpyati sa tarpayati ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 10,1
Now, concerning the self (<s>adhyātmikam</s>). They call it the inner <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-sacrifice). These deities are indeed established in the person: <s>Agni</s> (fire) in speech, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) in breath, <s>Āditya</s> (sun) in the eye, <s>Candramā</s> (moon) in the mind, the quarters in the ear, the waters in semen. Offerings are made in all of these when one who knows this eats and drinks and feeds and gives drink. He eats, he drinks, he is satisfied, he satisfies [others].

children.text:
ŚĀ 10,2
sa tṛpto vācaṃ tarpayati | vāk tṛptāgniṃ tarpayati | agnis tṛptaḥ pṛthivīṃ tarpayati | pṛthivī tṛptā yat kiṃcit pṛthhivyāpihitaṃ bhavad bhaviṣyad bhūtaṃ tat sarvaṃ tarpayati | ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca so 'śnāti sa pibati sa tṛpyati sa tarpayati ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 10,2
Being satisfied, he satisfies speech. Speech, being satisfied, satisfies <s>Agni</s> (fire). <s>Agni</s>, being satisfied, satisfies the earth. The earth, being satisfied, satisfies everything that has been, will be, and is, encompassed by the earth. One who knows this and eats and drinks and feeds and gives drink — he eats, he drinks, he is satisfied, he satisfies [others].

children.text:
ŚĀ 10,3
sa tṛptaḥ prāṇaṃ tarpayati | prāṇas tṛpto vāyuṃ tarpayati | vāyus tṛpta ākāśaṃ tarpayati | ākāśas tṛpto yat kiṃcākāśenāpihitam bhavad bhaviṣyad bhūtaṃ tat sarvaṃ tarpayati | ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca so 'śnāti sa pibati sa tṛpyati sa tarpayati ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 10,3
Being satisfied, he satisfies <s>prāṇa</s> (breath). <s>Prāṇa</s>, being satisfied, satisfies <s>Vāyu</s> (wind). <s>Vāyu</s>, being satisfied, satisfies <s>ākāśa</s> (space). <s>Ākāśa</s>, being satisfied, satisfies everything that has been, will be, and is, encompassed by space. One who knows this and eats and drinks and feeds and gives drink — he eats, he drinks, he is satisfied, he satisfies [others].

children.text:
ŚĀ 10,4
sa tṛptaś cakṣus tarpayati | cakṣus tṛptam ādityaṃ tarpayati | ādityas tṛpto divaṃ tarpayati |dyaus tṛptā yat kiṃcid divāpihitam bhavad bhaviṣyad bhūtaṃ tat sarvaṃ tarpayati | ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca so 'śnāti sa pibati sa tṛpyati sa tarpayati ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 10,4
Being satisfied, he satisfies the eye. The eye, being satisfied, satisfies <s>Āditya</s> (the sun). <s>Āditya</s>, being satisfied, satisfies heaven. Heaven, being satisfied, satisfies everything that has been, will be, and is, encompassed by heaven. One who knows this and eats and drinks and feeds and gives drink — he eats, he drinks, he is satisfied, he satisfies [others].

children.text:
ŚĀ 10,5
sa tṛpto manas tarpayati | manas tṛptaṃ candramasaṃ tarpayati | candramās tṛpto nakṣatrāṇi tarpayati | nakṣatrāṇi tṛptāni māsāṃs tarpayanti | māsās tṛptā ardhamāsāṃs tarpayanti | ardhamāsās tṛptā ahorātre tarpayanti | ahorātre tṛpte ṛtūṃs tarpayataḥ | ṛtavas tṛptāḥ saṃvatsaraṃ tarpayanti | saṃvatsaras tṛpto yat kiṃcit saṃvatsareṇāpihitam bhavad bhaviṣyad bhūtaṃ tat sarvaṃ tarpayati | ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca so 'śnāti sa pibati sa tṛpyati sa tarpayati ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 10,5
Being satisfied, he satisfies the mind. The mind, being satisfied, satisfies <s>Candramā</s> (the moon). <s>Candramā</s>, being satisfied, satisfies the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions). The <s>nakṣatras</s>, being satisfied, satisfy the months. The months, being satisfied, satisfy the half-months. The half-months, being satisfied, satisfy the days and nights. The days and nights, being satisfied, satisfy the seasons. The seasons, being satisfied, satisfy the year. The year, being satisfied, satisfies everything that has been, will be, and is, encompassed by the year. One who knows this and eats and drinks and feeds and gives drink — he eats, he drinks, he is satisfied, he satisfies [others].

children.text:
ŚĀ 10,6
sa tṛptaḥ śrotraṃ tarpayati | śrotraṃ tṛptaṃ diśas tarpayati | diśas tṛptā avāntaradiśas tarpayanti | avāntaradiśas tṛptā yat kiṃcāvāntaradigbhir apihitam bhavad bhaviṣyad bhūtaṃ tat sarvaṃ tarpayati | ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca so 'śnāti sa pibati sa tṛpyati sa tarpayati ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 10,6
Being satisfied, he satisfies the ear. The ear, being satisfied, satisfies the quarters. The quarters, being satisfied, satisfy the intermediate quarters. The intermediate quarters, being satisfied, satisfy everything that has been, will be, and is, encompassed by the intermediate quarters. One who knows this and eats and drinks and feeds and gives drink — he eats, he drinks, he is satisfied, he satisfies [others].

children.text:
ŚĀ 10,7
sa tṛpto retas tarpayati | retas tṛptam apas tarpayati | āpas tṛptā nadīṃs tarpayanti | nadyas tṛptāḥ samudraṃ tarpayanti | samudro tṛpto yat kiṃcit samudreṇāpihitam bhavad bhaviṣyad bhūtaṃ tat sarvaṃ tarpayati | ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca so 'śnāti sa pibati sa tṛpyati sa tarpayati ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 10,7
Being satisfied, he satisfies semen. Semen, being satisfied, satisfies the waters. The waters, being satisfied, satisfy the rivers. The rivers, being satisfied, satisfy the ocean. The ocean, being satisfied, satisfies everything that has been, will be, and is, encompassed by the ocean. One who knows this and eats and drinks and feeds and gives drink — he eats, he drinks, he is satisfied, he satisfies [others].

children.text:
ŚĀ 10,8
sa tṛptas tad etad vairājaṃ daśavidhaṃ agnihotraṃ bhavati | tasya prāṇa evāhavanīyaḥ | apāno gārhapatyo vyāno 'nvāhāryapacano mano dhūmo manyur arcir dantā aṅgārāḥ śraddhā payo vāk samit satyam āhutiḥ prajñātmā sa rasaḥ | tad etad vairājaṃ daśavidhaṃ agnihotraṃ hutaṃ bhavati | rohobhyāṃ rohobhyām abhyārūḷham abhi svargaṃ lokaṃ gamayati ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca | atha ya idam avidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti yathāṅgārān apohya bhasmani hutaṃ tādṛk tatyās tādṛk tat syāt ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 10,8
Being satisfied — this is the tenfold <s>Vairāja agnihotra</s> (fire-sacrifice). In it, <s>prāṇa</s> (exhalation) is the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (offering fire); <s>apāna</s> (inhalation) is the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (household fire); <s>vyāna</s> (diffused breath) is the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> (southern fire); mind is the smoke; anger is the flame; teeth are the embers; faith is the milk; speech is the fuel; truth is the oblation; the intelligent self (<s>prajñātman</s>) is the essence. This tenfold <s>Vairāja agnihotra</s> is offered. It ascends from world to world and conveys to the heavenly world one who knows this and eats and drinks and feeds and gives drink. But for one who, without knowing this, offers the [external] <s>agnihotra</s> — it would be as if one were to push aside the embers and pour the oblation into the ashes; such would be the nature of that [offering].

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake daśamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 11,1
prajāpatir vā imaṃ puruṣam udañcata | tasminn etā devatā āveśayad vācy agniṃ prāṇe vāyuṃ apāne vidyuta udāne parjanyaṃ cakṣuṣy ādityaṃ manasi candramasaṃ śrotre diśaḥ śarīre pṛthivīṃ retasy apo bala indraṃ manyāv īśānaṃ mūrdhany ākāśaṃ ātmani brahma | sa yathā mahān amṛtakumbhaḥ pinvamānas tiṣṭhed evaṃ haiva sa tasthau | atha hemā devatā īkṣāṃ cakrire kim ayam asmābhiḥ puruṣaḥ kariṣyati kiṃ vā vayam anena | hantāsmāc carīrād utkramāmeti | tā hoccakramuḥ | atha hedaṃ śarīraṃ riktam iva parisuṣiraṃ sa hekṣāñcakre prajāpatī randhrāya na kṣamam | hantāham imā aśanāyāpipāsābhyām upasṛjā iti | tā hopasasṛje | tā hopāṣrṣṭāḥ sukhaṃ alabhamānā imam eva puruṣaṃ punaḥ pratyāviviśuḥ ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 11,1
<s>Prajāpati</s> indeed fashioned this person. Having fashioned him, he placed these deities in him: <s>Agni</s> (fire) in speech, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) in <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), <s>Vidyut</s> (lightning) in <s>apāna</s> (out-breath), <s>Parjanya</s> (rain) in <s>udāna</s> (up-breath), <s>Āditya</s> (sun) in the eye, <s>Candramā</s> (moon) in the mind, the quarters in the ear, the earth in the body, the waters in semen, strength in <s>Indra</s>, anger in <s>Īśāna</s>, space in the crown of the head, <s>Brahman</s> in the self. He stood like a great vessel of nectar being filled. Then these deities deliberated: "What will this person do for us? What purpose shall we serve through him? Come, let us depart from this body!" They departed. Then this body lay empty, like a hollow [shell]. <s>Prajāpati</s> looked upon it [and thought]: "It is not fit for destruction. Come, let me attach hunger and thirst to these [deities]." He attached them to them. They, being attached, not finding comfort, entered this very person again.

children.text:
ŚĀ 11,2
vāṅ mamety agnir āviveśa | prāṇo mameti vāyur āviveśa | apāno mameti vidyuta āviviśuḥ | udāno mameti parjanya āviveśa | cakṣur mamety āditya āviveśa | mano mameti candramā āviveśa | śrotram asmākam iti diśa āviviśuḥ | śarīraṃ mameti pṛthivy āviveśa | reto 'smākam ity āpa āviviśuḥ | balaṃ mametīndra āviveśa | manyur mametīśāna āviveśa | mūrdhā mamety ākāśa āviveśa | ātmā mameti brahmāviveśa | sa yathā mahān vṛkṣa ārdra upasiktamūlas tiṣṭhed evaṃ haiva sa tasthau ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 11,2
"Speech is mine!" — <s>Agni</s> entered. "<s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) is mine!" — <s>Vāyu</s> entered. "<s>Apāna</s> (out-breath) is mine!" — <s>Vidyut</s> (lightning) entered. "<s>Udāna</s> (up-breath) is mine!" — <s>Parjanya</s> (rain) entered. "The eye is mine!" — <s>Āditya</s> (sun) entered. "The mind is mine!" — <s>Candramā</s> (moon) entered. "The ear is ours!" — the quarters entered. "The body is mine!" — <s>Pṛthivī</s> (earth) entered. "Semen is ours!" — the waters entered. "Strength is mine!" — <s>Indra</s> entered. "Anger is mine!" — <s>Īśāna</s> entered. "The crown of the head is mine!" — <s>Ākāśa</s> (space) entered. "The self is mine!" — <s>Brahman</s> entered. He stood like a great moist tree with its roots well-watered.

children.text:
ŚĀ 11,3
athāyaṃ puruṣaḥ preṣyan purā saṃvatsarāt saṃvatsarasya dṛṣṭīḥ paśyati | chidrā chāyā bhavati na vā bhavati | mahāmeghe vā marīcīr iva paśyed anabhre vā vidyutaṃ paśyed abhra enāṃ na paśyet | akṣiṇī vā apidhāya varāṭakānīvā na paśyati | karṇau vāpidhāyopabdim iva na śṛṇoti | nāsmiṁl loke ramate nainaṃ manaś chandayati | iti pratyakṣadarśanāni ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 11,3
Now, when this person is about to depart, he sees these signs before a year, within the year's span. He sees broken shadows, or they do not appear at all. In a great cloud he sees something like mirages, or in a cloudless [sky] he sees lightning, but in clouds he does not see it. Or closing his eyes, he does not see [things that appear] like cowrie shells. Or closing his ears, he does not hear something like a sound. He does not delight in this world, nor does the mind bring him pleasure. These are the directly perceived signs.

children.text:
ŚĀ 11,4
atha svapnāḥ | puruṣaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇadantaṃ paśyati sa enaṃ hanti varāha enaṃ hanti markaṭa enaṃ hanti enaṃ hanti bisāni khādayati suvarṇaṃ bhakṣayitvāvagiraty ekapauṇḍarīkaṃ dhārayati gāṃ savatsāṃ dakṣiṇāmukho naladamālī vrājayati | sa yady eteṣāṃ kiṃcit paśyet pāṇḍuradarśanāṃ kālīṃ strīṃ muktakeśāṃ muṇḍāṃ tailābhyaṅgaṃ kausumbhaparidhānaṃ gītāny uṣṭrārohanaṃ dakṣiṇāśāgamanādīni vīkṣyopoṣya pāyasaṃ sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā sarūpavatsāyā goḥ payasi na tv eva tu kṛṣṇāyā agnim upasamādhāya parisamuhya paristīrya paryukṣya dakṣiṇaṃ jānv ācya sruveṇājyahutīr juhoti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 11,4: Now, [concerning] dreams. [If] one sees a dark man with dark teeth — he kills him; a boar kills him; a monkey kills him; [the wind] kills him; he eats lotus stalks; having eaten gold, he swallows it; he holds a single white lotus; he drives a cow with her calf, facing south, wearing a garland of <s>nalada</s> (spikenard). If he should see any of these — [or if he sees] a pale-complexioned dark woman with disheveled hair, a shaven [woman], oil-anointment, a garment of safflower, songs, riding a camel, going toward the south, and such — having observed [these omens], he should fast. Then having cooked a milk-porridge (<s>pāyasa sthālīpāka</s>) in the milk of a cow with a calf of the same color — but not of a dark cow — he should build up the fire, sweep around it, spread the sacrificial grass, sprinkle water, and bending the right knee, offer oblations of ghee with the ladle.

children.text:
ŚĀ 11,5
vāci me 'gniḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ svāhā | prāṇe me vāyuḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ svāhā | apāne me vidyutaḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ svāhā | udāne me parjanyaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ svāhā | cakṣuṣi ma ādityaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ svāhā | manasi me candramāḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ svāhā | śrotre me diśaḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ svāhā | śarīre me pṛthivī pratiṣṭhitā svāhā | retasi ma āpaḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ svāhā | bale ma indraḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ svāhā | manyau ma īśānaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ svāhā | mūrdhani ma ākāśaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ svāhā | ātmani me brahma pratiṣṭhitaṃ svāhā | athaitad ājyāvaśeṣaṃ sthālīpāke samavaninīya sthālīpākasyopaghātaṃ juhoti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 11,5: '<s>Agni</s> is established in my speech — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Vāyu</s> is established in my <s>prāṇa</s> (outbreath) — <s>svāhā</s>!' 'The lightnings are established in my <s>apāna</s> (inbreath) — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god) is established in my <s>udāna</s> (upbreath) — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Āditya</s> (the sun) is established in my sight — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Candramā</s> (the moon) is established in my mind — <s>svāhā</s>!' 'The quarters are established in my hearing — <s>svāhā</s>!' 'The earth is established in my body — <s>svāhā</s>!' 'The waters are established in my semen — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Indra</s> is established in my strength — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Īśāna</s> is established in my anger — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Ākāśa</s> (space) is established in my crown — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Brahman</s> is established in my self — <s>svāhā</s>!' Then, having poured this remaining ghee into the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked offering), he offers the subsidiary oblation of the <s>sthālīpāka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 11,6
vāci me 'gniḥ pratiṣṭhito vāg hṛdaye hṛdayam ātmani tat satyaṃ devānāṃ māham akāmo mariṣyāmy annavān annādo bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | prāṇe me vāyuḥ pratiṣṭhito prāṇo hṛdaye hṛdayam ātmani tat satyaṃ devānāṃ māham akāmo mariṣyāmy annavān annādo bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | apāne me vidyutaḥ pratiṣṭhitā apāno hṛdaye hṛdayam ātmani tat satyaṃ devānāṃ māham akāmo mariṣyāmy annavān annādo bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | udāne me parjanyaḥ pratiṣṭhita udānaṃ hṛdaye hṛdayam ātmani tat satyaṃ devānāṃ māham akāmo mariṣyāmy annavān annādo bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | cakṣuṣi ma ādityaḥ pratiṣṭhitaś cakṣur hṛdaye hṛdayam ātmani tat satyaṃ devānāṃ māham akāmo mariṣyāmy annavān annādo bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | manasi me candramāḥ pratiṣṭhito mano hṛdaye hṛdayam ātmani tat satyaṃ devānāṃ māham akāmo mariṣyāmy annavān annādo bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | śrotre me diśaḥ pratiṣṭhitā diśo hṛdaye hṛdayam ātmani tat satyaṃ devānāṃ māham akāmo mariṣyāmy annavān annādo bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | śarīre me pṛthhivī pratiṣṭhitā pṛthivī hṛdaye hṛdayam ātmani tat satyaṃ devānāṃ māham akāmo mariṣyāmy annavān annādo bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | bale ma indraḥ pratiṣṭhitā balaṃ hṛdaye hṛdayam ātmani tat satyaṃ devānāṃ māham akāmo mariṣyāmy annavān annādo bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | manyau ma īśānaḥ pratiṣṭhito manyur hṛdaye hṛdayam ātmani tat satyaṃ devānāṃ māham akāmo mariṣyāmy annavān annādo bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | mūrdhani ma ākāśaḥ pratiṣṭhito
mūrdhā hṛdaye hṛdayam ātmani tat satyaṃ devānāṃ māham akāmo mariṣyāmy annavān annādo bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | ātmani me brahma pratiṣṭhitam ātmā hṛdaye hṛdayam ātmani tat satyaṃ devānāṃ māham akāmo mariṣyāmy annavān annādo bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | athaitat sthālīpākaśeṣam ātmani samavaninīya juhoti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 11,6: '<s>Agni</s> is established in my speech; speech is in the heart; the heart is in the self — that is the truth of the gods. May I not die without desire. May I become possessed of food, an eater of food — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Vāyu</s> is established in my <s>prāṇa</s>; <s>prāṇa</s> is in the heart; the heart is in the self — that is the truth of the gods. May I not die without desire. May I become possessed of food, an eater of food — <s>svāhā</s>!' 'The lightnings are established in my <s>apāna</s>; <s>apāna</s> is in the heart; the heart is in the self — that is the truth of the gods. May I not die without desire. May I become possessed of food, an eater of food — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Parjanya</s> is established in my <s>udāna</s>; <s>udāna</s> is in the heart; the heart is in the self — that is the truth of the gods. May I not die without desire. May I become possessed of food, an eater of food — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Āditya</s> is established in my sight; sight is in the heart; the heart is in the self — that is the truth of the gods. May I not die without desire. May I become possessed of food, an eater of food — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Candramā</s> is established in my mind; mind is in the heart; the heart is in the self — that is the truth of the gods. May I not die without desire. May I become possessed of food, an eater of food — <s>svāhā</s>!' 'The quarters are established in my hearing; the quarters are in the heart; the heart is in the self — that is the truth of the gods. May I not die without desire. May I become possessed of food, an eater of food — <s>svāhā</s>!' 'The earth is established in my body; the earth is in the heart; the heart is in the self — that is the truth of the gods. May I not die without desire. May I become possessed of food, an eater of food — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Indra</s> is established in my strength; strength is in the heart; the heart is in the self — that is the truth of the gods. May I not die without desire. May I become possessed of food, an eater of food — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Īśāna</s> is established in my anger; anger is in the heart; the heart is in the self — that is the truth of the gods. May I not die without desire. May I become possessed of food, an eater of food — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Ākāśa</s> is established in my crown; the crown is in the heart; the heart is in the self — that is the truth of the gods. May I not die without desire. May I become possessed of food, an eater of food — <s>svāhā</s>!' '<s>Brahman</s> is established in my self; the self is in the heart; the heart is in the self — that is the truth of the gods. May I not die without desire. May I become possessed of food, an eater of food — <s>svāhā</s>!' Then, having poured this remaining <s>sthālīpāka</s> [offering] into himself, he makes the final oblation of the <s>sthālīpāka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 11,7
aśmā jāgatam ayas traiṣṭubhaṃ loham auṣṇihaṃ sīsaṃ kākubhaṃ rajataṃ svārājyaṃ suvarṇaṃ gāyatram annaṃ vairājaṃ tṛptir ānuṣṭubhaṃ nākaṃ sāmrājyaṃ bṛhaspatir bārhataṃ brahma pāṅktaṃ prajāpatir ātichandasaṃ sāvitrī sarvavedachandasena chandaseti ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 11,7: Stone is of the <s>Jagatī</s> [meter]; iron is of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; copper is of the <s>Uṣṇih</s>; lead is of the <s>Kakubh</s>; silver is of <s>Svārājya</s> (self-sovereignty); gold is of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>; food is of the <s>Virāj</s>; satisfaction is of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>; heaven is of <s>Sāmrājya</s> (supreme sovereignty); <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is of the <s>Bārhatī</s>; <s>Brahman</s> is of the <s>Paṅkti</s>; <s>Prajāpati</s> is of the <s>Atichandas</s> (beyond meter); <s>Sāvitrī</s> is with the meter of all the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 11,8
aśmeva sthiro vasāni jāgatena chandasā | puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ sūtram annaṃ granthis taṃ granthim udgrathnāmy annakāmaḥ | mṛtyave brāhmaṇaṃ api sarvam āyur aśīyāyuṣmān māham akāmo mariṣyāmy annavān annādo bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | aya iva sthiro vasāni traiṣṭubhena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ ... svāhā | loham iva sthiro vasāny auṣṇihena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ ... svāhā | sīsam iva sthiro vasāni kākubhena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ ... svāhā | rajatam iva sthiro vasāni svarājyena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ ... svāhā | suvarṇam iva sthiro vasāni gāyatreṇa chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ ... svāhā | annam iva sthiro vasāni vairājena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ ... svāhā | tṛptir iva sthiro vasāny ānuṣṭubhena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ ... svāhā | nākam iva sthiro vasāni
sāmrājyena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ ... svāhā | bṛhaspatir iva sthiro vasāni bārhatena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ ... svāhā | brahmeva sthiro vasāni pāṅktena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ ... svāhā | prajāpatir iva sthiro vasāny ātichandasena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ ... svāhā | sāvitrīr iva sthiro vasāni sarvavedachandasena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ ... svāhā | priyāyai vā jāyāyai priyāya vāntevāsine 'nyasmai vāpi yasmai kāmayeta tasmā ucchiṣṭaṃ dadyāt | sa hāpi śataṃ varṣāṇi jīvati punaḥ punaḥ prayuñjāno jīvaty eva jīvaty eva ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 11,8: 'May I dwell firm as stone, with the <s>Jagatī</s> meter. The person is the jewel; <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) is the thread; food is the knot. That knot I tie, desiring food. May death [spare] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. May I live the full lifespan; may I be long-lived. May I not die without desire. May I become possessed of food, an eater of food — <s>svāhā</s>!' 'May I dwell firm as iron, with the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter. The person is the jewel; <s>prāṇa</s> is the thread... <s>svāhā</s>!' 'May I dwell firm as copper, with the <s>Uṣṇih</s> meter. The person is the jewel; <s>prāṇa</s> is the thread... <s>svāhā</s>!' 'May I dwell firm as lead, with the <s>Kakubh</s> meter. The person is the jewel; <s>prāṇa</s> is the thread... <s>svāhā</s>!' 'May I dwell firm as silver, with the <s>Svārājya</s> meter. The person is the jewel; <s>prāṇa</s> is the thread... <s>svāhā</s>!' 'May I dwell firm as gold, with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter. The person is the jewel; <s>prāṇa</s> is the thread... <s>svāhā</s>!' 'May I dwell firm as food, with the <s>Vairāja</s> meter. The person is the jewel; <s>prāṇa</s> is the thread... <s>svāhā</s>!' 'May I dwell firm as satisfaction, with the <s>Ānuṣṭubha</s> meter. The person is the jewel; <s>prāṇa</s> is the thread... <s>svāhā</s>!' 'May I dwell firm as heaven, with the <s>Sāmrājya</s> meter. The person is the jewel; <s>prāṇa</s> is the thread... <s>svāhā</s>!' 'May I dwell firm as <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, with the <s>Bārhata</s> meter. The person is the jewel; <s>prāṇa</s> is the thread... <s>svāhā</s>!' 'May I dwell firm as <s>Brahman</s>, with the <s>Pāṅkta</s> meter. The person is the jewel; <s>prāṇa</s> is the thread... <s>svāhā</s>!' 'May I dwell firm as <s>Prajāpati</s>, with the <s>Ātichandas</s> meter. The person is the jewel; <s>prāṇa</s> is the thread... <s>svāhā</s>!' 'May I dwell firm as <s>Sāvitrī</s>, with the meter of all the <s>Vedas</s>. The person is the jewel; <s>prāṇa</s> is the thread; food is the knot. That knot I tie, desiring food. May death [spare] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. May I live the full lifespan; may I be long-lived. May I not die without desire. May I become possessed of food, an eater of food — <s>svāhā</s>!' To a beloved wife, or to a beloved pupil, or to any other person one may wish — to that person one should give the leftovers. He indeed lives a hundred years. Using this [rite] again and again, he lives, he truly lives.

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake ekādaśamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 12,1
om | hastivarcasaṃ prathatāṃ bṛhad vayo yad adityai tanvaḥ saṃbabhūva | tan mahyaṃ samaduḥ sarva eta ādityāso adityā saṃvidānāḥ ||1|| yat te varco jātavedo bṛhad bhavaty āhitam | tena mā varcasā tvam agne varcasvinaṃ kuru ||2|| yac ca varco vā puruṣe yac ca hastiṣv āhitam | suvarṇe goṣu yad varco mayi tad dhastivarcasam ||3|| yad akṣeṣu hiraṇyeṣu goṣv aśveṣu yad yaśaḥ | surāyāṃ pūyamānāyāṃ mayi tad dhastivarcasam ||4|| mayi bhargo mayi maho mayi yajñasya yad yaśaḥ | tan mayi prajāpatir divi divam iva dṛṃhatu ||5||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 12,1: May the elephant-vitality (<s>hastivarcasa</s>) spread far and wide — the great vigor that was born from the body of <s>Aditi</s>. All these <s>Ādityas</s>, in agreement, have milked that [vitality] for me — the <s>Ādityas</s>, the sons of <s>Aditi</s>. ||1|| O <s>Jātavedas</s> (fire), whatever radiance of yours becomes great when kindled — by that radiance, O <s>Agni</s>, make me radiant. ||2|| Whatever radiance is in a person, and whatever is deposited in elephants, in gold, in cattle — may that elephant-vitality be in me. ||3|| Whatever glory is in dice, in gold, in cattle, in horses — that glory which is in liquor being purified — may that elephant-vitality be in me. ||4|| May radiance be in me, may greatness be in me, may the glory of the sacrifice be in me. May <s>Prajāpati</s> make that firm for me in heaven, as heaven itself is firmly established. ||5||

children.text:
ŚĀ 12,2
aśvinā sāragheṇa mā sam aṅktāṃ madhunā payaḥ | yathā madhumatīṃ vācam āvadāni janeṣu ||6|| ghṛtād ullupto madhumān payasvān dhanaṃjayo dharuṇo dhārayiṣṇuḥ | rujan sapatnān adharāṃś ca kṛṇvan ā roha māṃ mahate saubhagāya ||7|| prajāpate na tvad etāny anyo viśvā jatāni pari tā babhūva | yatkāmās te juhumas tan no astu vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇām ||8|| ayaṃ sano nudatāṃ me sapatnān indra iva vṛtraṃ pṛtanāsu sāḷhā | agnir iva kakṣaṃ vibhṛtaḥ purutrā vāteṣu nas tigmajambho 'nu mārṣṭi ||9|| ayaṃ sano yo 'nuvādī kīla iva vṛtraṃ vi puro ruroja | anenendro vi mṛdho vihatyā śatrūyatām ābharā bhojanāni ||10||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 12,2: May the <s>Aśvins</s> anoint me with honey-sweet <s>sāragha</s> (clarified butter); milk mixed with honey — so that I may speak honey-sweet speech among people. ||6|| Anointed with ghee, rich in honey, rich in milk, wealth-winning, sustaining, supporting — crushing rivals and making them low, mount upon me for great good fortune. ||7|| O <s>Prajāpati</s>, none other than you has encompassed all these creatures. Whatever desires we have when we offer to you, may they be ours. May we be lords of riches. ||8|| May this one drive away our rivals for me — victorious in battles like <s>Indra</s> [conquering] <s>Vṛtra</s>, spread in many ways like fire [consuming] brushwood. In the winds, the sharp-toothed one sweeps [them] away for us. ||9|| This one who speaks for us, like a peg he has burst open the enemies' strongholds. With this, <s>Indra</s> has struck down the hostile armies. Bring the food [provisions] of those who are hostile. ||10||

children.text:
ŚĀ 12,3
jayendra śatrūñ jahi śūra dasyūn vṛtraṃ hatveva kuliśenā vi vṛśca | augha iva śāpān pra ṇudāt sapatnāñ jahyāt sapatnān svadhitir vaneva ||11|| anu vṛśca madhyāt prati vṛścopariṣṭād vi vṛśca paścāt prati śūra vṛśca | tvayā praṇuttān maghavann amitrān śūra riṣantaṃ maruto 'nu yantu ||12|| tvāṃ rudrair hetibhiḥ pinvamānā indraṃ manvānā maruto juṣanta | suparṇāḥ kaṅkāḥ pra mṛśanto enān mahīyatāṃ daṃṣṭrī vardhaneṣu ||13|| brahmaṇuttasya maghavan pṛtanyato viṣvag indra bhaṅgāḥ patantu | mā jñātāram īśata mā pratiṣṭhāṃ mitho vighnānā upa yānti mṛtyum ||14|| agne yaśasvin yaśase sam arpayendravatīm apacitim ihā vaha | ayaṃ mūrdhā parameṣṭhī suvarcāḥ sajātānām uttamaśloko astu ||15||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 12,3: Conquer, O <s>Indra</s>, the enemies! Slay, O hero, the <s>Dasyus</s>! Having slain <s>Vṛtra</s>, cut them down as with a thunderbolt! Like a flood, may he drive away the curses of rivals; may he strike down rivals as an axe [strikes] a forest! ||11|| Cut from the middle, cut from above, cut from behind — strike back, O hero! Driven away by you, O bounteous one, may the <s>Maruts</s> pursue the enemy, O hero, as he is harmed! ||12|| Swelling with the weapons of the <s>Rudras</s>, thinking of <s>Indra</s>, the <s>Maruts</s> rejoice. Like eagles, like herons, seizing them — may the fanged one be exalted in the encounters! ||13|| O bounteous <s>Indra</s>, may the destructions of the one who fights with sacred speech fall in all directions! May he find no kinsman, no foothold — striking one another, they go to death! ||14|| O <s>Agni</s>, glorious one, bring him to glory! Bring here the <s>Indra</s>-empowered tribute! May this chief, the supreme, of excellent radiance, be the highest in fame among his kinsmen! ||15||

children.text:
ŚĀ 12,4
bhadraṃ paśyanta upa sedur āgan tato dīkṣām ṛṣayaḥ svarvidaḥ | tataḥ kṣatraṃ balam ojaś ca jātaṃ tad asmai devā abhi saṃ namantām ||16|| dhātā vidhātā paramota saṃdṛk prajāpatiḥ parameṣṭhī suvarccāḥ | stomāṃś chandāṃsi nivido ma āhur etasmai rāṣṭram abhi saṃ namantām ||17|| abhy ā vartadhvam upa sevatāgnim ayaṃ śāstādhipatir no astu | asya vijñānam anu saṃ rabhadhvam imaṃ paścād anu jīvātha sarve ||18|| alardo nāma jāto 'si purā sūryāt puroṣasaḥ | taṃ tvā sapatnakṣayaṇaṃ vedātha viṣṭambhajambhanam ||19|| nārdhe pramīyeta tared dviṣantaṃ kalpeta vākyaṃ pṛtanāḥ saheta | pramāyukaṃ tasya dviṣantam āhur irāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti ||20||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 12,4: Seeing auspiciousness, they approached and came. Then the <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers), knowers of heaven, undertook the <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration). From that were born <s>kṣatra</s> (ruling power), strength, and vigor. May the gods bow down to him for this! ||16|| <s>Dhātṛ</s> (the Creator), <s>Vidhātṛ</s> (the Disposer), the supreme seer, <s>Prajāpati</s>, the supreme, of excellent radiance — the <s>stomas</s> (praises), meters, and <s>nivids</s> (liturgical formulas) they declare to me; may the kingdom bow down to him! ||17|| Turn yourselves around, attend to <s>Agni</s>! May this one be our ruler and overlord! Follow after his wisdom; live hereafter, all of you, following him! ||18|| '<s>Alarda</s> is your name at birth, born before the sun, before the dawn. I know you as the destroyer of rivals and the suppressor of enemies.' ||19|| He shall not perish in mid-life; he shall overcome the hostile one; he shall be fit for battle; he shall conquer armies. They declare his enemy to be short-lived — he who wears the <s>irāmaṇi</s> amulet made of <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) wood. ||20||

children.text:
ŚĀ 12,5
na sa śaptam aśnāti kilbiṣaṃ kṛtaṃ nainaṃ divyo varuṇo hanti bhītam | nainaṃ kruddhaṃ manyavo 'bhi yantīrāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti ||21|| nāsya tvacaṃ hiṃsati jātvedā na māṃsam aśnāti na hanti tāni | śatāyur asmiñ jaradaṣṭiḥ praitīrāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti ||22|| nāsya prajā duṣyati jāyamānā na śailago bhavati na pāpakṛtyā | nānyan mithas tasya kuleṣu jāyata irāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti ||23|| nāsyāpavādā na pravādakā gṛhe na saṃpatatryo na viveśa tasmai | nāsminn alakṣmīḥ kurute niveśanam irāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti ||24|| nainaṃ rakṣo na piśāco hinasti
na jambhako nāpy asuro na yakṣaḥ | na sūtikā tasya kuleṣu jāyate irāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti ||25||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 12,5: He eats no cursed food, commits no sin; the divine <s>Varuṇa</s> does not strike him when afraid; angry spirits do not assail him — he who wears the <s>irāmaṇi</s> amulet made of <s>bilva</s>. ||21|| <s>Jātavedas</s> (<s>Agni</s>) does not harm his skin, does not consume his flesh, does not destroy those [limbs]. Living a hundred years, reaching old age with his walking-staff — he who wears the <s>irāmaṇi</s> of <s>bilva</s>. ||22|| His offspring are not corrupted at birth; he does not become a leper nor an evildoer; no deformed child is born among his family — he who wears the <s>irāmaṇi</s> of <s>bilva</s>. ||23|| No evil speech, no slanderers in his home, no birds of ill omen enter for him; misfortune (<s>alakṣmī</s>) does not act upon him —

children.text:
ŚĀ 12,6
nainaṃ vyāghro na vṛko na dvīpī na śvāpadaṃ hiṃsati kiṃcanainam | na hastinaṃ kruddham upaiti bhītim irāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti ||26|| nainaṃ sarpo na pṛdākur hinasti na vṛściko na tiraścīnarājiḥ | nainaṃ kṛṣṇo 'hir abhi saṃhata irāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti ||27|| nainaṃ pramattaṃ varuṇo hinasti na makaro na grahaḥ śiṃśumāraḥ | pārāvarāc chivam asmai kṛṇotīrāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti ||28|| pramāyukam asya dviṣantam āhuḥ | puṣpam iva chinnaṃ saha bandhanena | ogha iva śāpān pra ṇudāt sapatnān | irāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti ||29|| ayaṃ maṇiḥ pratisaro
jāmbo jīvāya badhyate | anenendro vṛtram ahann ṛṣiṇā ca manīṣiṇā ||30||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 12,6: Neither tiger, nor wolf, nor leopard, nor any wild beast harms him at all; he does not meet fear from an enraged elephant — he who wears the <s>irāmaṇi</s> of <s>bilva</s>. ||26|| Neither serpent, nor spotted snake harms him, nor scorpion, nor cross-striped [snake]; the black cobra does not attack him — he who wears the <s>irāmaṇi</s> of <s>bilva</s>. ||27|| <s>Varuṇa</s> does not harm him when heedless, neither crocodile, nor sea-monster, nor <s>śiṃśumāra</s> (porpoise); from ocean to ocean it makes [the way] auspicious for him — he who wears the <s>irāmaṇi</s> of <s>bilva</s>. ||28|| They declare his enemy to be short-lived; like a flower cut from its stalk, like a flood he drives away the curses of rivals —

children.text:
ŚĀ 12,7
sahendra dviṣataḥ sahasvārātīḥ sahasva pṛtanāyataḥ | nāga iva pūrvapādābhyām abhi tiṣṭha pṛtanyataḥ ||31|| āgād ayaṃ bailvo maṇiḥ sapatnakṣapaṇo vṛṣā | taṃ paśyanti kavayaḥ sarvavīrā yathā sapatnān samare saheyuḥ ||32|| anṛtaṃ me maṇau sūtram aśvināv api nahyatām | bailvaḥ sahasravīryo 'si mā te bhartā riṣam aham ||33|| ghṛtād ullupto madhumān payasvān dhanaṃjayo dharuṇo dhārayiṣṇuḥ | rujan sapatnān adharāṃś ca kṛṇvan ā roha māṃ mahate saubhagāya ||34|| prajāpate na tvad etāny anyo viśvā jatāni pari tā babhūva | yatkāmas te juhumas tan no astu vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇām ||35|| śāsa itthā mahāṁ asīti pañca ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 12,7: With <s>Indra</s>, conquer the haters! Conquer the enemies! Conquer those who fight! Like an elephant with its front feet, trample upon those who battle! ||31|| This <s>bilva</s> amulet has come, the rival-destroying bull. The seers, all-heroic, see it — how it may conquer rivals in battle! ||32|| The thread on my amulet is unfailing; may the <s>Aśvins</s> bind it on! O <s>bilva</s>, you have a thousand-fold power; may I, your wearer, not be harmed! ||33|| Anointed with ghee, rich in honey, full of milk, wealth-winning, supporting, sustaining — crushing rivals and making them inferior, mount upon me for great good fortune! ||34|| O <s>Prajāpati</s>, no other than you [has brought forth] all these...

children.text:
ŚĀ 12,8
athāto maṇikalpaḥ | bhūtikāmaḥ puṣpeṇa trirātropoṣito jīvato hastino dantān mātrām uddhṛtyāgnim upasamādhāya parisamuhya paristīrya paryukṣya dakṣiṇaṃ jānv ācyottarato 'gneḥ kaṃse maṇiṃ kṛtvā hutvā homān maṇau saṃpātam ānayet | hastivarcasam ity etābhiḥ pratyṛcam aṣṭābhiḥ saptarātraṃ madhusarpiṣor vāsayitvā trirātram ekāṃ vā badhnīyād ghṛtād ullupta ity etayarcā | ata evottaraṃ ṣaḍbhir hṛdayaśūlāgramaṇiṃ pratodāgramaṇiṃ vā muśalāgramaṇiṃ vā khadirasāramaṇiṃ vā māṃsaudane vāsayitvā trirātram ekāṃ vā badhnīyāt | ata evottaraṃ catasṛbhir vṛṣabhaśṛṅgāgramaṇiṃ ghṛtaudane vāsayitvā trirātram ekāṃ vā badhnīyāt | ata evottaraṃ ekayairaṇḍamaṇiṃ tilaudane vāsayitvā trirātram ekāṃ vā badhnīyāt | ata evottaraṃ ṣoḷaśabhir bailvaṃ saptarātraṃ madhusarpiṣor vāsayitvā trirātram ekāṃ vā badhnīyād ghṛtād ullupta ity etayarcā | ata evottaraṃ pañcabhir mahāvarāsyodohaṃ mudgaudane vāsayitvā trirātram ekāṃ vā badhnīyāc chaktau sati prathamaṃ hastichāyāyāṃ vaiyāghre vāpi carmaṇy āsīno vāpi juhuyād āsīno vāpi juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 12,8: Now then, the amulet ritual (<s>maṇikalpa</s>). One desiring prosperity, having fasted for three nights with flowers, should extract a piece (<s>mātrā</s>) from the tusks of a living elephant. Having built up the fire, swept around it, strewn [grass], and sprinkled [water], kneeling on his right knee to the north of the fire, having placed the amulet in a vessel, having offered the oblations, he should bring the remainder into the amulet. With the [verses beginning] 'elephant-splendor' — with these eight verses, one per verse, having soaked [the amulet] for seven nights in honey and ghee, he should tie it on for three nights or one [night] with the verse 'Anointed with ghee.' For the remaining [purposes], with the six [verses following], [he should prepare] a heart-point amulet, or a goad-point amulet, or a pestle-point amulet, or a <s>khadira</s>-heartwood amulet, having soaked it in a meat-and-rice offering for three nights —

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake dvādaśamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 13,1
athāto vairāgyasaṃskṛte śarīre brahmayajñaniṣṭho bhavet | apa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati | tad u ha vātmā draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavya iti | tam etaṃ vedānuvacanena vividiṣanti brahmacaryeṇa tapasā śraddhayā yajñenānāśakena ceti māṇḍūkeyaḥ | tasmād evaṃvic chānto dānta uparatas titikṣuḥ śraddhāvitto bhūtvātmany evātmānaṃ paśyed iti māṇḍavyaḥ | yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ puruṣaḥ prāṇeṣu sa eṣa neti nety ātmā na gṛhya idaṃ brahmedaṃ kṣatram ime devā ime vedā ime lokā imāni sarvāṇi bhūtānīdaṃ sarvaṃ yad ayam ātmā | sa eṣa tat tvam asīty ātmāvagamyo 'haṃ brahmāsmīti | tad etad brahmāpūrvam aparam anaparam anantaram abāhyam ayam ātmā brahma sarvānubhūr ity anuśāsanam iti yājñavalkyaḥ | tad etan nāputrāya nānantevāsine vā brūyād iti | ya imām adbhiḥ parigṛhītāṃ vasumatīṃ dhanasya pūrṇāṃ dadyād idam eva tato bhūya idam eva tato bhūya ity anuśāsanam | tām etām upaniṣadaṃ vedaśiro na yathā kathaṃ cana vadet | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 13,1: Now then, in a body purified by dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), one should become devoted to the <s>brahmayajña</s> (worship of <s>Brahman</s>). One conquers repeated death (<s>punarmṛtyu</s>). That <s>ātman</s> (Self) is to be seen, heard, reflected upon, and deeply meditated upon (<s>nididhyāsitavya</s>). They seek to know it through Vedic recitation (<s>vedānuvacana</s>), through <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship), through <s>tapas</s> (austerity), through faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), through sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>), and through fasting (<s>anāśaka</s>) — thus [teaches] <s>Māṇḍūkeya</s>. Therefore, one who knows thus, being peaceful, self-controlled, withdrawn, patient, and full of faith, should see the <s>ātman</s> in the <s>ātman</s> itself — thus [teaches] <s>Māṇḍavya</s>. This <s>puruṣa</s> (person) who consists of knowledge (<s>vijñānamaya</s>), who is among the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) — he is the <s>ātman</s> [described as] '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this), not to be grasped. This is <s>Brahman</s>, this is <s>kṣatra</s> (ruling power), these are the gods, these are the <s>Vedas</s>, these are the worlds, these are all beings —

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake trayodaśamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 14,1
ṛcāṃ mūrdhānaṃ yajuṣām uttamāṅgam | sāmnāṃ śiro 'tharvāṇāṃ muṇḍamuṇḍam | nādhīte 'dhīte vedam āhus tam ajñam | śiraś chitvāsau kurute kabandham ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 14,1: The crown of the <s>Ṛc</s> verses, the topmost part of the <s>Yajus</s> formulas, the head of the <s>Sāman</s> chants, the very tonsured crown of the <s>Atharvan</s> [hymns] — one who does not study it, though he has studied the <s>Veda</s>, they call him ignorant; having cut off the head, he makes [of himself] a headless trunk.

children.text:
ŚĀ 14,2
sthāṇur ayaṃ bhārahāraḥ kilābhūt | adhītya vedaṃ na vijānāti yo 'rtham | yo 'rthajña it sakalaṃ bhadram aśnute | nākam eti jñānavidhūtapāpmā ||
children.translated_text: ŚĀ 14,2: This [person] has become like a post, a mere burden-bearer, it is said — one who, having studied the <s>Veda</s>, does not understand its meaning. He who knows the meaning enjoys complete blessedness. He goes to heaven, his sins destroyed by knowledge.

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake caturdaśamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text:
ŚĀ 15,1
atha vaṃśaḥ | oṃ namo brahmaṇe nama ācāryebhyaḥ | guṇākhyāc chāṅkhāyanād asmābhir adhītam | guṇākhyaś śāṅkhāyanaḥ kahoḷāt kauṣītakeḥ | kahoḷaḥ kauṣītakir uddālakād āruṇeḥ | uddālaka āruṇiḥ priyavratāt saumāpeḥ | priyavrataḥ saumāpiḥ somapāt | somapaḥ saumāt prātiveśyāt | saumaḥ prātiveśyaḥ prativeśyāt | prativeśyo bṛhaddivāt | bṛhaddivaḥ sumnayoḥ | sumnayur uddālakāt | uddālako viśvamanasaḥ | viśvamanā vyaśvāt | vyaśvaḥ sākamaśvāt | sākamaśvo devarātāt | devarāto viśvāmitrāt | viśvāmitra indrāt | indraḥ prajāpateḥ | prajāpatir brahmaṇaḥ | brahmā svayaṃbhūḥ | namo brahmaṇe namo brahmaṇe ||
children.translated_text:
ŚĀ 15,1
Now the lineage (<s>vaṃśa</s>). <s>Oṃ</s>. Homage to <s>Brahman</s>. Homage to the teachers. From <s>Guṇākhya Śāṅkhāyana</s> this has been studied by us. <s>Guṇākhya Śāṅkhāyana</s> [received it] from <s>Kahoḷa Kauṣītaki</s>. <s>Kahoḷa Kauṣītaki</s> from <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s>. <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s> from <s>Priyavrata Saumāpi</s>. <s>Priyavrata Saumāpi</s> from <s>Somapa</s>. <s>Somapa</s> from <s>Sauma Prātiveśya</s>. <s>Sauma Prātiveśya</s> from <s>Prativeśya</s>. <s>Prativeśya</s> from <s>Bṛhaddiva</s>. <s>Bṛhaddiva</s> from <s>Sumnayu</s>. <s>Sumnayu</s> from <s>Uddālaka</s>. <s>Uddālaka</s> from <s>Viśvamanas</s>. <s>Viśvamanas</s> from <s>Vyaśva</s>. <s>Vyaśva</s> from <s>Sākamaśva</s>. <s>Sākamaśva</s> from <s>Devarāta</s>. <s>Devarāta</s> from <s>Viśvāmitra</s>. <s>Viśvāmitra</s> from <s>Indra</s>. <s>Indra</s> from <s>Prajāpati</s>. <s>Prajāpati</s> from <s>Brahman</s>. <s>Brahman</s> is self-born (<s>svayaṃbhū</s>). Homage to <s>Brahman</s>, homage to <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyake pañcadaśamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth chapter of the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s>.

children.text: iti śāṅkhāyanāraṇyakaṃ samāptam ||
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka</s> is complete.
